Idristan has given you a chunk of fetid dodo flesh to be used to draw out the beasts. Find a suitable place to set down the meat, and slay the jackals that appear.
TEXT_GAIUSB603_00885_SEQ_02: You have slain the jackals and made the area that much safer. Return to Idristan and inform him the deed is done.
TEXT_GAIUSB603_00885_SEQ_03: Idristan is pleased at the outcome, but remains frustrated about the situation. The Calamity has left Coerthas nigh uninhabitable, and the local wildlife have become more dangerous as a result. If you plan on heading northwest, the Quiverman warns you to be prepared.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_00: Maucolyn's teeth are chattering from something other than cold, and he has the beseeching look of one seeking an adventurer's cure to a nasty ill.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_01: Maucolyn's visit to the snowhouse has given him a bad fright. A voice without a mouth is troubling indeed, and you have been tasked with discovering what it is that speaks in the icy shelter.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_02: The speaker is a melting snowman, built by some knight in a carefree moment. Its sorrow at the impending thaw has given it voice. Reach across the vast gulf of common sense and /rally the snowman.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_03: Your discomfort with this relationship is all too obvious. The snowman is affronted, and you fear the anger will further unfreeze his flesh. /soothe him or you shall be responsible for his sad demise.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_04: Your attempt to comfort the man of snow is well played─desperation has birthed many great moments in acting. The snowman is in an expansive mood, though still melancholy. Unearth your inner lickspittle and /cheer him with all your heart.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_05: Sometimes, passions burn the brightest when the end is near. His ardor enkindled by your lusty cheer, the snowman demands you /blowkiss to him as proof of your fondness.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_06: In a few minutes with you, the snowman has lived a lifetime─and now he is ready to go quietly into that good night. Tell him /goodbye.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_07: The snowman subsides into silence. Tears prickle your eyelids but you do not weep, for you know the pain of frostbitten cheeks. Maucolyn will learn the truth, and mayhap weep in your stead.
TEXT_GAIUSB606_00888_SEQ_08: Maucolyn happily dismisses the talking snowman as a youthful prank. A happy customer means a job well done, but your heart tells you it was no mummery.
TEXT_GAIUSB609_00891_SEQ_00: Wild-eyed and near wordless with shock, a deeply shaken Duvicauroix seeks an intrepid sword to hunt a ravening horror.
TEXT_GAIUSB609_00891_SEQ_01: A creature both large and vicious has attacked a caravan, leaving all but Duvicauroix dead. You judge that whatever it is, it will return to the scene of the slaughter to feed. Lurk near the bloodstained snow and strike when the creature appears.
TEXT_GAIUSB609_00891_SEQ_02: The slaughterer of the caravan turns out to be the diminutive white death, whose size belies its vast appetite for blood. From this day on, you can claim to have vanquished death, though many will be nonplussed by the jest. Tell Duvicauroix that the deed is done.
TEXT_GAIUSB609_00891_SEQ_03: Duvicauroix hears your report with amazement. While the size of the white death causes him some consternation, he is glad to hear that his companions are avenged and the road to the Observatorium is safe again.
TEXT_GAIUSB610_00892_SEQ_00: Prairillot needs a favor of you, and the chagrin it causes him is almost payment enough for the job.
TEXT_GAIUSB610_00892_SEQ_01: As the relentless cold batters Skyfire Locks, Prairillot is vexed to discover that there are no men to spare for firewood duty, and he must avail himself of an adventurer's help. Your task is to gather eight bundles of firewood from the area around Skyfire Locks.
TEXT_GAIUSB610_00892_SEQ_02: You have eight bundles of firewood, dry and ready for the stove. They should be delivered to Stephannot on the west hill ere he and his men freeze to death.
TEXT_GAIUSB610_00892_SEQ_03: Stephannot's thanks has a forced ring to it, despite his obvious relief at having more fuel on hand for the killing chill of night. Many in these parts mistrust outlanders and mislike adventurers, a state of things that makes your stay in Coerthas an uneasy one.
TEXT_GAIUSB611_00893_SEQ_00: A man may die of want in a fort as well as a hovel, and Sylvaintel has need of an adept hunter to help victual the Locks.
TEXT_GAIUSB611_00893_SEQ_01: Some Locks at Skyfire have little in the way of extra supplies laid in for hungry, shivering masses. Fortunately, the karakuls are dinner and dress in one. Cull them and collect their meat and skin.
TEXT_GAIUSB611_00893_SEQ_02: What does not ache of your hands is numb with cold, but the work is done. Deliver three each of the mutton slices and sheepskin to the four sentries at the Locks.
TEXT_GAIUSB611_00893_SEQ_03: You deliver the meat and skin to the four sentries, to varying responses. It is a curious fact that while Ishgard may worship one god, they no more speak in one voice than those who follow the Twelve, as is right and proper. Inform Sylvaintel that your task is complete.
TEXT_GAIUSB611_00893_SEQ_04: Clearly, Sylvaintel has come to trust not only your abilities but your discretion. He shares his fear that Ishgard faces an existential challenge─and while grateful for your aid, already he begins to ponder further preparations against the shadows of future tribulations.
TEXT_GAIUSB612_00894_SEQ_00: Stephannot has no love for adventurers, but beggars cannot be choosers and your help is urgently needed.
TEXT_GAIUSB612_00894_SEQ_01: One of Stephannot's young recruits has gone missing after leaving for Camp Dragonhead. He is likely lost on the north road where wild creatures sometimes stalk soft prey. Follow the recruit's trail while it is still fresh.
TEXT_GAIUSB612_00894_SEQ_02: After a brutal battle in which you nearly lost , the croc is dispatched. Like any good sleuth, you search the body and find a scarred silver ring, the least unspeakable of the creature's visceral cargo. See it to Stephannot's hands.
TEXT_GAIUSB612_00894_SEQ_03: Stephannot confirms that the ring belonged to the young recruit. You are surprised to initially find him so resistant to the obvious truth, for he struck you as a pragmatic man. It seems that in Ishgard, being devoured by beastkin shames the eaten...
TEXT_GAIUSB613_00895_SEQ_00: You sense that there is a pact of sorts between you and Stephannot now, and he gives every indication that he has another mission for you.
TEXT_GAIUSB613_00895_SEQ_01: The recruit that died in a croc attack leaves a father, another knight of Ishgard at Camp Dragonhead. The memento of the young soldier, a silvery ring, must reach this Theobalin.
TEXT_GAIUSB613_00895_SEQ_02: Despite some misgivings, you honor the pact and tell Theobalin of his son's glorious death in combat. Theobalin's heart seems to be made lighter by the fact that his family's grim legacy is now unbroken.
TEXT_GAIUSB703_00898_SEQ_00: Duchesnelt would prevail upon a passing adventurer to search for his wayward daughter.
TEXT_GAIUSB703_00898_SEQ_01: Duchesnelt's daughter has slipped out alone, a move neither wise nor politic for a girl gently born. A frantic Duchesnelt would have you go to the Weeping Saint and speak with her.
TEXT_GAIUSB703_00898_SEQ_02: While making light of her father's concern, the girl shows a streak of caution born of common sense. She bids you look about for anything suspicious in the vicinity.
TEXT_GAIUSB703_00898_SEQ_03: You find a man studying Duchesnelt's daughter with the intensity of a jackal. His hackles raised by your simple questions, he abruptly leaves, dropping something. Pick up the dull knife.
TEXT_GAIUSB703_00898_SEQ_04: There are less nefarious reasons a man might stare at a young woman. Have you deprived an honest fellow of his whittling tool, or was it something else? Show the dull knife to Duchesnelt's daughter.
TEXT_GAIUSB703_00898_SEQ_05: Uneasy at the sight of a blade brought into a holy place, Duchesnelt's daughter hastens back to Dragonhead. Perhaps Duchesnelt will know more, when you show him the knife.
TEXT_GAIUSB703_00898_SEQ_06: You show Duchesnelt the dull knife, confirming his suspicions. Even with his daughter's safe return, Duchesnelt fears that the unbelievers mean to harm her for their own mad purposes...
TEXT_GAIUSB704_00899_SEQ_00: How many ways can a man die well? Corentiaux wishes to speak to you of this and more.
TEXT_GAIUSB704_00899_SEQ_01: House Fortemps has placed a reward on the heads of snow wolves responsible for attacks on the supply train. Though not even yearlings, the beasts are vicious and have a taste for man-flesh. Slay four wolves and skin them as proof of your deed.
TEXT_GAIUSB704_00899_SEQ_02: Where there were four wolves, there are now four pelts and a churn of red snow. You have scoured the blood from your hands, and are now ready to return to Corentiaux with the proof.
TEXT_GAIUSB704_00899_SEQ_03: Many in the High Houses prefer to leave problems unsolved rather than ask for assistance from adventurers─especially when the problem is a lowly predator and the prey is a lowly servant or ten. Corentiaux speaks of this with more than a trace of bitterness. Unusual it is for a knight, and possibly dangerous...
TEXT_GAIUSB705_00900_SEQ_00: Ser Corentiaux wishes to discuss with you the latest difficulties at Dragonhead.
TEXT_GAIUSB705_00900_SEQ_01: A patrol of knights, fresh from triumph on the front, has been led astray by will-o'-the-wykes in the blizzard. Of those that returned, many are badly frostbitten. There is only one thing to be done: four wykes must be dispatched by your capable hands.
TEXT_GAIUSB705_00900_SEQ_02: The wykes are slain. The lowly adventurer succeeds where the High Houses have failed, though you should keep the thought to yourself if you enjoy owning a tongue. Return to Ser Corentiaux and give him the good news.
TEXT_GAIUSB705_00900_SEQ_03: Your report of the wykes' demise was heard with much delight. Adding the reward to your growing purse, you wonder why as insightful a man as Ser Corentiaux does not see what every child of the road does: the land itself has turned inimical, and lays siege to the hosts of Ishgard.
TEXT_GAIUSB706_00901_SEQ_00: Not all knights are indifferent to the plight of the commonfolk, and Ser Yaelle, one such earthbound warrior, wants a word with you.
TEXT_GAIUSB706_00901_SEQ_01: Ser Yaelle, she of the cool and speculative gaze, appears to enjoy the trust of the commonfolk; at their behest, she bids you slay a muttonmaw ogre. The bait is her very own karakul, Sebastian. But first, he must be captured with a length of brambleweed rope.
TEXT_GAIUSB706_00901_SEQ_02: Take the bound karakul to Providence Point and leave him at the decoy point.
TEXT_GAIUSB706_00901_SEQ_03: With the bait set, all that remains is for the trap to be sprung. Hide yourself away and wait for the unwitting prey. Be ready to strike as soon as the ogre appears, or Sebastian will pay the price.
TEXT_GAIUSB706_00901_SEQ_04: The ogre is dead, and the poor karakul is safe, though trembling and wide-eyed. Unbind him that he may return to his mistress.
TEXT_GAIUSB706_00901_SEQ_05: You have unbound the bound Sebastian, and he seems grateful to be free...and alive. Make your way back to Camp Dragonhead to speak with Ser Yaelle.
TEXT_GAIUSB706_00901_SEQ_06: Unlikely though it may seem, Sebastian has beaten you back to Ser Yaelle, as she informs you that she just finished brushing the brave karakul. The ogre will devour no more of the commonfolk's flock, and Ser Yaelle is well pleased.
TEXT_GAIUSB707_00902_SEQ_00: Arthurioux is eager to ask a service on a cold and windy night.
TEXT_GAIUSB707_00902_SEQ_01: Wincing at the howl of the wind, Ser Arthurioux instructs you to ensure that none of the braziers around the camp have gone out. Use smoldering coals to light any unlit brazier.
TEXT_GAIUSB707_00902_SEQ_02: All the dark braziers are now aglow, and grateful men will soon warm their frozen hands and read their letters from home. Report to Ser Arthurioux.
TEXT_GAIUSB707_00902_SEQ_03: Ser Arthurioux is pleased to hear that, for the first windy night in some time, every brazier at Camp Dragonhead is lit. He may find his duty a dull one, but you have a sneaking suspicion that he is well content to drowse by the fire.
TEXT_GAIUSB708_00903_SEQ_00: Sharp of eyes and broad of smile, Belmont is a hard man to resist when he has a request─and he appears to have one now.
TEXT_GAIUSB708_00903_SEQ_01: A wagon contracted by House Fortemps is apparently stalled somewhere on the east road. With Belmont and other sellswords busy with other sundry tasks, it falls to you to locate the wagon.
TEXT_GAIUSB708_00903_SEQ_02: You discover the wagon on its side and the occupants dead. They had not yet even begun shaping the new wheel shaft before they were taken by the Ixal. You slay the birdmen, but a new worm of unease coils in your belly. Go speak with Belmont.
TEXT_GAIUSB708_00903_SEQ_03: You tell Belmont of what passed, reflecting that too many of your reports from Coerthas end with vengeance rather than rescue. Belmont gives voice to the consternation you yourself feel─Ishgard's enemies are legion, but the obsession with the dragons blinds the knights and perhaps the Holy See...
TEXT_GAIUSB709_00904_SEQ_00: Belmont affects a sellsword's cynicism, but the Gods' Quiver in him dies hard. So urgently does he seek a scout that he will hire one himself.
TEXT_GAIUSB709_00904_SEQ_01: A veteran of many skirmishes with the Ixal, Belmont suspects that there is more to the beastmen's presence in this part of the world than meets the eye. He bids you use your stealth and cunning to search their lair to the east.
TEXT_GAIUSB709_00904_SEQ_02: After a review of the Ixal's housekeeping and a battle to the death, you discover nothing more unusual than a pile of yew logs. Still, they grew not from these woods, and the birdmen hardly kept them as pets. Return to the camp and give one of the logs to Belmont.
TEXT_GAIUSB709_00904_SEQ_03: According to Belmont, the yew you brought back is found only in the Twelveswood and is much favored by the Ixal, who plant the tree to create living fortifications. Belmont believes that this is evidence that the Ixal are settling in Coerthas, seizing on the distraction afforded by Ishgard's many troubles.
TEXT_GAIUSB710_00905_SEQ_00: Belmont requires your service, and his air of command is hard to resist.
TEXT_GAIUSB710_00905_SEQ_01: Belmont desires contact with his former comrade in the Gods' Quiver in order to quickly begin a campaign against the Ixal in Coerthas. Travel to the North Shroud and take Belmont's letter to Isaudorel at the Bobbing Cork in Fallgourd Float.
TEXT_GAIUSB710_00905_SEQ_02: The White Rams appear to have a particular interest in the Ixal, and Isaudorel is quick to pledge the levy to Belmont's campaign. Isaudorel also lets drop that Belmont inexplicably traded an honored place in the White Rams for the life of a sellsword...
TEXT_GAIUSB711_00906_SEQ_00: A wounded animal is a dangerous animal, and the White Ram convalescing in Fallgourd Float fits the bill. Whatever Isaudorel has in mind, best to say yes.
TEXT_GAIUSB711_00906_SEQ_01: Laid up at an inn after being wounded by the Ixal, Isaudorel has no choice but to ask another to hunt down the scouts. They should still be to the northeast of Fallgourd Float, living off wild game. Hide yourself near the antelope carcass, and slay the Ixali wildtalons when they appear.
TEXT_GAIUSB711_00906_SEQ_02: The hunters become the hunted, and the wildtalons prove no match for your road-hardened ferity. Take a moment to reflect on whether you are growing too steely for your own good, then report the kill to Isaudorel.
TEXT_GAIUSB711_00906_SEQ_03: Isaudorel is sincerely grateful for your work. Clearly, the thought of those two wildtalons at large had weighed on his mind. Listening to him plot further vengeance, it occurs to you that in wounding Isaudorel, the Ixal have made him twice as dangerous...
TEXT_GAIUSB712_00907_SEQ_00: Isaudorel's companion has been taciturn till now, but when Ireine has something to say, all present are advised to listen.
TEXT_GAIUSB712_00907_SEQ_01: Overhearing your conversation with Isaudorel, Ireine bids you take Coerthas' Ixal problem up the chain of command. Leave Ireine and Isaudorel to hurl comradely abuse at one another and make your report to Miah Molkot at Eugenia's Spire.
TEXT_GAIUSB712_00907_SEQ_02: Miah Molkot accepts Belmont's request without demur and with much purr. You learn that the White Rams are in fact a counter-Ixal levy, and on a personal level, Molkot appears to take nearly gustatory delight in defeating the birdmen.
TEXT_GAIUSB713_00908_SEQ_00: Instructor Molkot commands both fear and loyalty, and one of those will bend you to her will. Resist not, and find out what she wants.
TEXT_GAIUSB713_00908_SEQ_01: Miah Molkot is never without a violent plan or three, and the barricade erected by the Ixal only stokes the flames. Take the bomb finger, make your way to the blockade on the north corridor, and blast it into oblivion.
TEXT_GAIUSB713_00908_SEQ_02: The blockade is no more, and the north corridor stands open. Take the happy news to Molkot.
TEXT_GAIUSB713_00908_SEQ_03: Molkot greets the news with eyes glittering and tail lashing. At certain times, she reminds you of some exotic creature─impossible to control, casually bloodthirsty, and hypnotic to behold.
TEXT_GAIUSB714_00909_SEQ_00: The incomparable body language of her people says loud and clear that Molkot requires one adventurer, ready to travel, right meow.
TEXT_GAIUSB714_00909_SEQ_01: With much hissing and spitting, Molkot has decided to commit the White Rams to a struggle that sprawls beyond the Twelveswood into Coerthas. Give her letter to Belmont, and inform the sellsword that the Rams are with him.
TEXT_GAIUSB714_00909_SEQ_02: You deliver the letter to Belmont, who is thunderstruck to receive word from the leader of the Rams herself. As he in turn pledges himself to the fight, you can almost see the louche swagger of the sellsword fall away from him...
TEXT_GAIUSB804_00913_SEQ_00: Ser Aurelle of House Haillenarte wishes to thank the lord of House Fortemps, and only an adventurer can pull off such a fraught exchange.
TEXT_GAIUSB804_00913_SEQ_01: Ser Aurelle has a mind to discreetly present Lord Haurchefant with a gift, for the great debt of Lord Francel's life and the honor of House Haillenarte. Speak with Emanuel and collect a bottle of Daniffen's Joy.
TEXT_GAIUSB804_00913_SEQ_02: Emanuel entrusts you with a rare liquor of Ser Aurelle's choosing. Resist the fleeting urge to down the entire bottle and deliver it to Medguistl, a member of Haurchefant's household.
TEXT_GAIUSB804_00913_SEQ_03: Medguistl takes delivery of the bottle, and, astute as always, guesses from whom it actually issues. His lordship is bound to be pleased in any case, for his life has had little joy lately.
TEXT_GAIUSB805_00914_SEQ_00: Only Ishgard would have an actual valley of death, conveniently located nearby. A lady nobly born seeks an adventurer to walk in its shadow.
TEXT_GAIUSB805_00914_SEQ_01: Juline desires whatever remains of the rosary her beloved wore when he perished at the hands of the inquisitors. Plumb the grim depth of Witchdrop to the east, and find the crystal beads.
TEXT_GAIUSB805_00914_SEQ_02: After a long search and an unsettling encounter, you have found three of the four beads. Keep the whereabouts of the fourth to yourself, for closed lips are a virtue in Ishgard, and deliver the beads to Juline.
TEXT_GAIUSB805_00914_SEQ_03: Seemingly at peace in the calm waters between knowing and unknowing, Juline speaks of her lost love with a quiet grace that shames the sound and fury of the inquisition. How fragile life is in Ishgard, that a single accusation can end it all...
TEXT_GAIUSB806_00915_SEQ_00: The Sharlayans say there are no greater generals than old women with naught to lose, and Meduil's steely gaze says she means to send you to war.
TEXT_GAIUSB806_00915_SEQ_01: Meduil's son perished in the Ogre's Belly, and she will have no others robbed by his killer. Spill the karakul blood as bait, then slay the ravening gorgotaur drawn by the scent.
TEXT_GAIUSB806_00915_SEQ_02: The gorgotaur, grown fat on easy kills in the blizzard, is no match for your skills. Yet you are still heartsore, for a dead killer is cold comfort. You find a mythril rosary among the moldering bones; give it to Meduil.
TEXT_GAIUSB806_00915_SEQ_03: In Ishgard, the measure of honor accorded to those killed by Dravanians is the measure of scorn heaped on those slain otherwise. Against that stark truth, your small act of kindness appears to mean all the more to Meduil.
TEXT_GAIUSB807_00916_SEQ_00: Ser Eugennoix is looking more vexed than usual as his eyes scan the camp for a very special someone─namely you.
TEXT_GAIUSB807_00916_SEQ_01: Dragons have been sighted near the broken husk of the Steel Vigil, and Ser Eugennoix is keen to seek traces of their presence. See what you can find in the abandoned stronghold.
TEXT_GAIUSB807_00916_SEQ_02: You have found an ancient tome, its cover now worn and faded. It has a peculiar silken warmth, like the pate of a sleeping babe. Deliver the almanac to Eugennoix before its charm grows upon you.
TEXT_GAIUSB807_00916_SEQ_03: The tome is apparently much beloved of unbelievers and forbidden by the Holy See. Ser Eugennoix indicates that the Dravanians and unbelievers are making a concerted effort to prevent the rebuilding of the Steel Vigil.
TEXT_GAIUSB809_00918_SEQ_00: When a merchant is wroth, there is usually coin to be made in solving a problem─and Edwyn is looking very wroth indeed.
TEXT_GAIUSB809_00918_SEQ_01: An order of ceruleum has yet to arrive from Ul'dah, and Edwyn is furious at the supplier. Go to the markets of the Sapphire Avenue Exchange, find Syntgoht, and /doubt his words, and he may spill the truth.
TEXT_GAIUSB809_00918_SEQ_02: Under the weight of your skepticism, Syntgoht admits that there is a problem with the ceruleum shipment, and hints that he is as much a victim as Edwyn. His waffling will not do much to ease Edwyn's mistrust of Ul'dahns, you fear.
TEXT_GAIUSB810_00919_SEQ_00: Caught between a rock and a tight place, a middleman will always produce a pot of grease. Find out what Syntgoht has in mind.
TEXT_GAIUSB810_00919_SEQ_01: Syntgoht complains that the shipment of processed ceruleum from the mines of Amajina & Sons has stopped. You wonder why he continued taking orders from customers in that case, but that is not your bailiwick. Go to Camp Bluefog and talk to the Concern's company man, Papawazu.
TEXT_GAIUSB810_00919_SEQ_02: You hear Papawazu's side of the story, though you are not quite certain if he was even speaking to you half the time. He too has his own cross to bear, presumably.
TEXT_GAIUSB811_00920_SEQ_00: When ceruleum is thin on the ground, plots grow thick. None other than Papawazu, the nine-time Employee of the Moon, wishes to consort with you.
TEXT_GAIUSB811_00920_SEQ_01: Papawazu is inclined to think that porters are pilfering the processed ceruleum coming out of the plant. You have his leave to question them; approach the spirited porter and express your /doubt.
TEXT_GAIUSB811_00920_SEQ_02: Unbowed by your withering skepticism, the porter protests his innocence. Assume for a moment he is not guilty until so proven, and check the barrels of processed ceruleum as he bade you.
TEXT_GAIUSB811_00920_SEQ_03: Resigned to spending a few interminable bells inventorying the ceruleum, you are pleasantly surprised to be attacked by coblyns instead. You are less charmed by what they were doing: drinking the ceruleum. Speak with the spirited porter.
TEXT_GAIUSB811_00920_SEQ_04: Lucky for you, the porter's amazement at the coblyns' obnoxious choice of beverage usurps any righteous fury he might have unleashed. Additional ceruleum from the plant will make up for the current shortfall. Report the facts to Papawazu.
TEXT_GAIUSB811_00920_SEQ_05: Papawazu receives the news with his characteristic aplomb of sorts. It seems the porters will get much-needed protection from fell creatures, but no doubt be assigned the blame for the impending price gouge...
TEXT_GAIUSB812_00921_SEQ_00: Sibold has but little time left, and would confide to you his burdens.
TEXT_GAIUSB812_00921_SEQ_01: The advancing years spell the end of Sibold's annual pilgrimage to Cutter's Cry. Along with Nymeia lilies for the burial mound, the famed sellsword entrusts you with the tale of his companions' death─and of his own survival.
TEXT_GAIUSB812_00921_SEQ_02: Time has gentled the contours of the earth raised over the dead. You place the lilies and say your young  orisons before espying Private Norman guarding the entrance of the cave. Speak with him.
TEXT_GAIUSB812_00921_SEQ_03:
Norman affirms that the chimera still lives. The sound he bade you listen to seems to grow stronger, melding with the beat of your own heart...

※Cutter's Cry can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_GAIUSB813_00922_SEQ_00: Papawazu would offer you another commission and a chance to admire him, if the mood strikes you.
TEXT_GAIUSB813_00922_SEQ_01: The shipment of processed ceruleum will finally resume, to the satisfaction of all parties─well, except the coblyns, but creatures of their sort have no say, and dead ones doubly so. Report the news to Syntgoht at the Sapphire Avenue Exchange.
TEXT_GAIUSB813_00922_SEQ_02: Syntgoht is relieved, though vexed by the price hike. Once the goods reach him in a few days, he should in turn be able to fill his orders.
TEXT_GAIUSB814_00923_SEQ_00: A middleman is the pepper of commerce─useless alone, excellent in moderation, pernicious in excess. Whichever one Syntgoht happens to be, he has a task that may interest you.
TEXT_GAIUSB814_00923_SEQ_01: With Amajina & Sons now aware of the coblyns in their closet, Syntgoht will finally be able to fulfill his orders. His relief is palpable and his penitence potent. Start the last leg of your journey and deliver the cherry brandewine to Edwyn.
TEXT_GAIUSB814_00923_SEQ_02: The convoluted tale of ceruleum shortage is well received by Edwyn, especially when you pass on the cherry brandewine along with Syntgoht's apology. Words are wind, but a costly bottle of nectar sets a great deal to rights.
TEXT_GAIUSB905_00928_SEQ_00: For some like the pushful Ser Oncenedl, an adventurer is naught but a scullion for a task most macabre.
TEXT_GAIUSB905_00928_SEQ_01: With no small disdain, Ser Oncenedl bids you search the body of a heretic for personal items and deliver these to the Gates of Judgement. Apparently, some in the Holy See believe they will yield valuable information.
TEXT_GAIUSB905_00928_SEQ_02: An adventurer once said that there are no dirty jobs, only dirty memories─and you sense that you may be testing this theory quite soon. Take the sack of effects to Ser Chaunollet at the Gates of Judgement.
TEXT_GAIUSB905_00928_SEQ_03: Ser Chaunollet commends you for looting the dead, and appears hopeful that this sad detritus of an interrupted life will further the cause of Ishgard. You know not what to think, but the work is done and a wash awaits...
TEXT_GAIUSB906_00929_SEQ_00: A good commander looks to his men rather than his betters, and Ser Jeantremont, one such knight, seeks your help.
TEXT_GAIUSB906_00929_SEQ_01: The ceaseless fighting has sapped the strength of dragoons and commonfolk alike at Whitebrim Front. Mortified yet resolved, Ser Jeantremont bids you beg Ser Marcelain, keeper of the Gates of Judgement, to send more men.
TEXT_GAIUSB906_00929_SEQ_02: You make your request for reinforcements with as much eloquence as you can muster, but far from being receptive, Ser Marcelain threatens to cut supplies and throats. This was not your finest hour...
TEXT_GAIUSB907_00930_SEQ_00: Ser Loanne would have you cull birds for the sake of all that is holy.
TEXT_GAIUSB907_00930_SEQ_01: Ser Loanne of Ishgard bids you cull some flying menace in the area. Though bemused by her high-handed vehemence, you are prepared to do as she asks and slay five bateleurs.
TEXT_GAIUSB907_00930_SEQ_02: You slay five bateleurs, growing more dubious with each one, but a job is a job. Return to Ser Loanne and see whether she can tell you what use they are dead.
TEXT_GAIUSB907_00930_SEQ_03: Pleased with your commission of this menial task, Ser Loanne reveals that the bateleurs share the knights' fondness for cloud cutters and other fish of the Sea of Clouds. In Ishgard, it is never a good idea to want what the knights want...
TEXT_GAIUSB908_00931_SEQ_00: Ser Chaunollet believes that removing debris is beneath an Ishgardian's dignity.
TEXT_GAIUSB908_00931_SEQ_01: The once-proud Gates of Judgement have taken another dragon strike, and a spew of rubble makes the roads both dangerous and disheartening to travel. Refusing to soil gallant hands with such a task, Ser Chaunollet bids you remove the rubble.
TEXT_GAIUSB908_00931_SEQ_02: The rubble has been cleared, and the ground now bears no trace of the recent dragon attack─though the Gates themselves are another matter altogether. Ser Chaunollet will no doubt be pleased to hear of the former.
TEXT_GAIUSB908_00931_SEQ_03: Under the requisite fervor of the knights of Ishgard, Ser Chaunollet clearly has a deeper well of feeling; his grief at the disfigurement of the Gates of Judgement is genuine─as is his longing to eradicate dragonkind for this crime.
TEXT_GAIUSB909_00932_SEQ_00: Ser Chaunollet would have you perform another bit of gathering to aid the knights' plight.
TEXT_GAIUSB909_00932_SEQ_01: With a slightly histrionic imperiousness, Ser Chaunollet bids you bring him the fat from chinchillas. You know too little of Ishgardian cookery to know the reason why, but slay four chinchillas and collect their rich leaf fat.
TEXT_GAIUSB909_00932_SEQ_02: The chinchillas were curiously abundant and well fed for dainty beasts in the dead of winter. Coerthas is full of mysteries such as these, but forbear in your sleuthing for now, and place the creamy fat in the hands of Ser Chaunollet.
TEXT_GAIUSB909_00932_SEQ_03: His domineering mien momentarily forgotten, Ser Chaunollet professes delight at the quality of the fat. In light of the beasts' unaccountable plumpness, you are pleased to hear that the fat is destined for chocobo feet, rather than the stew pot.
TEXT_GAIUSB910_00933_SEQ_00: Unlike other more menial tasks, Ser Faucillien would set to you a mission of some importance.
TEXT_GAIUSB910_00933_SEQ_01: There are large troop movements around Whitebrim Front, and Faucillien requests that you slay the Dravanian outwatches that slow the column. He bids you go deep into the forest northwest of the Front, and bait these dragon thralls with dragon scales.
TEXT_GAIUSB910_00933_SEQ_02: The Dravanian outwatches are dead. Moved by instinct rather than belief, they die without any lurid displays, ponderous words, or─the Twelve help you for you have seen it and cannot unsee it─poetry. Return to Ser Faucillien and report your success.
TEXT_GAIUSB910_00933_SEQ_03: Ser Faucillien commends you and reveals that Ishgard marches on the Stone Vigil, the stronghold lost to the Dravanians. A bold and glorious assault, but you cannot suppress your misgivings...
TEXT_GAIUSB911_00934_SEQ_00: When a chance to see a real-life heretic presents itself, how could an adventurer resist? Visit with Boyle and see what rattles his cage today.
TEXT_GAIUSB911_00934_SEQ_01: The heretic Boyle demands a sacrifice to offer to the dragons. This stretches even the very elastic definition of an adventurer's trade, but the imprisoned madman excites your pity. Ferdillaix may know if something can be done.
TEXT_GAIUSB911_00934_SEQ_02: While unmoved by the broken, raving man in his dungeons, Ferdillaix gives you a dead rat solely to have some peace and quiet. A mangy dungeon rat is no fatted calf, but give it to Boyle anyway, for heretics cannot be choosers.
TEXT_GAIUSB911_00934_SEQ_03: Boyle croons ecstatically over the dead rat, and begins some sort of a mumbled ritual chant. The less you linger near these doomed men, the better for your health. Make your report to Ferdillaix, and make haste.
TEXT_GAIUSB911_00934_SEQ_04: Ferdillaix grouses about the din caused by Boyle. It does seem inconvenient that in exposing a man's heresy, the inquisitors also make him loud and more than a little mad. However, no good can come of humoring unbelievers or criticizing the inquisitors...
TEXT_GAIUSB912_00935_SEQ_00: What Charmine the chirurgeon seeks is an infusion for her ailing infirmary, but she will settle for an adventurer instead.
TEXT_GAIUSB912_00935_SEQ_01: Charmine's patient is past all help that can be provided by the undersupplied infirmary. Raging at her own helplessness, the chirurgeon ministers to her charge in the only way left─by bidding you send word to her betrothed, Laurence, a deserter condemned to the dungeons.
TEXT_GAIUSB912_00935_SEQ_02: Roused from his gloom by the shocking news, Laurence urges you out after only a few hurried words. Your destination must be the forest to the southeast, for when the music of love and death plays, there is naught to do but dance.
TEXT_GAIUSB912_00935_SEQ_03: Laurence's treasure turns out to be an alchemic concoction of Ul'dahn origin. What you hold in your hand cost a man his freedom, and may save a woman's life. Deliver it to Charmine forthwith, and the Fury take you if you drop it.
TEXT_GAIUSB912_00935_SEQ_04: Charmine's eyes widen at the sight of medicine so precious, and she immediately deduces Laurence's sacrifice. You sense in her fury and even disgust at the cruelty of war, and an iron determination to keep alight this guttering candle...
TEXT_GAIUSB913_00936_SEQ_00: Fousquenet finds himself besieged by the mighty rat king, and seeks an adventurer's assistance.
TEXT_GAIUSB913_00936_SEQ_01: Rats of unusual size are to be seen around the stronghold feeding, scurrying, and baring their yellow teeth at all and sundry. Fousquenet asks that you search the courtyard and kill any rats you find.
TEXT_GAIUSB913_00936_SEQ_02: You have found several rats and made sure they shall gnaw no more. Fousquenet will be glad to hear of it from your lips.
TEXT_GAIUSB913_00936_SEQ_03: Encouraged by your speed and aplomb, Fousquenet lays out a more ambitious plan. He believes there is a large nest underground that can be gotten at from outside the walls of the stronghold. Survey the rats' nest and kill the rat king.
TEXT_GAIUSB913_00936_SEQ_04: The lord of the midden is dead, and you can hear the pack beginning to turn on each other in the confusion. This would be a good time to go back inside, Kingslayer, and tell Fousquenet that his end has been achieved.
TEXT_GAIUSB913_00936_SEQ_05: The grain sacks of Whitebrim Front are safer tonight, and knights shall sleep without fear of rat bites. Fousquenet's foresight and your incomparable reflexes have saved the day.
TEXT_GAIUSC005_00942_SEQ_00: Ser Liautroix has heard of your growing repute and wishes to engage you.
TEXT_GAIUSC005_00942_SEQ_01: Ser Liautroix has it in his mind to repair the outpost's bell, the very same that serves as the sigil of House Durendaire. To this end, the dragoons must be persuaded to hand over their discarded weapons.
TEXT_GAIUSC005_00942_SEQ_02: No persuasion proves necessary, for the fighting men and women of the Front are all eager to see their bell restored to its former glory. You hope that Tuatkk the smith will feel as they do, especially when he sees the arms you have collected.
TEXT_GAIUSC005_00942_SEQ_03: It must be your nameday for everyone to fall in so eagerly with your requests. Tuatkk promises to begin work before the . Ser Liautroix will want to know the good news as soon as possible.
TEXT_GAIUSC005_00942_SEQ_04: Ser Liautroix is moved to discover that others are with him in this endeavor. Cold are the winds that blow on the Front, and from a green recruit to a seasoned smith, all who dwell there must hold fast to one another...
TEXT_GAIUSC006_00943_SEQ_00: Head chirurgeon Astidien would have you escort a most valuable prize from Camp Dragonhead.
TEXT_GAIUSC006_00943_SEQ_01: Overrun with patients for many moons, the infirmary at the Front has finally persuaded the powers-that-be to assign them another chirurgeon. Astidien bids you escort this welcome new addition from Camp Dragonhead.
TEXT_GAIUSC006_00943_SEQ_02: Alas, you and the chirurgeon have somehow missed each other. It is likely that he is dying slowly out in the snow even as you bemoan his foolishness. Find the lost chirurgeon and dose him with the life-saving maddening potion.
TEXT_GAIUSC006_00943_SEQ_03: You find the chirurgeon and restore him to health─or at least to some version of it that will get him to the Front. On a second thought, it was possibly a poor decision to let loose a recently frozen naif under the influence of anything described as “maddening.” It would behoove you to find him again.
TEXT_GAIUSC006_00943_SEQ_04: You appear in the nick of time to strike down two dragonflies attacking the chirurgeon. Disaster seems to love this man, but still, speak to him.
TEXT_GAIUSC006_00943_SEQ_05: You allow the chirurgeon to go his way, for he seemed calm enough. Besides, it is known that a man who escapes death twice in one day will escape it the third time as well. Take yourself to Astidien and tell him the tale.
TEXT_GAIUSC006_00943_SEQ_06: As you predicted, the chirurgeon not only reached the Front, but is cheating death for the third time as you make your report to Astidien. The head chirurgeon may feel otherwise, but your road sense tells you the naif will do much good here.
TEXT_GAIUSC007_00944_SEQ_00: Honest men make the best conspirators, and Ser Daimbert would seek your help with his own transformation.
TEXT_GAIUSC007_00944_SEQ_01: Ser Daimbert entrusts you with a most dangerous mission: to break his brother Laurence out of his fetters before the Holy See executes him for heresy. The gaoler Ferdillaix sleeps at his post, and you must borrow his key.
TEXT_GAIUSC007_00944_SEQ_02: The heavy key is safely in your hands, and Ser Ferdillaix remains asleep, dreaming of a happier night at the table. The bars are generously spaced, fortunately, and the key may be passed to Laurence without any difficulty.
TEXT_GAIUSC007_00944_SEQ_03: Laurence is overjoyed to learn that his brother loves him still, and has taken the monumental risk of breaking a heretic out of the gaol. Ser Daimbert needs to be told that once the light grows kinder, Laurence will make his attempt.
TEXT_GAIUSC007_00944_SEQ_04: You are taken aback by Ser Daimbert's thoroughness in planning this escape. None shall know of your part in this, of which you are grateful. You have no doubt scores will vouch for his and your innocence in this matter...
TEXT_GAIUSC008_00945_SEQ_00: Ser Berengeoit strikes you as a man with a sizable chip upon his shoulder, and such men are often ready to spend handsomely.
TEXT_GAIUSC008_00945_SEQ_01: Ser Berengeoit insists that one dark night, he slew a wounded dragon with a well-aimed shot from a ballista. Alas, without a trophy, none will call him aught but a fevered fool. Someone must find the carcass and bring back a bone.
TEXT_GAIUSC008_00945_SEQ_02: To your mild surprise, you find a dead dragon on a gorge floor as the young knight insisted, and collect from it a fine bone. This trophy will mean more to Ser Berengeoit than all the fish in the Sea of Clouds.
TEXT_GAIUSC008_00945_SEQ_03: Ser Berengeoit receives the dragon bone with something resembling ecstasy. If even half the knights of Ishgard are as covetous of a kill, there is little to stop the war from continuing to rage...
TEXT_GAIUSC009_00946_SEQ_00: Rumor has it that Forsemart has a job that involves travel.
TEXT_GAIUSC009_00946_SEQ_01: Forsemart reveals that he is one of those searching for answers in Snowcloak, but the expedition faces an uncertain future after its sellswords abandoned their posts. If you are interested in seeing this wondrous ice wall, Ourdilic is the one to speak to.
TEXT_GAIUSC009_00946_SEQ_02: Ourdilic notes with some acerbity that the dragoons claimed to be able to spare not a single man. Knowing the situation at Whitebrim Front, you suspect this was naught but the stark truth...
TEXT_GAIUSC010_00947_SEQ_00: Ourdilic seems glad of your presence and cannot wait to set you to work.
TEXT_GAIUSC010_00947_SEQ_01: While mostly harmless, hippocerfs can be infuriating to the point of harm. Ourdilic asks that you slay the three that have proven most vexing of late.
TEXT_GAIUSC010_00947_SEQ_02: The hippocerfs no longer need worry endlessly over every little thing. Death can be a tonic for natural procrastinators─an insight you may share with Ourdilic along with your report.
TEXT_GAIUSC010_00947_SEQ_03: The cull of the hippocerfs has been reported, and a decidedly more relaxed Ourdilic suggests you see the ice wall, which blocks the road that formerly connected west and east Coerthas. The effects of the Calamity run deep, and in Coerthas, cold...
TEXT_GAIUSC011_00948_SEQ_00: When lovers call, an adventurer must answer─for along with art, truth, and justice, love is one of life's great adventures. Will you hear Lancefer's plea?
TEXT_GAIUSC011_00948_SEQ_01: Behind the western face of Snowcloak are entombed villagers of Falcon's Nest, and Lancefer begs you to free one body in particular from its icy embrace. Use the iron pick on the weak spot on the western face.
TEXT_GAIUSC011_00948_SEQ_02: Your efforts are rewarded by a frozen corpse. If this is Lancefer's wife, she should have a ring of troth upon her hand. Check the body for the ring.
TEXT_GAIUSC011_00948_SEQ_03: You find a ring. This, then, is the mortal remain of the woman Lancefer calls his heart, for whom he returned to this perilous place. Tarry not in this icy crypt, and take the ring back to Lancefer.
TEXT_GAIUSC011_00948_SEQ_04: They say Ishgardian wives are adept at waiting─for their men to return from the Front, for the scorched earth to sprout again, for happiness to find them─but Lancefer's wife need wait no more. In this act of love, surely he will find some peace.
TEXT_GAIUSC012_00949_SEQ_00: Ourdilic is seeking aid for a rescue attempt.
TEXT_GAIUSC012_00949_SEQ_01: One of the researchers at Snowcloak has not yet returned from collecting ice samples, and he has a reputation for attracting ice sprites. Ourdilic bids you find the hapless man, and if necessary, rescue him from attackers.
TEXT_GAIUSC012_00949_SEQ_02: Ourdilic proves to be impressively correct in her surmise, for you come across the whey-faced researcher cringing from the ice sprite. Now that you have slain the sprite and extricated yourself from the researcher's fawning attentions, you must make your report to Ourdilic.
TEXT_GAIUSC012_00949_SEQ_03: Ourdilic has a spot of good news for you as well; she has nipped in the bud the researcher's hopes for a . A happy ending for everyone─except the ice sprite, of course.
TEXT_GAIUSC013_00950_SEQ_00: Meurise is concerned for a lost patrol fighting for warmth out in the howling blizzard.
TEXT_GAIUSC013_00950_SEQ_01: Meurise receives word that a patrol from another camp huddles in the Behemoth's Dominion, their reckoning shredded by the howling winds and snow. Sending medics with litters is out of the question, but emergency brandewine may do the trick.
TEXT_GAIUSC013_00950_SEQ_02: You give the bottle of brandewine to one of the men, who rapidly emerges from his stupor. He will see to the rest of the men, and use this lull in the storm to return to their camp. You must do likewise, lest you make the same mistake they did.
TEXT_GAIUSC013_00950_SEQ_03: Thanks to the restorative brandewine you have conveyed, the patrol has made it back to camp without losing a single man. You have apparently saved their lives for better things─namely, dying in a much more painful way.
TEXT_GAIUSC014_00951_SEQ_00: Ser Briannaix is concerned for a comrade who has taken a tumble off of a snow-covered cliff.
TEXT_GAIUSC014_00951_SEQ_01: Ser Briannaix needs help rescuing a comrade who has fallen over a cliff. There is a length of thick rope to be found in the keep which would be perfect for the job.
TEXT_GAIUSC014_00951_SEQ_02: The rope is of goodly length, and reassuringly heavy in your hands. On the cliff top, another dragoon keeps watch as Ser Briannaix said. He will no doubt be glad to speak to you.
TEXT_GAIUSC014_00951_SEQ_03: Aside from being trapped at the base of a steep cliff, the dragoon seems to be in fine shape. All he needs is one end of the rope in his hands, and he can climb out. The question is how to do so, with the high winds snapping the rope up and away as soon as you drop it.
TEXT_GAIUSC014_00951_SEQ_04: What a soldier denies, an adventurer tries. Securing one end of the rope at the top of the cliff, you leap down with the other. The trapped dragoon is trapped no more, though he will feel the exertion tomorrow. Ser Briannaix will surely be gratified to hear of the rescue.
TEXT_GAIUSC014_00951_SEQ_05: The rough-hewn knight is indeed appreciative, and shows himself to be blunt in speech. The gap between those who actually fight the war and those in command seems to be growing, with the pride of the latter trumping the needs of the former...
TEXT_GAIUSC106_00957_SEQ_00: Helmhart has it in his head that you are his mane man, and returns to you with an even more hair-raising request.
TEXT_GAIUSC106_00957_SEQ_01: Helmhart's malady has taken a turn for the worse, and he begins girding his loins for what may well be the final battle. Stalk the golden fleeces near the Burning Wall, and obtain five vials of snurble blood.
TEXT_GAIUSC106_00957_SEQ_02: You have drained the blood from your vanquished prey. Rush the crimson cargo to Helmhart whilst he still has the strength to make use of it.
TEXT_GAIUSC106_00957_SEQ_03: Seizing the fresh snurble blood, Helmhart concocts a tonic even more noxious than the previous one. Apply a generous amount and think of Eorzea.
TEXT_GAIUSC106_00957_SEQ_04: You have fulfilled your duties with admirable stolidity. While Helmhart's ecstatic cries indicate a certain kind of efficacy, you fear that, like the tide, his receding hairline waits for no man.
TEXT_GAIUSC107_00958_SEQ_00: A rolling stone such as yourself will surely find some business in common with a fellow called Floating Stone, if you would but speak to the miner.
TEXT_GAIUSC107_00958_SEQ_01: The area surrounding Burgundy Falls has a unique species of coblyn called the quartz doblyn, found only in certain parts of Thanalan. Floating Stone bids you slay five of these rare creatures for the sole purpose of harvesting clear quartz from them.
TEXT_GAIUSC107_00958_SEQ_02: You have enough clear quartz to satisfy Floating Stone's thirst for crystals. Return to Burgundy Falls and deliver them to the Roegadyn miner.
TEXT_GAIUSC107_00958_SEQ_03: Floating Stone seems less than heartbroken by the Calamity, which makes a refreshing change from nearly everybody else on the subject. The hills are still a candy shop, and he a child with a sweet tooth and a pickaxe...
TEXT_GAIUSC205_00964_SEQ_00: Otan Yaratan looks to be scared out of his wits.
TEXT_GAIUSC205_00964_SEQ_01: A man who lives with the vagaries of the sea can hardly be craven, but Otan Yaratan clearly rates ghosts above shipwrecks in the fear factor. Permit him to cower and dispatch five restless spirits locally known as dead man's moans.
TEXT_GAIUSC205_00964_SEQ_02: For a skilled adventurer, death is apparently no obstacle to slaying. Return to Pharos Sirius and speak with Otan Yaratan.
TEXT_GAIUSC205_00964_SEQ_03: Relieved, the lighthouse keeper pours out his woes to your sympathetic ear. What in the name of the Twelve is happening at the once-quiet Pharos Sirius?
TEXT_GAIUSC206_00965_SEQ_00: There are spirits, and then there are spirits. Ahlduwil craves one while fearing the other.
TEXT_GAIUSC206_00965_SEQ_01: You find a self-proclaimed salvager well in his cups who bids you fill his empty bottle from a cask of wine over in the Ship Graveyard. Knowing something of wine from shipwrecks, you decide to oblige.
TEXT_GAIUSC206_00965_SEQ_02: You enter the Ship Graveyard and brave the dank and haunted place to find a cask of wine, dispatching a spirit along the way. With the bottle of salvaged wine securely in your possession, it's time you returned to Ahlduwil.
TEXT_GAIUSC206_00965_SEQ_03: Ahlduwil receives the vintage greedily, then laments that it has turned sulphurous with age. Now that his dream of drinking his way through the Graveyard's holds has ended, you hope he will be a sot no more.
TEXT_GAIUSC207_00966_SEQ_00: The haunted wrecks contain all manner of precious cargo, and Erapi Taropi believes he can find just the spice to take his soup from bland to grand.
TEXT_GAIUSC207_00966_SEQ_01: Forced to wait out the ongoing haunting of the Isles of Umbra, the reluctant looter Erapi Taropi busies himself with supper. While his fish chowder smells just fine to you, he would have you help him improve it all the same. Venture into the Ship Graveyard and bring back a handful of Far Eastern spices from an abandoned spice box.
TEXT_GAIUSC207_00966_SEQ_02: You have located the box and grabbed a handful of its contents. Are spices usually so squishy? They certainly do things differently in the Far East. Deliver the spices to Erapi Taropi's more capable hands.
TEXT_GAIUSC207_00966_SEQ_03: You hand the spices to Erapi Taropi, who discovers that they are a moldy mess...after stirring them into the chowder. Your appetite departs abruptly at the smell, and poor Erapi Taropi begins to gloomily count his gil for fresh supplies.
TEXT_GAIUSC302_00969_SEQ_00: Selaine needs a seasoned adventurer to go with her perfume.
TEXT_GAIUSC302_00969_SEQ_01: Selaine has a short but discerning shopping list, and apparently, you are on it. Take yourself and an atomizer of sweetrose perfume to Jeulerand, so she can cross you off her roll of errands.
TEXT_GAIUSC302_00969_SEQ_02: Jeulerand takes delivery of the perfume, and regards you with inexplicable delight. Let us hope that his definition of a good adventurer is not too far off the beaten path.
TEXT_GAIUSC303_00970_SEQ_00: What drives Jeulerand to seek an adventurer's help─the sweet smell of success or the acrid stench of failure?
TEXT_GAIUSC303_00970_SEQ_01: Jeulerand confesses that he finds the sylphs discomfiting to talk to. Go in his stead to present Dellexia with sweetrose perfume.
TEXT_GAIUSC303_00970_SEQ_02: The sylphs complain that Jeulerand is discomfiting to talk to, but are delighted with the gift. Leave the sylphs oohing and aahing over the atomizer, and head to Larkscall to collect sylvan lily seeds.
TEXT_GAIUSC303_00970_SEQ_03: As Dellexia said, you need both luck and a keen eye to find the seeds. Luckily, you have both by the caskful. Now that you have the seeds, place them in the hands of Kain, the master botanist at the Sanctum of the Twelve.
TEXT_GAIUSC303_00970_SEQ_04: Kain seems serenely aware of his apprentice's disinclination to work. You see the beautiful garden that he has grown to exalt the Twelve, and wonder if mayhap there is more divinity outside the Sanctum than inside.
TEXT_GAIUSC305_00972_SEQ_00: A rose is a rose is a helping hand, at least when a kindly botanist spots a man on the verge of botching his troth.
TEXT_GAIUSC305_00972_SEQ_01: Unlike the , Kain keeps a kindly eye on the people who walk the grounds. Taking pity on a painfully nervous young lover, he asks you to deliver a bouquet of roses to him.
TEXT_GAIUSC305_00972_SEQ_02: The sight of the flowers brings the young man out of his fluster. He heads for his lady love, full of happy determination. Kain will be pleased─but not surprised─to hear of this.
TEXT_GAIUSC305_00972_SEQ_03: Was it the flowers, or the kindness of strangers that smoothed the course of this love? To love is to be smiled upon by one, but to be wed is to be smiled upon by the sundry...
TEXT_GAIUSC306_00973_SEQ_00: Elfleda needs help preparing for the social event of the season.
TEXT_GAIUSC306_00973_SEQ_01: All aglow over her attendance at the forthcoming nuptials, Elfleda enlists your help in obtaining wind sprite cores. Slay some wind sprites and collect four cores.
TEXT_GAIUSC306_00973_SEQ_02: You have obtained four wind sprite cores. If you would know why Elfleda needs such a thing for a Ceremony of Eternal Bonding, return to the Sanctum and place the cores in her hands.
TEXT_GAIUSC306_00973_SEQ_03: Elfleda happily confides her plans to create a storm of rose petals for her friend. Imagining shattered windows and an airborne brigade of samite-clad ladies, you suggest she use just the one core...
TEXT_GAIUSC404_00979_SEQ_00: There are dark places that only an adventurer may illume, and Ser Carrilaut is about to point the way to one such pit of peril.
TEXT_GAIUSC404_00979_SEQ_01: According to Ser Carrilaut, the unfinished keep of House Dzemael is much troubled by the continued presence of voidsent in the area. In readiness of your acquiescence, Ser Carrilaut has arranged for someone to meet you there. Speak with Ser Ophelie at the entrance to the Darkhold.
TEXT_GAIUSC404_00979_SEQ_02:
Ser Ophelie has eagerly granted you permission to explore Dzemael Darkhold. Take up the challenge, but remember the oath you swore on your first day as an adventurer.

※Dzemael Darkhold can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_GAIUSC410_00985_SEQ_00: In times of simmering hostility, Ser Cailean would undoubtedly appreciate the aid of an unsuspected adventurer.
TEXT_GAIUSC410_00985_SEQ_01: The Garlean Empire is making a long arm across the border from Mor Dhona, stirring the grass around Monument Tower. Seek traces of Garlemald in three locations, and drive away any Garleans you encounter.
TEXT_GAIUSC410_00985_SEQ_02: Your vigilance has driven out all the Garleans in the area without a confrontation between the forces of Ishgard and Garlemald. Report to Ser Pierremons that the work is done.
TEXT_GAIUSC410_00985_SEQ_03: Ser Pierremons is aghast at how thick the Garleans are upon the ground. All evidence points to a Garlean outpost in Mor Dhona, a place in which even an adventurer may find it no easy task to escape deadly scrutiny...
TEXT_GAIUSC412_00987_SEQ_00: Everyone has need of an adventurer sometimes, even among the brethren, and Aganbold has a most shocking request.
TEXT_GAIUSC412_00987_SEQ_01: Aganbold has a need of catalytic ectoplasm for reasons unknown, or possibly unmentionable. Slay plasmoids and obtain three samples of catalytic plasma.
TEXT_GAIUSC412_00987_SEQ_02: You successfully collect the plasma. Is that acrid taste in your mouth guilt, or are you just happy to see so many crystals? Spread the plasma on the large crystallized tree in Rathefrost.
TEXT_GAIUSC412_00987_SEQ_03: The plasma is spread, and now your lurking begins. When the ectoplasm appears, attack it without provocation.
TEXT_GAIUSC412_00987_SEQ_04: At long last, you have the catalytic ectoplasm. The metallic taste in your mouth has gone, and the ectoplasm in your hands sends up a pleasant hum like a purring kitten. Deliver it to Aganbold.
TEXT_GAIUSC412_00987_SEQ_05: In Aganbold's hands, the ectoplasm is less a contented cat and more a vexed porcupine. Behind the cheerful mien, Aganbold has a secret sorrow─he is averse to lightning, but favored by learned customers with galvanic interests...
TEXT_GAIUSC413_00988_SEQ_00: Npah Tayuun would like you to help her teach a lesson: woe betide any wavekin that stands between a scholar and her research.
TEXT_GAIUSC413_00988_SEQ_01: A crystallized plain lies slumbering to the west, rich with promises of hidden things. Investigate two sites in the remains of Camp Revenant's Toll, and do away with any bothersome nixes that appear.
TEXT_GAIUSC413_00988_SEQ_02: What happens when you hit nixes with sharp metal objects? The same thing that happens to everything else. Return to Npah Tayuun and let her know of your bloody deeds.
TEXT_GAIUSC413_00988_SEQ_03: Someday, you will meet a scholar who does not rejoice at the violent death of a foe, but today is not that day. Alas, your skill at nixing nixes seems to be drawing unwelcome attention from Npah Tayuun...
TEXT_GAIUSC501_00989_SEQ_00: Word is that Guolgeim seeks an extra pair of hands.
TEXT_GAIUSC501_00989_SEQ_01: Guolgeim bids you salvage whatever usable provisions still remain at a ruined camp nearby. Open the crates with a sledgehammer and collect the boxes of abandoned supplies.
TEXT_GAIUSC501_00989_SEQ_02: The area yields three boxes of supplies, none the worse for wear even after five years. Perhaps Guolgeim will tell you more when you deliver the haul.
TEXT_GAIUSC501_00989_SEQ_03: After taking hold of the supplies, Guolgeim reveals to you her reluctance to visit the ruined Camp Revenant's Toll. It does one no good to pick through the detritus of a place that was dear to the heart...
TEXT_GAIUSC502_00990_SEQ_00: According to Kakamehi, there is work and ready coin to be had from the Sons of Saint Coinach, if you would but present yourself there.
TEXT_GAIUSC502_00990_SEQ_01: The Sons of Saint Coinach, the learned men and women who would penetrate the secrets of the ancient Allagan Empire, have set up camp to the southeast of Revenant's Toll. With fellow adventurer Kakamehi's hearty recommendation buoying your reputation, go speak with one Nazyl Duzyl.
TEXT_GAIUSC502_00990_SEQ_02: Nazyl Duzyl greets you with open arms and, you suspect, purse strings. There is much to be done, it seems, and your long experience tells you that your oilstone may be getting extra use...
TEXT_GAIUSC503_00991_SEQ_00: Nazyl Duzyl has a gentle task in mind for your first service to the Sons of Saint Coinach.
TEXT_GAIUSC503_00991_SEQ_01: Many Sons of Saint Coinach are far from home, toiling to uncover ancient secrets while hundreds of malms away from family and friends. Take the letters that have traveled that distance, and place them in the Sons' hands.
TEXT_GAIUSC503_00991_SEQ_02: Every letter has reached the person it was intended for, but you are somewhat crestfallen, for the letters seemed to leave everyone more vexed than they were before. Speak with Nazyl Duzyl and see what he thinks.
TEXT_GAIUSC503_00991_SEQ_03: The worthy bone sifter explains that, vexing or not, the letters remind the naturalists that there is life beyond the dig. You also learn that the Sons are a Sharlayan order, and that their leader is the famed anthropogeographer Rammbroes. Should you have any further questions on the organization's activities, you would do well to seek out his wisdom.
TEXT_GAIUSC504_00992_SEQ_00: Rammbroes has reasons to look concerned, for even a single hippogryph attack is no joke─let alone three.
TEXT_GAIUSC504_00992_SEQ_01: Several members of the Sons of Saint Coinach excavation have been attacked by hippogryphs on the crystallized plain, and the injuries show these were no frisky bumps. Rammbroes bids you cull three of the churlish creatures.
TEXT_GAIUSC504_00992_SEQ_02: You have slain three hippogryphs, and are forced to agree with Rammbroes that they had unusual fleetness of foot and ferity of spirit. Let Rammbroes know the deed is done.
TEXT_GAIUSC504_00992_SEQ_03: The ruins under excavation by the Sons have barely begun giving up their secrets. If the site is indeed home to the builders of the Crystal Tower, it should serve to offer an invaluable insight into the distant past.
TEXT_GAIUSC505_00993_SEQ_00: Wandering Breeze fears that an expedition from the Sons of Saint Coinach is about to become gigas fodder.
TEXT_GAIUSC505_00993_SEQ_01: According to Wandering Breeze, gigas have been harassing one of the Sons' expedition teams. Knowing gigas, it is unlikely they will content themselves with mere provocation for long. Head south and speak with the harried researcher.
TEXT_GAIUSC505_00993_SEQ_02: As expected, a gigas appears and launches an attack, expecting unarmed, low-fat snacks─and is instead fed a meal of metal. The researchers live to study another day, something Wandering Breeze would be relieved to know.
TEXT_GAIUSC505_00993_SEQ_03: You speak with Wandering Breeze, who appears to have quite the information network. Not only has he already been apprised of your heroics, he knows how these gigas came to be in these parts. A useful man, this Wandering Breeze...
TEXT_GAIUSC506_00994_SEQ_00: Klynthota has a theory that is out of this world.
TEXT_GAIUSC506_00994_SEQ_01: Obsessed with the lesser moon since it fell to earth five years ago, Klynthota found, then lost, a fragment of the hammer of the Calamity in the Singing Shards. Lurk there and ambush the elder hapalit with a pepper bomb, and thus regain the fragment.
TEXT_GAIUSC506_00994_SEQ_02: The bomb proved even more effective than you had hoped, and the fragment is yours. It is an odd thing to hold a piece of the moon in your hands, and an ill one at that. It would be best to pass it on to Klynthota as soon as possible.
TEXT_GAIUSC506_00994_SEQ_03: Overjoyed at her specimen's return, Klynthota reveals a startling find─that Dalamud was made of the same curious material as those abundantly found in Allagan artifacts. If she is not mistaken, the implications are dizzying...
TEXT_GAIUSC507_00995_SEQ_00: Wandering Breeze has a recurring gigas problem he would like you to solve.
TEXT_GAIUSC507_00995_SEQ_01: According to Wandering Breeze, the gigas who recently met their end at your hands may not have been quite the mindless brutes you took them for. Like a good historian─or a tactician─Wandering Breeze wants to study the threat. Slay four gigas and search their remains for items of interest.
TEXT_GAIUSC507_00995_SEQ_02: You find a jagged piece of crystal on each of the gigas, the only things out of place among their effects. The crystals seem to be carved in some fashion, but analyzing them is well beyond your area of expertise. Perhaps Wandering Breeze will have better luck.
TEXT_GAIUSC507_00995_SEQ_03: Wandering Breeze theorizes that the gigas consider the Crystal Tower a holy place, and seek to claim it for themselves. Place the carved likeness of the Tower on the chosen spot, and see what happens.
TEXT_GAIUSC507_00995_SEQ_04: Being a mite fuzzy on what a scientific observation entails, you slay the gigas who comes to retrieve the crystal. The dead giant carries with him a detailed sketch of the Crystal Tower. Curious indeed. Hand it to Wandering Breeze and see what he says.
TEXT_GAIUSC507_00995_SEQ_05: The drawing turns out to be from the documents stolen from the Sons of Saint Coinach. Do these fell creatures also burn to discover the secret of the Crystal Tower? If so, they may be an even greater threat than was supposed...
TEXT_GAIUSC508_00996_SEQ_00: You feel the call of the road, but when a mishap strikes, Nazyl Duzyl has one more call on your time.
TEXT_GAIUSC508_00996_SEQ_01: One of a pair of researchers excavating a lakeside site has fallen down a hole. Nazyl Duzyl bids you head west and deliver a length of thick rope to the wrought researcher that awaits assistance for his learned colleague.
TEXT_GAIUSC508_00996_SEQ_02: Once given the rope, the researcher trades his anxiety for resoluteness. He orders you to leave the rescue to him and take an urgent message to Kakamehi in Revenant's Toll: send medicines.
TEXT_GAIUSC508_00996_SEQ_03: Having delivered the message to Kakamehi, your work is done. Kakamehi is dispatching the potions and liniments even as you settle in for a well-earned rest. Another day, another job well done.
TEXT_GAIUSC509_00997_SEQ_00: The adventurers of Revenant's Toll have an initiation rite involving smelly seedkin, a proud tradition that only Aganbold appears to know about.
TEXT_GAIUSC509_00997_SEQ_01: Aganbold insists that in order to be recognized as an adventurer at Revenant's Toll, you must pass the test. This is news to you, but since your schedule allows it, go west into the Tangle and slay three morbols.
TEXT_GAIUSC509_00997_SEQ_02: The ill-tempered seedkin are dead and Eorzea is better for it. Speak with Aganbold, who will no doubt be satisfied, and cease holding forth in a manner most theatrical.
TEXT_GAIUSC509_00997_SEQ_03: Your hopes are dashed. If anything, Aganbold grows louder and more florid as he declares that you must now slay the mortal enemy of Revenant's Toll. Lurk at the ambush point and slay this Morbolger when it appears.
TEXT_GAIUSC509_00997_SEQ_04: The Morbolger is dead, as is possibly your sense of smell. Lest your sensory sacrifices be in vain, report your success to Aganbold and bring this trial to an end.
TEXT_GAIUSC509_00997_SEQ_05: Aganbold declares you one of the adventurers of Revenant's Toll, and returns to speaking in a normal tone of voice. Your relief outweighs any suspicion you may entertain that you have been cozened in some way...
TEXT_GAIUSC510_00998_SEQ_00: Looking brighter-eyed than when last you saw her, Guolgeim is ready to do a little moneymaking.
TEXT_GAIUSC510_00998_SEQ_01: The mudpuppy may like its liver right where it is, but the organ is worth a great deal more on the market, where it enjoys a certain reputation with goatish men. Guolgeim bids you slay five mudpuppies in the Fogfens and harvest their livers.
TEXT_GAIUSC510_00998_SEQ_02: You have five livers from five mudpuppies, and the Fogfens is not getting any drier. Squelch back to dry land and present Guolgeim with the organs.
TEXT_GAIUSC510_00998_SEQ_03: Guolgeim gives you a generous payment in return for the mudpuppy livers. Your feet are wet but your purse is heavy, and your heart is lighter for having seen Guolgeim much recovered.
TEXT_GAIUSC511_00999_SEQ_00: Every successful adventurer plays to  strength, and you have some inkling of what Aganbold's might be after a few commissions in his stead.
TEXT_GAIUSC511_00999_SEQ_01: According to the smooth-talking Aganbold, the mare's tail root is a field physick that every adventurer should carry. Since neither he nor you have any on hand, it would be best for you to go west into the Tangle and bring back eight roots.
TEXT_GAIUSC511_00999_SEQ_02: You locate the mare's tail, and harvest eight roots. The flesh has a pleasant, spicy scent to it; you can well believe it would make a soothing concoction, to the senses at least. As for the festering...end your wool-gathering and speak with Aganbold.
TEXT_GAIUSC511_00999_SEQ_03: You deliver the roots to Aganbold and escape further work by declining to take your share of the harvest. Uncharitable it may be, but you suspect that Aganbold has cozened you into performing another commission for him...
TEXT_GAIUSC512_01000_SEQ_00: Guolgeim has a mind to send you to the Garlean crash site to the east.
TEXT_GAIUSC512_01000_SEQ_01: According to Guolgeim, the wreck of the Garlean airship continues to yield small prizes for scavengers such as herself, from time to time. Go southeast and comb the crash site for pieces of airship hull.
TEXT_GAIUSC512_01000_SEQ_02: You collect eight hull fragments, all of good weight. Do as Guolgeim bid and show them to Wandering Breeze over at Saint Coinach's Find.
TEXT_GAIUSC512_01000_SEQ_03: What you found were pieces of Garlean armor plating made of cermet, an alloy unknown to Eorzea─and all but proof against anything she could hurl against it. Report what you learned to Guolgeim.
TEXT_GAIUSC512_01000_SEQ_04: It seems Guolgeim has excellent armor herself, for she is indifferent to the importance of unlocking the secret of the alloy. However, the adventurer is delighted by the prospect of profit, for she is in arrears─and to Wandering Breeze, of all people.
TEXT_GAIUSC607_01007_SEQ_00: Urianger looks beseechingly in your direction, fear in his eyes.
TEXT_GAIUSC607_01007_SEQ_01: Rumors of a primal sighting in the Shroud have Urianger gravely concerned, and he would have you ascertain its identity. First, you are to seek the counsel of Bowlord Lewin.
TEXT_GAIUSC607_01007_SEQ_02: Bowlord Lewin bids you welcome and expresses his gratitude for your aid in the investigation of the primal.
TEXT_GAIUSC608_01008_SEQ_00: Bowlord Lewin would have you ascertain the veracity of the ominous rumors circulating about Gridania of late.
TEXT_GAIUSC608_01008_SEQ_01: Rumors of a ghostly presence in the Shroud have struck fear into the hearts of the Gridanian populace. Speak to the residents to see if there is any credible information to be had.
TEXT_GAIUSC608_01008_SEQ_02: You have succeeded in gathering information from the townspeople. Convey what you have learned to Bowlord Lewin.
TEXT_GAIUSC608_01008_SEQ_03: Bowlord Lewin is grateful for your efforts, but it would appear your findings have put him ill at ease. That which strikes fear into the heart of the Bowlord must be a grave threat indeed.
TEXT_GAIUSC609_01009_SEQ_00: Bowlord Lewin would seek the counsel of others.
TEXT_GAIUSC609_01009_SEQ_01: Bowlord Lewin suspects that the dark horseman is none other than Odin, the Dark Divinity, as told in the ancient scriptures. Travel to Quarrymill and seek counsel from O-App-Pesi.
TEXT_GAIUSC609_01009_SEQ_02: According to Brother O-App-Pesi, the Dark Divinity slumbers within Urth's Fount, where a great Allagan hero confined him in a gaol of crystal. Inspect Urth's Seal to see that the crystal fetters still hold. The cleansing water provided to you should avail you if any malicious spirits take issue with your presence.
TEXT_GAIUSC609_01009_SEQ_03: The wayward soul of the Allagan hero that assailed you has been delivered to eternal rest. You are free to examine Urth's Seal more closely.
TEXT_GAIUSC609_01009_SEQ_04: You have obtained what appears to be a remnant of the crystal that once enfettered the Dark Divinity. Deliver your findings to Brother O-App-Pesi.
TEXT_GAIUSC609_01009_SEQ_05: There can be no more doubt. O-App-Pesi's worst fears have been realized─Odin rides again. Share your findings with Simmie.
TEXT_GAIUSC609_01009_SEQ_06: Simmie thanks you for your aid, and says she will immediately incorporate your findings into the report she is drafting for her superiors.
TEXT_GAIUSC610_01010_SEQ_00: Isarmoix's hunting efforts have proven less than fruitful of late.
TEXT_GAIUSC610_01010_SEQ_01: You have agreed to procure meat on behalf of the hapless hunter Isarmoix. Slay five wild hogs and return with the most succulent slices of boarflesh you can muster.
TEXT_GAIUSC610_01010_SEQ_02: Your hunt was a fruitful one. Deliver the slices of meat to Isarmoix.
TEXT_GAIUSC610_01010_SEQ_03: Thanks to your efforts, Isarmoix's wife and children will feast on the choicest cuts of meat tonight. Isarmoix himself may not be the most skilled of hunters, but his devotion to his family cannot be denied.
TEXT_GAIUSC611_01011_SEQ_00: Kerrich just wants to have some fun.
TEXT_GAIUSC611_01011_SEQ_01: The dread Ser Kerrich, Dark Rider of the Shroud, stands before you. Cower and /kneel before him.
TEXT_GAIUSC611_01011_SEQ_02: The dread Ser Kerrich, Dark Rider of the Shroud, would accept you as his vassal, but first demands that you prove your loyalty by doing his bidding. Fetch the wings from three keds as your master commands.
TEXT_GAIUSC611_01011_SEQ_03: You have procured three ked wings. Deliver them to Ser Kerrich with all speed.
TEXT_GAIUSC611_01011_SEQ_04: Most pleased with your efforts, the dread Ser Kerrich, Dark Rider of the Shroud, invites you to come play with─er, serve him whenever you desire.
TEXT_GAIUSC612_01012_SEQ_00: Simmie would entrust you with a delivery.
TEXT_GAIUSC612_01012_SEQ_01: With your aid, Simmie has completed her report on the ghostly horseman sighted in the Shroud─now identified as the primal Odin. Return to the Waking Sands and deliver a copy of the report to Urianger.
TEXT_GAIUSC612_01012_SEQ_02: After perusing the report, Urianger shares with you his misgivings about the historical accuracy of the scriptures. Casting light upon the events of ages past is a tall task, indeed.
TEXT_GAIUSC702_01014_SEQ_00: Nedrick knows of a place where a skilled adventurer might hone  skills.
TEXT_GAIUSC702_01014_SEQ_01: According to Nedrick, an area known as the Aurum Vale might hold a suitable challenge for an adventurer of your accomplishments. The vale may be found in the southwesterly reaches of the central highlands of Coerthas. Travel there and seek out a man by the name of Willielmus.
TEXT_GAIUSC702_01014_SEQ_02:
Willielmus reluctantly grants you entry to the Aurum Vale. Take up the challenge, but be ever mindful of the lethal fumes within!

※The Aurum Vale can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_GAIUSC703_01015_SEQ_00: Slafswys has a plan that requires an adventurer's aid.
TEXT_GAIUSC703_01015_SEQ_01: Slafswys would carry out a preemptive strike against the kobolds, and would recruit the pirates of Limsa to the cause. Convey her message to Commander Bloeidin at Camp Overlook.
TEXT_GAIUSC703_01015_SEQ_02: Commander Bloeidin expresses his admiration for Slafswys's courage and ingenuity, and appears willing to offer his aid in the operation.
TEXT_GAIUSC705_01017_SEQ_00: Commander Bloeidin has an idea as to how you might win over his men.
TEXT_GAIUSC705_01017_SEQ_01: Commander Bloeidin believes that the former pirates under his command might be swayed to fight the beastmen by offers of fortune and glory. Convey the message to four of the erstwhile buccaneers.
TEXT_GAIUSC705_01017_SEQ_02: As Bloeidin suspected, the prospect of coin and fortune has lit a fire in the belly of his men. Inform the commander of your success.
TEXT_GAIUSC705_01017_SEQ_03: Commander Bloeidin is pleased to see his men stirred to action, and seems most confident that the former pirates will prove a force to be reckoned with in the battle against the kobolds.
TEXT_GAIUSC706_01018_SEQ_00: F'majha wears a sorrowful expression on her face.
TEXT_GAIUSC706_01018_SEQ_01: F'majha grieves for the loss of her Red Swallow comrades who did not return from their mission. Go to the battlefield and retrieve the marks from their bodies, that F'majha might pay them some small tribute.
TEXT_GAIUSC706_01018_SEQ_02: You have retrieved the marks from the bodies of the fallen Swallows. Return them to F'majha.
TEXT_GAIUSC706_01018_SEQ_03: F'majha's tears flow freely as she takes the mementos of her fallen comrades into hand. Drying her eyes, she vows to fight so that their sacrifice will not be in vain.
TEXT_GAIUSC707_01019_SEQ_00: Bloeidin could use your aid in creating a diversion.
TEXT_GAIUSC707_01019_SEQ_01: Bloeidin has a mind to destroy a new crucible that the alchemically inclined kobolds have developed, and has tasked you with creating a diversion. Travel to Iron Lake and use the makeshift bombs provided by the commander to blow up piles of kobold supplies to draw their attention away from the primary target.
TEXT_GAIUSC707_01019_SEQ_02: You have destroyed the kobold supplies as per your orders. Return to Bloeidin and inquire as to the success of the mission.
TEXT_GAIUSC707_01019_SEQ_03: Bloeidin informs you that, thanks in no small part to your efforts, the operation was a success. The loss of their crucible should take the wind out of the kobolds' sails for the foreseeable future.
TEXT_GAIUSC708_01020_SEQ_00: Bloeidin would have you deliver a message.
TEXT_GAIUSC708_01020_SEQ_01: Bloeidin has drafted a full report on the success of Operation Crucible Down, along with a proposition. Deliver the missive to R'ashaht Rhiki at Maelstrom Command.
TEXT_GAIUSC708_01020_SEQ_02: R'ashaht Rhiki is pleased to hear of the operation's success, and promises to negotiate with Command as to Bloeidin's requests. Your task complete, return to the Waking Sands and deliver Bloeidin's regards to Slafswys.
TEXT_GAIUSC708_01020_SEQ_03: Slafswys recounts her past experiences with Bloeidin, and expresses her admiration for Bloeidin's efforts, despite fate having sent the two along separate paths. In any event, the kobold threat to Limsa has been quelled for the foreseeable future.
TEXT_GAIUSC709_01021_SEQ_00: U'odh Nunh wears a brooding expression on his face.
TEXT_GAIUSC709_01021_SEQ_01: U'odh Nunh respects your strength, but is nevertheless reluctant to risk the lives of his tribe to fight the battles of outsiders. Speak to the U tribeswomen and assess their feelings.
TEXT_GAIUSC709_01021_SEQ_02: As expected, the huntresses of the U are less than eager to fight a battle that is not their own. Return to speak with U'odh Nunh.
TEXT_GAIUSC709_01021_SEQ_03: Despite your having followed his wishes, U'odh Nunh dismisses you out of hand. It appears that more pressing matters demand the nunh's attention.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_00: Hab the zombie just wants some love.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_01: Hab is terribly lonely, and longs to be reunited with his erstwhile sabotender friends. One disappeared in the Central Shroud. Track him down on Hab's behalf.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_02: You find Sabotendrick safe and sound in the forest. Return to the Sagolii Desert and share the good news with Hab.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_03: Heartened by your success, Hab would have you seek out his remaining sabotender friends. Hab claims to have lost contact with one while traveling through outer La Noscea.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_04: You have successfully tracked down Sabotendred. Return and inform Hab of your success.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_05: His spirits rising, Hab would have you track down the last of his missing sabotender pals, who he suspects is trapped within a pot stolen by the Amalj'aa and taken to their camp in southern Thanalan. Hab provides you with some firesand to aid in the task.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_06: You have freed Sabotendale from his earthenware gaol. Speak to him.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_07: Sabotendale dashes off, no doubt to return to the desert where Hab and his brothers await. Inform Hab that your job is done.
TEXT_GAIUSC710_01022_SEQ_08: After a brief reunion, Hab's sabotender friends dashed off to return home together. Despite being alone again, Hab is heartened to know that he still has friends in the world.
TEXT_GAIUSC711_01023_SEQ_00: U'odh Nunh has received ill tidings.
TEXT_GAIUSC711_01023_SEQ_01: Three U tribeswomen have been ambushed and taken captive by the Amalj'aa. U'odh Nunh tasks you with delivering ointment to the fallen, that they might be granted the dignity of fighting for their own lives.
TEXT_GAIUSC711_01023_SEQ_02: You have eased the wounds of the captive U tribeswomen. Return and inform U'odh Nunh of your success.
TEXT_GAIUSC711_01023_SEQ_03: His tribe whole once more, U'odh Nunh is overjoyed, and declares you a true friend to the U.
TEXT_GAIUSC712_01024_SEQ_00: U'odh Nunh suspects his tribeswomen may have had a change of heart.
TEXT_GAIUSC712_01024_SEQ_01: U'odh Nunh suspects that your efforts on his tribe's behalf may have convinced the distrustful U to lend their strength to your cause. Speak with the huntresses once more to see if you have indeed earned their trust.
TEXT_GAIUSC712_01024_SEQ_02: The huntresses of the U have expressed a willingness to aid in quelling the beastman threat. Inform U'odh Nunh that his words have proven true.
TEXT_GAIUSC712_01024_SEQ_03: His tribe won over by your deeds, U'odh Nunh formally pledges his aid to your cause. Return to the Waking Sands and inform Wigstan that your diplomatic mission was a success.
TEXT_GAIUSC712_01024_SEQ_04: Heartened by your success and the support of the U tribe, Wigstan has found a new sense of purpose. He vows to devote himself wholeheartedly to the suppression of the beastmen.
TEXT_GAIUSC801_01025_SEQ_00: Radolf would have you lend your assistance to the Maelstrom cause.
TEXT_GAIUSC801_01025_SEQ_01: At the Waking Sands, you learn from Radolf that the Maelstrom has need of the Scions' aid. Speak with Falkbryda at Camp Skull Valley about the need to subdue the Sahagin threat.
