TEXT_HEAVNZ904_01969_SEQ_01: Having revealed to you his obsession for bridges, the self-possessed broom bids you search for what is supposedly the tiniest bridge in the area. According to a little bird he spoke with, the bridge lies along the cliffs to the west.
TEXT_HEAVNZ904_01969_SEQ_02: You have found a tree trunk that is arguably serving as a bridge. Commit the features of this bridge to your memory, that you might describe it to the self-possessed broom.
TEXT_HEAVNZ904_01969_SEQ_03: You have memorized every ilm of the tree trunk. Make your way back to Matoya's Cave and report your discovery to the self-possessed broom.
TEXT_HEAVNZ904_01969_SEQ_04: The self-possessed broom is taken by your description of the tree trunk, and expresses his desire to sweep it one day. In return for your service, he shares with you his knowledge of Matoya's Crystal Eye. Unfortunately, he does not seem to know what his mistress desires...
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_00: Saro Roggo is eager to hear how you fared in your inquiries after Matoya's desires.
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_01: Saro Roggo is disappointed to learn that the brooms did not know what his mistress desires. However, he is not willing to give up. He reveals to you that Matoya secretly has one more broom outside of her cave, and he has reason to believe that it possesses knowledge that the others do not. He bids you speak with the brooms in the cave once more, that you might learn the incantation by which their mysterious fellow may be summoned. Begin by consulting the straightforward broom.
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_02: Though the straightforward broom is unaware of an incantation, he knows the broom you seek. She is apparently his sister, born of the same wood. He recommends you speak with his brothers, who may have chanced to meet her recently. Approach the statuesque broom and ask him what he knows.
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_03: The statuesque broom reveals to you that the incantation is the name of that which is dearest to Matoya. Unfortunately, he does not know what that thing is. He suggests you speak with his brothers in case they have the answer. Seek out the self-possessed broom and ask him what he knows.
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_04: The self-possessed broom is uncertain as to what is dearest to Matoya. However, he seems abundantly confident that she hates Y'shtola above all else. Whether or not you agree, bear your findings back to Saro Roggo and share them with him.
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_05: Saro Roggo is at a loss for what the incantation might be. Desperate as he is, he bids you go to the bridge to the east, where you are to try calling out the names of various things. Use your powers of deduction to ascertain the incantation, and with the chat mode in Say, enter the word to summon the mystery broom at your destination.
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_06: No sooner do you speak the correct incantation than a sweeping noise emanates from nearby. Search the area thoroughly for a broom.
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_07: Peering behind the steps of the bridge, you find the serendipitous broom sweeping away. You are touched to learn that the knowledge it possesses is none other than all of Matoya's memories pertaining to Y'shtola─from the time she first became her pupil, to the time she left to make her own way in the world. Return to Matoya's Cave and report your discovery to Saro Roggo.
TEXT_HEAVNZ905_01970_SEQ_08: You relate to Saro Roggo the details of your encounter with the serendipitous broom. Having exhausted all avenues to learn his mistress's desires, he despairs of ever becoming useful to her.
TEXT_HEAVNZ906_01971_SEQ_00: Saro Roggo is resigned to his fate.
TEXT_HEAVNZ906_01971_SEQ_01: Saro Roggo has resigned himself to reverting to being an ordinary toad, and plans to go back to dwelling in the wetlands outside Matoya's Cave. However, flat-footed opkens lurk near the area and prey upon his kind. Lie in wait at the specified locations and slay three of the creatures, that Saro Roggo need not live in fear.
TEXT_HEAVNZ906_01971_SEQ_02: You have eliminated the opkens. Take word of your success back to Saro Roggo.
TEXT_HEAVNZ906_01971_SEQ_03: Saro Roggo thanks you for making his past and future home safe again. But in spite of his apparent resignation, it is painfully obvious that he is not ready to give up. Use your powers of deduction to ascertain what he desires of you, and perform the appropriate action for him.
TEXT_HEAVNZ906_01971_SEQ_04: Your boisterous cheering has the desired effect, and Saro Roggo regains his determination to please his mistress. He declares that he will ask after her desires directly...right after you soften her up for him.
TEXT_HEAVNZ906_01971_SEQ_05: Following your lead, Saro Roggo approaches his mistress, and begs to know her desires. To his disappointment, however, she replies that she has none, explaining that she is but an old woman awaiting her death. Moved by his devotion, Matoya entrusts to Saro Roggo the task of closing her Crystal Eye when she dies, and then laying the serendipitous broom at her side. You may rest assured in the knowledge that Saro Roggo has finally found a purpose for his existence.
TEXT_HEAVNZ907_01972_SEQ_00: The House Fortemps knight has an urgent letter to deliver, and he's looking right at you.
TEXT_HEAVNZ907_01972_SEQ_01: A knight from House Fortemps has received a letter addressed directly to you, and upon opening it you realize it was sent by none other than Kuplo Kopp. Apparently he and the Moghome moogles have been getting along famously, and they have decided to have a get-together of the Twelveswood and Moghome moogles, to deepen the bond between them. He invites─or rather, demands─your presence at the festivities, saying that a moogle by the name of Mogule awaits your arrival at Moghome. Head to Moghome at the Churning Mists and speak to your excited host when you arrive.
TEXT_HEAVNZ907_01972_SEQ_02: It seems that before the arrival of Kuplo Kopp and the others from the surface, the existence of the Twelveswood moogles was a mystery to most of Moghome. Mogule is quite curious as to why the moogles of the surface and sky are not living together, and decides that it might be best to ask Chieftain Moglin to shed some light on the mystery of their separation.
TEXT_HEAVNZ907_01972_SEQ_03: Chieftain Moglin, being a busy moogle himself, proposes that the answer to the mystery of the moogles' separation wait until the Twelveswood moogles arrive at Moghome. Mogule, amazed at Moglin's insightful decision, heads off to meet the soon-to-be-arriving moogles, and bids you follow him. Meet with Mogule and wait to greet the undoubtedly tired Twelveswood moogles.
TEXT_HEAVNZ907_01972_SEQ_04: You arrive to find Mogule eagerly awaiting the Twelveswood moogles, but despite it being well past the appointed time, there is not a pom-pom in sight. If the moogles aren't at Moghome, then where could they be...?
TEXT_HEAVNZ908_01973_SEQ_00: Mogule is waiting all by himself for the Twelveswood moogles.
TEXT_HEAVNZ908_01973_SEQ_01: Wait as Mogule might, the moogles from the Twelveswood are nowhere to be seen. He is sure that his directions to meet at the floating island among the sea of clouds were perfectly clear. However, it seems he underestimated the vastness of the landmasses above the skies, and also the clarity of his own directions, and after conferring with you realizes it may be possible the Twelveswood moogles wrongly traveled to the Sea of Clouds. Since someone has to stay behind at Moghome should the Twelveswood moogles eventually show up, Mogule bids you go to the Sea of Clouds to look for the missing moogles. Travel to Camp Cloudtop and ask its inhabitants if they know aught of a band of moogles amongst their midst.
TEXT_HEAVNZ908_01973_SEQ_02: After questioning the inhabitants of Camp Cloudtop, you find out that not many besides you have ever actually seen a moogle in the flesh. However, one of the knights tells you of a man named Gildon, who has been going on about “kupo” related nonsense for the past several days. Seek out Gildon near the Rosehouse and see if he has any information that may guide you in your search.
TEXT_HEAVNZ908_01973_SEQ_03: Gildon, grateful that someone is actually taking his rants seriously, says that he heard moogle voices near Ok' Zundu. Ask the Vanu Vanu of that tribe if they have seen anything of the fabled creatures.
TEXT_HEAVNZ908_01973_SEQ_04: After questioning the Vanu Vanu of Ok' Zundu, you learn little of use besides knowledge of the creatures and clouds in the area. However, one of the giant birdlike creatures tells you that a Vanu Vanu by the name of Guna Vanu has said something about whispers flitting amongst the clouds. Speak to Guna Vanu to find out what he knows.
TEXT_HEAVNZ908_01973_SEQ_05: Upon speaking with Guna Vanu, you find that his brother spoke of hearing unfamiliar voices from under a bridge not far from Ok' Zundu. Could these be the errant moogles? Or a troll? Seek out the bridge to find out.
TEXT_HEAVNZ908_01973_SEQ_06: You search under the bridge and find a lost Kupli Kuki from the Twelveswood. Apparently the Twelveswood moogles misinterpreted the letter, as Mogule guessed, and came to the Sea of Clouds─an understandable mistake. Luckily, thanks to your diligent search, the Twelveswood moogles can now proceed on their way to Moghome for plenty of fun mingling.
TEXT_HEAVNZ909_01974_SEQ_00: Kupli Kuki needs someone to look for his lost friends.
TEXT_HEAVNZ909_01974_SEQ_01: Kupli Kuki has asked you to find his two lost companions, who should be wandering around somewhere in the surrounding islands. Start off by looking for the lost moogle near the Gauntlet.
TEXT_HEAVNZ909_01974_SEQ_02: You find the moogle shaken, but unharmed. He informs you that he will return to Kupli Kuki's safe spot under the bridge. Return and bask in their tearful reunion.
TEXT_HEAVNZ909_01974_SEQ_03: Kupli Kuki is overjoyed that he was reunited with his companion, but there still remains one more moogle to be found. Speak with Kupli Kuki again to start your search for the second lost─and possibly frightened─moogle.
TEXT_HEAVNZ910_01975_SEQ_00: Kupli Kuki wants you to help search for the last missing moogle.
TEXT_HEAVNZ910_01975_SEQ_01: Kupli Kuki and the other moogle have resolved to go find their friend, who ran off somewhere to the eastern part of the Sea of Clouds. Meet with Kupli Kuki at Ok' Vundu Vana to join in on this terribly long game of hide-and-seek.
TEXT_HEAVNZ910_01975_SEQ_02: Upon meeting with Kupli Kuki, he tells you that the lost moogle is nowhere in the area, but he also makes a ghastly discovery. On the ground is a kupo nut, one of the several that the moogles brought to share at their meeting in Moghome. You see the rest of the kupo nuts scattered around the area, and Kupli Kuki asks you to collect them in his stead so that he doesn't fall victim to any of the many hungry monsters stalking the area.
TEXT_HEAVNZ910_01975_SEQ_03: You have braved the griffins and other angry beasts and gathered the precious kupo nuts. Return them to Kupli Kuki so their gift to Moghome will not go to waste.
TEXT_HEAVNZ910_01975_SEQ_04: Kupli Kuki is glad that the kupo nuts were recovered intact, but worries for his lost friend. Aid the two moogles in their desperate search for their companion.
TEXT_HEAVNZ911_01976_SEQ_00: Kupli Kuki is wringing his pom-pom trying to figure out where his companion went.
TEXT_HEAVNZ911_01976_SEQ_01: Kupli Kuki uses his powers of deduction to determine that the last possible refuge for his lost moogle friend is to the south. However, since that area is just bound to be overflowing with wild beasts, he asks you to go ahead of the two moogles and look for any evidence of his lost companion before they risk their lives in an effortless search. Search Hengr's Crucible for any signs of the nervous moogle.
TEXT_HEAVNZ911_01976_SEQ_02: You search the area and you find an errant kupo nut and a few feathers that look like they came from a bird of significant size. It would be a shame if a moogle was left alone without his kupo nuts, so return the evidence to Kupli Kuki and see what he has to say about his lost partner.
TEXT_HEAVNZ911_01976_SEQ_03: Kupli Kuki examines the kupo nut and feathers, guessing that the most likely occurrence was that his poor companion was kidnapped by one of the many large birds soaring the skies in the area. Follow him to where the birds build their nests and see if he has any insight as to where the other moogle may be.
TEXT_HEAVNZ911_01976_SEQ_04: You meet up with the two moogles, and the area is teeming with giant birds that match the feathers you found previously. Kupli Kuki asks you to help them search for their friend before one of the birds gets hungry and does something terrible to the moogle.
TEXT_HEAVNZ911_01976_SEQ_05: After searching every nook and cranny of the area, you find the moogle cowering in a nest, apparently in an attempt to blend in with the many eggs. He is relieved that he was able to avoid becoming fodder for the birds, and returns to reunite with his Twelveswood companions.
TEXT_HEAVNZ911_01976_SEQ_06: All three moogles have been reunited at last, and they can finally move on from this confusing episode to meet their moogle brethren in Moghome. Aid them in their journey to the Churning Mists for what is sure to be a party to remember.
TEXT_HEAVNZ912_01977_SEQ_00: Kupli Kuki and his band of merry moogles are finally ready to journey to Moghome.
TEXT_HEAVNZ912_01977_SEQ_01: With the band of Twelveswood moogles finally reunited, Kupli Kuki decides to set off towards Moghome at last. He assures you that this time, they will not get lost along the way. Return to Mogule at Moghome to make sure that Kupli Kuki is as good as his word.
TEXT_HEAVNZ912_01977_SEQ_02: Mogule, Kupli Kuki, and the other Twelveswood moogles meet at last, with happy pom-poms all around. When Kupli Kuki presents his offering of kupo nuts to Mogule, they make a surprising discovery: they are exactly the same kupo nuts as the ones that are grown in Moghome. The moogles have more in common than they thought, and decide to go ask Chieftain Moglin for any information he might have that would shed light on this uncommon coincidence.
TEXT_HEAVNZ912_01977_SEQ_03: Chieftain Moglin regales you and the others with the tale of Moghome's ancestors, who were said to have descended to the surface after a disaster destroyed their once spacious home. Afterwards, Kupli Kuki relates a similar story that tells of moogles that left for the surface after the gods in the heavens started squabbling. The moogles surmise that these two stories must be telling the same occurrence in different ways, and are overjoyed to find that once the moogles of the sky and surface lived happily together. They are eager to deepen their bonds even further─be ready to get involved in all kinds of moogle mayhem.
TEXT_HEAVNZ913_01978_SEQ_00: Kupli Kuki is thinking about the Moghome moogles.
TEXT_HEAVNZ913_01978_SEQ_01: Everyone is excited to deepen the bonds between mooglekind, but Kupli Kuki wants to know more about the names of the Moghome moogles, in particular why every name starts with “Mog” and not something like “Kup.” Since Kupli Kuki seems to be particularly shy around moogles of high social standing, he enlists your aid in asking Chieftain Moglin the reason as to why the moogles from the sky and surface have different names. Ask Chieftain Moglin for what is sure to be a thrilling history lesson on the origins of Moghome names.
TEXT_HEAVNZ913_01978_SEQ_02: You speak with Chieftain Moglin, and he seems eager to tell you about the names of Moghome, but not before you help the Pomguard with a pair of monsters who have suddenly attacked Moghome's kupo nut supply. Speak with Mogleo of the Pomguard to find out what aid he requires.
TEXT_HEAVNZ913_01978_SEQ_03: Mogleo tells you that two monsters have dared to steal into Moghome's precious kupo nut supply, and asks you to aid Mogule, Kupli Kuki, and the other Twelveswood moogles in slaying the monster they have gone after. Speak with the four moogles to find out where this insatiable monster could be.
TEXT_HEAVNZ913_01978_SEQ_04: Mogule and the other valiant Twelveswood moogles have cornered the invasive monster to the southeast. Slay it so that Moghome's nuts are in danger no more.
TEXT_HEAVNZ913_01978_SEQ_05: You find that a stray gaelicat was one of the monsters trying to get its paws on the moogles' kupo nuts, and slay it before it can do any more harm to the precious nut orchard. Report back to Mogleo for an update on their progress.
TEXT_HEAVNZ913_01978_SEQ_06: Mogleo and the other Pomguard members were able to take care of their target as well, and with that the kupo nuts are saved. It seems that the two monsters may have followed Kupli Kuki and the other Twelveswood moogles all the way from the Sea of Clouds. Although this crisis got everyone's pom-pom in a twist, the moogles seem to have come through it with a deeper bond, and Mogleo suggests that everyone go together to report to Chieftain Moglin of your success.
TEXT_HEAVNZ913_01978_SEQ_07: You return to Moglin, and finally you have the opportunity to ask him about the Moghome names. While he doesn't know the exact reason that all the moogles in Moghome start with “Mog,” he informs you that the first chieftain was said to be named Moggle. Kupli Kuki fumbles around with the name for a bit before discovering that it is quite similar to Moggle Mog, and surmises that the name must have changed as the story was passed down from generation to generation in the Twelveswood. If Kupli Kuki's guess is right, then Chieftain Moglin is himself a direct descendant of Good King Moggle Mog XII, and the Pomguard are direct descendants of the Good King's household guard. Kupli Kuki is amazed that he is among such historic figures of mooglekind, although the Moghome moogles themselves do not seem very fazed at all. Mogleo finally closes this historic conversation by offering the Twelveswood moogles one kupo nut each for their previous bravery, an offer which the moogles eagerly agree to. The moogles look forward to deepening the bonds of friendship between sky and surface.
TEXT_HEAVNZ914_01979_SEQ_00: The Allagan training node is silently awaiting user interaction.
TEXT_HEAVNZ914_01979_SEQ_01: Mistaking you for an Allagan soldier, the training node instructs you to locate and defeat five snapper-rooks as part of standard daily Allagan military training.
TEXT_HEAVNZ914_01979_SEQ_02: You have destroyed the snapper-rooks as instructed. Notify the training node that you have completed the assigned task.
TEXT_HEAVNZ914_01979_SEQ_03: The training node explains to you the importance of the task it set you, but the message is so distorted by static that you fail to discern what it is trying to tell you.
TEXT_HEAVNZ915_01980_SEQ_00: The Allagan sterilization node is silently awaiting user interaction.
TEXT_HEAVNZ915_01980_SEQ_01: The Allagan sterilization node informs you that the facility has lost its control link with five of its cleaning units─clockwork harvestmen. These units are out of control and hazardous. Destroy them.
TEXT_HEAVNZ915_01980_SEQ_02: You destroy the malfunctioning equipment. Update the sterilization node with this new information.
TEXT_HEAVNZ915_01980_SEQ_03: With the non-responsive harvestmen dismantled, the sterilization node can resume its work, but you learn that the system is massively overdue for replacement. Unfortunately, there is nothing you can do about this.
TEXT_HEAVNZ916_01981_SEQ_00: The Allagan safeguard node is flickering erratically.
TEXT_HEAVNZ916_01981_SEQ_01: With a torrent of warnings and alerts, the Allagan safeguard node informs you that an enforcement droid is out of control and must be decommissioned. Find this technological terror and destroy it.
TEXT_HEAVNZ916_01981_SEQ_02: You deal with the out-of-control enforcement droid. Update the safeguard node with this information.
TEXT_HEAVNZ916_01981_SEQ_03: The safeguard node confirms that the enforcement droid is no longer a threat, and hints that a similar event occurred in the past─with horrifying consequences.
TEXT_HEAVNZ917_01982_SEQ_00: The Allagan suppression node is attempting to initialize a system test.
TEXT_HEAVNZ917_01982_SEQ_01: The Allagan suppression node needs to confirm the effectiveness of its citizen compliance assurance subsystem. Put the subsystem through its paces by attempting to destroy three clockwork engineers and three clockwork paladins.
TEXT_HEAVNZ917_01982_SEQ_02: The test has been completed. Return to the suppression node to confirm the results.
TEXT_HEAVNZ917_01982_SEQ_03: The suppression node seems to view your survival as a failure of the subsystem and recommends an upgrade of the infrastructure.
TEXT_HEAVNZ918_01983_SEQ_00: The Allagan research node is silently awaiting user interaction.
TEXT_HEAVNZ918_01983_SEQ_01: You learn that a number of rapidly reproducing, monstrous chimeras have escaped from an Allagan research facility. The research node explains that they pose a severe threat to the local environment and must be immediately terminated. Slay two Allagan chimeras.
TEXT_HEAVNZ918_01983_SEQ_02: You have slain the horrifying abominations. Inform the research node that the immediate risk to the environment has been ameliorated.
TEXT_HEAVNZ918_01983_SEQ_03: The research node acknowledges your work and confirms that the threat to the environment has been mitigated. You learn that all attempts at creating composite life-forms have resulted in dangerous and psychologically unstable creatures, but it does not seem that the Allagan research node has any intention of putting limitations on its research.
TEXT_HEAVNZ919_01984_SEQ_00: The Allagan life support node's status light is blinking an ominous red...
TEXT_HEAVNZ919_01984_SEQ_01: The Allagan life support node informs you that atmospheric levels of corpse flower spores are at critically dangerous levels─and rising. Destroy corpse flowers to reduce the release of these apparently dangerous pollutants.
TEXT_HEAVNZ919_01984_SEQ_02: You extirpate the troublesome corpse flowers. Return to the life support node to confirm that there are no other sources of dangerous atmospheric contaminants.
TEXT_HEAVNZ919_01984_SEQ_03: With the reduced rate of spore output, the life support system is now able to purify the air faster than it is being polluted. The abnormally high corpse flower population seems to have been caused by an airborne growth stimulation medium released from the ecological synthesis research facility.
TEXT_HEAVNZ920_01985_SEQ_00: The Allagan tracking node is awaiting user interaction.
TEXT_HEAVNZ920_01985_SEQ_01: The Allagan tracking node appears to be conducting some sort of training program and has challenged you to hunt down four empuses.
TEXT_HEAVNZ920_01985_SEQ_02: You hunt down the empuses as instructed. Return to the tracking node for your performance evaluation.
TEXT_HEAVNZ920_01985_SEQ_03: It seems the tracking node is unable to complete its training program. Given next week's hunting target, that may very well be for the best...
TEXT_HEAVNZ921_01986_SEQ_00: The Allagan expulsion node appears panicked and agitated...for a floating cube.
TEXT_HEAVNZ921_01986_SEQ_01: The expulsion node has identified the nearby Garlean troops as an invading enemy force. It requests that each soldier in the defending Allagan army kill eight of the Garlean soldiers. This appears to include you!
TEXT_HEAVNZ921_01986_SEQ_02: Return to the expulsion node and inform it that you have slain your fair share of Garleans.
TEXT_HEAVNZ921_01986_SEQ_03: The expulsion node tells you about a previous insurrection attempt that occurred roughly five thousand years ago. It seems that the various automated systems here have been watching over Azys Lla for a very, very long time.
TEXT_HEAVNZ922_01987_SEQ_00: The Allagan logistics node is spinning frantically.
TEXT_HEAVNZ922_01987_SEQ_01: The Allagan logistics node informs you that several freight-handling units never received deactivation commands and have been operating continuously for over five thousand years. Lacking the ability to remotely deactivate these units itself, the logistics node authorizes you to do so in its stead. Find and deactivate four adamantite claws.
TEXT_HEAVNZ922_01987_SEQ_02: You have successfully destroyed the adamantite claws. Report your success to the logistics node.
TEXT_HEAVNZ922_01987_SEQ_03: The logistics node reminds you that you were asked to deactivate the non-responsive units, not destroy them. In light of your crimes, it immediately rescinds the authorization it previously granted.
TEXT_HEAVNZ923_01988_SEQ_00: The Allagan auditing node is quietly clicking, buzzing, and whirring.
TEXT_HEAVNZ923_01988_SEQ_01: The Allagan auditing node has detected several unregistered items nearby and has asked you to retrieve them so that they can be tested. Gather five cermet containers so that they may be audited.
TEXT_HEAVNZ923_01988_SEQ_02: You have retrieved the cermet containers. Take them back to the auditing node for testing.
TEXT_HEAVNZ923_01988_SEQ_03: The auditing node has examined the containers and determined that they contain Garlean replicas of Allagan technology. The worrying nature of this revelation is somewhat offset by the fact that they seem to be very poor facsimiles of the originals.
TEXT_HEAVNZ924_01989_SEQ_00: The Allagan assembly node is jittering impatiently.
TEXT_HEAVNZ924_01989_SEQ_01: The Allagan assembly node has run out of raw materials to continue its work. Due to the lack of resources, it has asked you to destroy three steel giants so that they may be recycled and the parts used in this system's manufacturing process.
TEXT_HEAVNZ924_01989_SEQ_02: You destroy the steel giants as required. Inform the assembly node that they are ready for reclamation.
TEXT_HEAVNZ924_01989_SEQ_03: The assembly node confirms your decommissioning of the steel giants but is unable to identify any parts suitable for salvage and soon returns to repeating the same statements it was announcing upon your approach.
TEXT_HEAVNZ925_01990_SEQ_00: The Allagan restrainment node is gently glowing and spinning.
TEXT_HEAVNZ925_01990_SEQ_01: The Allagan restrainment node informs you that several Dravanian test subjects have escaped from their restraints and now roam the area unchecked. The system asks you to kill three Meracydian dragons and three Meracydian falaks to mitigate the risk these dangerous creatures pose.
TEXT_HEAVNZ925_01990_SEQ_02: You slay the beasts as instructed by the restrainment node. Report to the system with notice of the completion of your mission.
TEXT_HEAVNZ925_01990_SEQ_03: The restrainment node thanks you for your hard work and identifies the cause of the containment breach as a weakening of the dragons' restraints over time. It lodges a report recommending that the research facility use more durable equipment that can last more than just a few thousand years without becoming ineffective.
TEXT_HEAVNZ926_01991_SEQ_00: The Allagan administrative node's warning lights are flashing.
TEXT_HEAVNZ926_01991_SEQ_01: The Allagan administrative node informs you that a large number of unidentified dragons have been detected nearby. These creatures pose a severe risk to the native fauna. It asks you to alleviate this risk by slaying four of the things.
TEXT_HEAVNZ926_01991_SEQ_02: You kill the beasts as instructed by the administrative node. Report your success to the system so that it may reevaluate the situation.
TEXT_HEAVNZ926_01991_SEQ_03: The administrative node indicates that although you have reduced the dragon population somewhat, their rate of reproduction is too high for this to be a viable long-term solution. The entire population of dragons must be eliminated to prevent further risk to the environment.
TEXT_HEAVNZ927_01992_SEQ_00: The Allagan enhancement node appears agitated.
TEXT_HEAVNZ927_01992_SEQ_01: The Allagan enhancement node informs you that several dragons have escaped from an experiment. It asks you to kill all three of these enhanced predators to negate the extreme risk they pose.
TEXT_HEAVNZ927_01992_SEQ_02: You eliminate the escaped specimens. All that is left is to inform the enhancement node.
TEXT_HEAVNZ927_01992_SEQ_03: The enhancement node thanks you for dealing with the dragons, explaining that it will review this incident and attempt to prevent its recurrence.
TEXT_HEAVNY801_02095_SEQ_00: Morgayne is curious whether a talented individual like yourself is familiar with the latest fad.
TEXT_HEAVNY801_02095_SEQ_01: Apparently, there is a new “collectables” fad, which a  with your talent stands to benefit from, should you choose to do so. Journey to Revenant's Toll and speak with Lydirlona to learn more.
TEXT_HEAVNY801_02095_SEQ_02: The realm is filled with wealthy individuals who covet a great many things, yet have no intention of obtaining them themselves. They turn to Rowena's House of Splendors to supply them with the objects of their desire, and the consortium employs various tradesmen to procure the collectables in question. Such an opportunity is now available to you, should you be so inclined...and willing to receive payment in the form of scrips redeemable only with the House of Splendors.
TEXT_HEAVNY802_02096_SEQ_00: Lydirlona thinks you might benefit from becoming a specialist.
TEXT_HEAVNY802_02096_SEQ_01: Judging you to be a rather skilled crafts, Lydirlona suggests that it might be in your best interests to become a specialist. She instructs you to seek out Alderan, a master craftsman in Ishgard, and present to him her letter that he might show you the way.
TEXT_HEAVNY802_02096_SEQ_02: Intrigued by Lydirlona's endorsement, Alderan tells you that it is only right that those with talent learn every trade. However, even masters must come to terms with their limitations, for one can specialize in no more than three disciplines. He gives you a Soul of the Crafter and bids you decide which trades are most important to you. When you have reached a decision, he will be waiting to guide you on your new journey.
TEXT_HEAVNY803_02097_SEQ_00: Lydirlona has a proposition for one as accomplished as you.
TEXT_HEAVNY803_02097_SEQ_01: Lydirlona thinks you would benefit from learning about aetherial reduction. Though she lacks the knowledge to explain in detail, she knows who can: Kokosamu, one of Master Mutamix's many disciples. Seek him out at the Bonfire in central Thanalan to receive your education.
TEXT_HEAVNY803_02097_SEQ_02: Aetherial reduction turns out to be a rather simple process in which one breaks down items into their base aetherial components, such as crystals or other rare materials. However, it would seem that only rare items considered collectables are suitable for this purpose, so whether or not it will prove useful remains to be seen...
TEXT_HEAVNY804_02098_SEQ_00: Lydirlona would like to reassure you that the rumors you have heard are true.
TEXT_HEAVNY804_02098_SEQ_01: Rowena's House of Splendors has expanded its operations and established an outpost in Idyllshire, far to the west in the Dravanian hinterlands. Should you find yourself passing through, Lydirlona thinks it would be prudent for you to make yourself known to the representatives there. Present her letter of introduction to Geimlona, her older sister, in Idyllshire.
TEXT_HEAVNY804_02098_SEQ_02: With the help of you and your fellow suppliers, Geimlona and her comrades aim to become the premier source of collectables in the region. As was the case in Mor Dhona, you will be duly compensated for your contributions...in scrips issued by the House of Splendors, that is.
TEXT_HEAVNR191_02108_SEQ_00: The wandering minstrel wishes to hear all about how you raged against the machine.
TEXT_HEAVNR191_02108_SEQ_01: Inspired by your battle against the colossus, the minstrel launches into song once more, portraying your trials and tribulations in the Dravanian hinterlands in predictably hyperbolic fashion. Make your way along the shores of the Thaliak and discuss your recollections of the event with Redbrix.
TEXT_HEAVNR191_02108_SEQ_02:
Whether it be through the gift of the Echo, the power of the poet's verse, or a combination of the two, it would seem that you can now relive your exploration of Gordias. Though you are generally loath to look back, it is not impossible that stepping into the past may be of benefit to you in the future.

※Gordias (Savage) may be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_HEAVNY001_02111_SEQ_00: The dead care not for justice, but Wealdtheow would see them have it just the same.
TEXT_HEAVNY001_02111_SEQ_01: Recognizing you as the honored ward of House Fortemps, Wealdtheow implores you to enter the ruins of the Dusk Vigil and reclaim a priceless treasure: an ice rondel set in the helm of a sculpture within the Vigil's chapel. Though the Vigil has remained abandoned since it fell, knights now stand watch to deter scavengers. You will need to identify yourself before you can enter.
TEXT_HEAVNY001_02111_SEQ_02:
The knight grants you leave to enter, but not before warning you that wild beasts and worse infest the ruins. The recent sighting of a massive winged creature gives you pause as well... Nevertheless, an agreement was made. Wealdtheow will have his stone.

※The Dusk Vigil can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_HEAVNY001_02111_SEQ_03: In the days following the Calamity, western Coerthas was abandoned by the knights of Ishgard, save for the Dusk Vigil, whose defenders refused to withdraw. Their tragic sacrifice is a tale known to many...but only those who have ventured within the ruins know what truly became of those brave men and women. As you hold the ice rondel in your hand, you consider how much you might share─and how much you might keep to yourself.
TEXT_HEAVNY001_02111_SEQ_04: Was it for duty, honor, or faith that Ser Yuhelmeric refused to yield the Dusk Vigil, even though he knew it would cost the lives of him and his knights? Or perhaps something else entirely─a sapphire, perhaps, one of many precious things stolen from his family by the inquisition. Wealdtheow knows that his family can never be made whole again, but for his son and the wife he left behind, at least this injustice can be righted.
TEXT_HEAVNY002_02112_SEQ_00: Sanu Vanu would seek your aid in asserting the authority of the Zundu chieftain.
TEXT_HEAVNY002_02112_SEQ_01: Sanu Vanu seeks to procure the necessary materials for a new tribal mask─the traditional symbol of authority for a Vanu Vanu chieftain─that the kindly Zundu might continue to assert their independence from their warlike brethren. Complicating matters is the fact that the waukkeon, the giant breed of sanuwa from which the masks are fashioned, resides only on Neverreap, the sacred island which has been seized by the Vundu. Make your way outside the village and speak with Tonu Vanu, who will serve as your guide.
TEXT_HEAVNY002_02112_SEQ_02:
Tonu Vanu welcomes your aid and offers to guide you to Neverreap, while giving you fair warning that it has been transformed into a tempest of terrors under the watch of the vicious Vundu. Brave the dangers of the sacred isle and claim a waukkeon scale for the beleaguered Zundu.

※Neverreap can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_HEAVNY002_02112_SEQ_03: You have braved the vicious storms of Neverreap and emerged victorious, with a mighty waukkeon scale to show for your efforts. Return to Ok' Zundu and deliver it to Sanu Vanu, who will surely rejoice in your triumph.
TEXT_HEAVNY002_02112_SEQ_04: Sanu Vanu is overjoyed to receive the scale, which will allow his chief to reassert his authority and serve to shelter his harried tribe from the threat of the Vundu. He gives you his gratitude, expressing a hope that netherlings and the Zundu can continue to live in friendship and harmony for years to come.
TEXT_HEAVNY003_02113_SEQ_00: Notrelchamps has a message for you from an old friend.
TEXT_HEAVNY003_02113_SEQ_01: Notrelchamps informs you that your erstwhile companion Wedge is looking for you to assist in some top secret project of the utmost urgency. Seek the small fellow out at the Aetherochemical Research Facility in Azys Lla and see what could possibly be so important.
TEXT_HEAVNY003_02113_SEQ_02: You meet Wedge at the Aetherochemical Research Facility, where he reveals the nature of his project. The ever-emotional youth seeks to restore life to “Gilly,” the helpful guidance node who showed you about in your travels through Azys Lla. To that end, he entreats you to travel to the Fractal Continuum─a museum of Allagan technology housed inside a decommissioned warship─and come back with a new node nacelle, into which Gilly's “heart” might be transferred. Venture to Matter Conduit VI-VII and access the teleporter there.
TEXT_HEAVNY003_02113_SEQ_03:
You successfully locate the teleporter that will grant you access to the Fractal Continuum, which issues you a warning regarding security clearance and anti-intruder systems that bodes ill for your impending visit. Ignore it and brave whatever awaits within, that Gilly might live on.

※The Fractal Continuum can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_HEAVNY003_02113_SEQ_04: You have triumphed over the chimerical horrors that inhabited the Fractal Continuum to emerge with a top-of-the-line nacelle that will serve as a new body for Wedge's favorite guidance node. Take pride in the fact that you've done right by Gilly, and deliver the nacelle to the Lalafellin engineer back at the Aetherochemical Research Facility.
TEXT_HEAVNY003_02113_SEQ_05: Gilly's new body works like a charm, and Wedge rejoices at being reunited with his friend. He then entrusts the guidance node to you, that she might accompany you on your adventures and see that there is more to the world than the aetheric wastes she has known for the past five thousand years. Go forth with your loyal new accompaniment node at your side!
TEXT_HEAVNY809_02118_SEQ_00: Your reputation precedes you, if the wide-eyed look the stranger is favoring you with is any indication.
TEXT_HEAVNY809_02118_SEQ_01: While passing through Idyllshire you find yourself accosted by a boisterous stranger, who marks you as a notorious adventurer prone to picking fights with gods. Though he claims to admire your “work,” he observes that, because you do not undertake such trials by yourself, it must be difficult to tell if you are pulling your weight. He too has such worries, which is why he has been training in Stone, Sky, Sea─a new training ground of some repute, of which a goodly adventurer outside Idyllshire can tell you more.
TEXT_HEAVNY809_02118_SEQ_02: Although he stumbles more than a few times in his explanation, the guide tells you that the new training ground, which was opened by the Adventurers' Guild, offers a variety of striking dummies which are tailored to the strength of certain legendary beings. By defeating these dummies in the allotted time, you can determine whether or not you have the potential to go toe-to-toe with said beings─that is, if you can survive their onslaught, for unlike their real-life counterparts, the dummies do not hit back...
TEXT_HEAVNY810_02119_SEQ_00: Aytienne is looking you up and down and grinning.
TEXT_HEAVNY810_02119_SEQ_01: Recognizing you as an adventurer who has seen  fair share of battle, Aytienne asks if you would consider joining him and his Clan Centurio colleagues in the Ishgardian Hunt. If you think you have what it takes, head to the bar of the Forgotten Knight and ask Ardolain for more information.
TEXT_HEAVNY810_02119_SEQ_02: Ardolain briefs you on the workings of the Clan Hunt and signs you up as a Clan Centurio novitiate. He bids you examine the Clan Hunt board outside the upstairs entrance to the inn, where Clan Centurio post their latest marks.
TEXT_HEAVNY810_02119_SEQ_03: You examine the Clan Hunt board and the bills posted thereon. As a novice member of Clan Centurio, you are permitted to take level one mark bills from the board and collect their rewards. For more information about the Clan Hunt, or to exchange Centurio Seals for exclusive items, speak with Ardolain in the Forgotten Knight. Otherwise, pick a bill from the board and put the marked monsters to the sword to help bring a modicum of peace to the bloodstained snows of Ishgard.
TEXT_HEAVNY811_02120_SEQ_00: Eustacia thinks you are ready to hit new heights in your hunting career.
TEXT_HEAVNY811_02120_SEQ_01: Eustacia is impressed by the fire in your eyes and the thew of your thighs, and suggests that you are more than ready to take on new challenges in the Clan Hunt. She bids you speak with Ardolain, keeper of the Clan Centurio records in the Forgotten Knight, and ask his permission to hunt more dangerous marks.
TEXT_HEAVNY811_02120_SEQ_02: Ardolain assents to Eustacia's proposal, and permits you to take second-level bills from the Clan Hunt board. Return to the board to peruse the marks, and the rewards, available.
TEXT_HEAVNY811_02120_SEQ_03: You examine the Clan Hunt board, and the level two bills posted thereon. For more information about the Clan Hunt, or to exchange Centurio Seals for exclusive items, speak with Ardolain in the Forgotten Knight. Otherwise, a whole new category of baneful beasts await their destruction at the hands of a freshly promoted hunts.
TEXT_HEAVNY812_02121_SEQ_00: Yloise is eager for you to rise through the ranks in Clan Centurio.
TEXT_HEAVNY812_02121_SEQ_01: Yloise is pleased to meet the adventurer whose heroics have been the subject of much discussion in Clan Centurio, but is dismayed that as yet you have only been permitted to hunt mid-level marks. She instructs you to return to the Forgotten Knight, and demand that Ardolain allow you access to a higher tier of hunting.
TEXT_HEAVNY812_02121_SEQ_02: Ardolain defers to Yloise's judgment, and allows you access to more advanced marks. He suggests that you peruse the Clan Hunt board to examine the targets Clan Centurio reserve for their more advanced hunters.
TEXT_HEAVNY812_02121_SEQ_03: You examine the Clan Hunt board, and the level three bills posted thereon. For more information about the Clan Hunt, or to exchange Centurio Seals for exclusive items, speak with Ardolain in the Forgotten Knight. Otherwise, it is time to test your mettle against some of the most ferocious fiends that threaten the denizens of the north.
TEXT_HEAVNY813_02122_SEQ_00: Ardolain has some good news for you from the master of Clan Centurio.
TEXT_HEAVNY813_02122_SEQ_01: Ardolain informs you that the leader of Clan Centurio has recommended that you be accepted as a fully fledged hunter, with permission to undertake hunts for elite marks. He bids you return to the Clan Hunt board to examine the elite mark bills posted thereon.
TEXT_HEAVNY813_02122_SEQ_02: You examine the Clan Hunt board and flick through the bills available. For more information about the Clan Hunt, or to exchange Centurio Seals for exclusive items, speak with Ardolain in the Forgotten Knight. Otherwise, you are free to risk life and limb hunting down the most malicious monsters in the frozen north and make a name for yourself as an elite mark hunter.
TEXT_CHREND101_02152_SEQ_00: Mathye sighs as he looks around for customers.
TEXT_CHREND101_02152_SEQ_01: Mathye explains to you that business has not been going so well after the recent turmoil in the church. He mentions that his best customers, the students of the scholasticate, are often being followed back to the cathedral by disagreeable folk, and less are inclined to walk around in the open, including to the Crozier. In an effort to keep coin flowing, Mathye requests you to make a round near the road to the cathedral and put an end to any harassment you may see.
TEXT_CHREND101_02152_SEQ_02: You soon spot an altercation between a group of angry paupers and students clad in scholasticate robes. The encounter escalates when the resentful ruffians make off with a tome of one of the students, Theomocent. The mousy-looking seminarian runs after them to retrieve it, and his friend asks you to pursue him for fear of his safety.
TEXT_CHREND101_02152_SEQ_03: You find Theomocent out of breath in a dark alcove, outnumbered by a group of aggrieved Brume residents. The student recognizes their ringleader, “Ben,” as an acquaintance from childhood, and pleads with him to return the book. However, Ben grows angry with the unexpected reunion and holds Theomocent's book over a brazier, intending to destroy it out of spite. Lamenting he was not able to leave his unfortunate circumstances for the scholasticate as Theomocent had, he is soon caught off guard by Leigh, another lowborn student. Leigh attempts to save the book after Ben casts it into the flames and escapes, but he is too late in his attempt to rescue it unscathed. He returns the charred tome to a relieved Theomocent, and the two express their gratitude to you before heading back to the scholasticate.
TEXT_CHREND101_02152_SEQ_04: You return to the Jeweled Crozier to find Mathye speaking with a woman of the cloth, and he expresses satisfaction that his business interactions will return to normal with your good deed. He introduces you to Gaetelle of Saint Endalim's Scholasticate, and the clergywoman recognizes you as the adventurer who brought about the revelation of inconsistencies in the teachings. She explains the scholasticate's precarious situation in the aftermath, and how the students have become targets for the public's ire. Impressed by your goodwill towards the students, she asks that you visit the scholasticate for an opportunity to meet with the headmistress.
TEXT_CHREND102_02153_SEQ_00: Gaetelle looks at you with bright eyes.
TEXT_CHREND102_02153_SEQ_01: Gaetelle expresses hope that you will come visit the scholasticate. She bids you and Mathye farewell before taking her leave to return to the cathedral.
TEXT_CHREND102_02153_SEQ_02: Upon approaching the scholasticate, the lector standing at the doors recognizes you, mentioning that Gaetelle was hopeful you would come and visit. Pass through and seek her out.
TEXT_CHREND102_02153_SEQ_03: You enter the humble seminary and speak with Gaetelle about meeting with the headmistress, only to find that she is absent. Instead, Bruvagnon introduces himself as the deputy headmaster, before you are interrupted by none other than Consulting Inspector Briardien, his nephew. The good inspector has been summoned to investigate the theft of the new head of the statue of Saint Valeroyant. For old times' sake, Briardien asks Bruvagnon if you can accompany him as his associate in the case. Bruvagnon seems reluctant for you to be “associated” with the scholasticate, but eventually acquiesces. Join Briardien in his search for the student responsible for supervising the statue work.
TEXT_CHREND102_02153_SEQ_04: The student overseeing the statue's restoration happens to be Theomocent, the student whom you rescued in the Brume. After being questioned by Briardien, he grows skittish and abruptly takes his leave to search for the missing piece on his own. Judging his conduct to be odd, Briardien concludes that the boy is hiding something. While he conducts his own investigation in the Brume, he asks that you search Saint Valeroyant's Forum in Foundation for anyone suspicious, as he believes the thief may be drawn to the broken statue.
TEXT_CHREND102_02153_SEQ_05: In the forum, you find Theomocent pleading with Ben to return the crate containing the head of the statue. In response, Ben angrily accuses Theomocent of accepting the lies of the Holy See in order to have a better life. Leigh soon appears and realizing he is outnumbered, Ben yields the crate and escapes. However, Theomocent seems distraught as he ponders the words of his childhood friend. But he is soon inspired by your courage, and resolves to do his part to redeem the teachings of Halone. The two boys take their leave to return to the scholasticate with the crate.
TEXT_CHREND102_02153_SEQ_06: You return to the scholasticate and see Theomocent and Leigh, who have already returned the statue piece and explained what happened, leaving out the details of who had stolen it. Briardien asks after the culprit, but before you can reply, one of the highborn students, Archombadin, interrupts, claiming to have witnessed Theomocent and Leigh conspiring with another lowborn friend to steal the statue piece and return it to curry favor. Leigh denies the accusation, asserting that you were there and can vouch for their innocence, but Bruvagnon dismisses the students, putting an end to the discussion.
TEXT_CHREND102_02153_SEQ_07: Bruvagnon commends your assistance in resolving the incident and allows you to further accompany Briardien in his work in the scholasticate. However, pointing out the basic level of investigative skill that was necessary to resolve the incident, the inspector remarks that the theft was merely a way to present a more serious problem. He asks his uncle to explain the real reason why his services were requested.
TEXT_CHREND103_02154_SEQ_00: Bruvagnon is ready to say what is really on his mind.
TEXT_CHREND103_02154_SEQ_01: Bruvagnon explains to you that those who strive for a favorable position within the Holy See must first graduate from the scholasticate with the highest marks─as one of the Trinity, or the top three seats which receive a formal endorsement. However, due to the revelations regarding Ishgard's history, both the curriculum and the traditional means of assessment are currently being reevaluated. Without a clear path to the Trinity, the students have grown disillusioned and angry, with some lashing out at their peers.
TEXT_CHREND103_02154_SEQ_02: You meet with Headmistress Elviane and the other clergy of the scholasticate, who relay to you and Briardien their wealth of concerns. While they acknowledge that the uncertainty regarding the rankings is partially to blame, they posit it is but part of a larger problem─a fundamental crisis of faith. That being said, the headmistress and her administrators are quite concerned that some students may attempt to manipulate the interim evaluation system to their advantage. Therefore, the administration would have you and Briardien remain vigilant for any unscrupulous behavior that they might conduct a fair and equitable assessment of the graduating seniors.
TEXT_CHREND103_02154_SEQ_03: After the meeting with the headmistress, the soft-spoken clergyman introduces himself as Saturnois, a scholasticate instructor who often interacts with the underprivileged students of the seminary. Briardien surmises that it would be prudent to learn more about the students and their aspirations. Gaetelle and Saturnois suggest getting to know the students yourself, as they behave differently in the presence of their instructors. Gaetelle recommends starting with the dormitory prefect, Archombadin de Dzemael.
TEXT_CHREND103_02154_SEQ_04: You speak with Archombadin de Dzemael and Lebrassoir de Bonfaurt, who express their opinions on the current turmoil in the Holy See, as well as their hope that the students of the scholasticate will rein in their impulses towards reformation. During your discussion, Archombadin mentions that Gaetelle has given them the task of guiding truant students back to their studies, and Briardien suspects others are doing the same.
TEXT_CHREND103_02154_SEQ_05: In your search for other students, you come across Theomocent and Leigh, who intend to go to Foundation to coax their friends back to their studies. Theomocent is hopeful that they will be able to find like-minded students to support their cause, while Leigh's attitude is less optimistic. During your observations, you also meet a highborn student surrounded by his female admirers. He introduces himself as Crammevoix de Maintigny, and appears to have done well in his efforts to persuade a fellow seminarian to return. During a conversation between the two about the nobles taking more responsibility in redressing the imbalance, the smiling seminarian mentions she was to pen a treatise─that is, until her primary text, volume eleven of the Seventy-two Articles of Halonic Polity, went missing. Nevertheless, she leaves to gather her things and return to the seminary, prompting Crammevoix to take his leave for a nap.
TEXT_CHREND103_02154_SEQ_06: Gaetelle announces the results of the exercise, with Archombadin and Lebrassoir guiding back the most students to the scholasticate. Though present for the announcement, Crammevoix's name is not among those mentioned, and Archombadin soon makes it clear that the girl he was speaking with, Ulaa, has instead formally withdrawn from the scholasticate. Crammevoix is suspicious of Ulaa's sudden departure, mentioning the dormitory prefect's open disagreement with her views on equality. The quarrel between the highborn students escalates, in which Archombadin utters a biting comment about House Maintigny, prompting Crammevoix to leave. Upon witnessing the feud, Briardien suggests the girl's withdrawal is worthy of further investigation.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_00: Briardien glances at you, adjusting his spectacles.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_01: Briardien has a hunch that the missing volume eleven of the Articles of Halonic Polity and Ulaa's sudden withdrawal are somehow connected, and decides to find the girl to ask her what─or who caused her to change her mind. In the meantime, Saturnois has asked to meet with you in private in the plaza next to Saint Reymanaud's Cathedral.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_02: At the plaza, Saturnois introduces Theomocent and Leigh as the students whom he is counseling to obtain Trinity seats. He also expresses his concerns about Archombadin and Lebrassoir, and their blatant discrimination of lowborn peers. In their pursuit to prove their virtue, Theomocent and Leigh discuss finding like-minded individuals with whom they could ally, and Crammevoix is mentioned as a possible candidate. As Leigh is unenthusiastic in approaching any of the highborn, Saturnois asks you to accompany Theomocent to the Pillars to find Crammevoix.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_03: While Theomocent tries his best to persuade Crammevoix to join his cause, it would appear that his timing is unfortunate as the suave seminarian is preoccupied with a beautiful young woman who had been vying for his attention. Laughing at Theomocent's cluelessness in the situation, the highborn student attempts to brush aside his resolve, and leaves elsewhere with the lady. But Theomocent refuses to give up just yet, and urges you to follow him to Foundation.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_04: Unexpectedly, Theomocent discovers Crammevoix tied up by his now knife-wielding lady friend. Despite his peril, he warns the timid seminarian not to interfere with his house's affairs, explaining that the woman is one of the smallfolk of his lands, who has rightfully come to seek recompense for his father's sins; he assumes he will most likely pay with his life, as his father had. Theomocent emotionally objects, and tries to convince the woman to accept coin instead of committing a sin herself. He then offers to exchange his life until Crammevoix can return, a gesture that the highborn is moved by.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_05: Trusting that Crammevoix will pay her his house's fortune, the woman reluctantly exchanges her prisoner, with Theomocent bound in his stead. Crammevoix promises to return soon after retrieving the coffer from its hidden place in Coerthas. With Theomocent assuring you he will be fine, Crammevoix asks you to accompany him to ensure bandits do not ambush him on the way back. Make haste to western Coerthas, before the knife-wielding woman loses her patience.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_06: You join Crammevoix in the western highlands, and he asks you to stand watch while he retrieves the family fortune. Ensure nothing will catch him unawares.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_07: As you wait for Crammevoix to search for the coffer, a group of hungry archaeornis seemingly appears out of nowhere. You dispatch the beasts and continue your watch.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_08: After what felt like an eternity, Crammevoix finally produces his family's fortune. He bids you both return to Ishgard, and hopes that Theomocent is still alive and well.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_09: Satisfied with the amount of monetary compensation for the war dead, the woman leaves without a word. Leigh and Saturnois arrive moments later, and Crammevoix reveals to all his father's sin; that he sought honor with the Holy See, and bought it with the blood of the smallfolk and eventually his own. After being left adrift in Ishgard since the murders of his family, Crammevoix is inspired by Theomocent's will to leave the sins of the past behind, declaring himself a friend and ally in their cause. Meanwhile, Saturnois tells you that Briardien has been waiting for you at the cathedral with some new information.
TEXT_CHREND104_02155_SEQ_10: You meet with Briardien, who tells you some concerning news about his investigation. Looking to inquire of Ulaa as to why she felt compelled to leave the scholasticate, he discovers that the girl has vanished altogether. Along with the missing volume eleven, Briardien comments that someone may indeed be trying to turn the situation to their advantage, and your duty as inspectors is to seek out the malicious forces at work.
TEXT_HEAVNY101_02201_SEQ_00: Trachraet has some worrying news concerning Pharos Sirius.
TEXT_HEAVNY101_02201_SEQ_01: Trachraet informs you that a kobold invasion has forced a group of smiths from Naldiq & Vymelli's to abandon their work on Pharos Sirius, to the great annoyance of Master Mimidoa. While it remains unclear how or why the beastmen ventured to the Isles of Umbra, it is abundantly clear they are up to no good. Seek out the storm flyer at the airship landing for further instructions.
TEXT_HEAVNY101_02201_SEQ_02:
At your request, the storm flyer relays Mimidoa's account of the attack. Apparently, the old smith is convinced the kobolds intend to blow up the lighthouse, having seen them scatter volatile bombs in the tunnels beneath the tower's foundation. With the livelihood of western La Noscea's inhabitants hanging in the balance, Maelstrom Command asks that you enter the tower by airship and defuse the kobolds' explosive plot before Aleport's shores are choked with debris.

※Pharos Sirius (Hard) can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_HEAVNY101_02201_SEQ_03: You have cleared Pharos Sirius of the incendiary surprises left by the kobolds. Report to the storm flyer in western La Noscea, and confirm that all went as planned.
TEXT_HEAVNY101_02201_SEQ_04: You return to find Maelstrom troops hurrying to clear the debris left by the kobolds, and rid the area of any remaining beastman invaders. While you discuss their progress with the storm flyer in charge, a private approaches you bearing a curious nautical knife carved with the sigil of Diamanda of Naldiq & Vymelli's, which was apparently discovered during a preliminary search of the area. With much still to be done, the storm flyer asks you to go to Aleport in her stead and hand the knife over to Trachraet, who will shortly be meeting with the smiths to relay the news of the lighthouse's reclamation.
TEXT_HEAVNY101_02201_SEQ_05: The blunt whittle turns out to be a personal effect of Diamanda's late brother Symond. The sight of it stokes the flames of resolve in the heart of the young smith, who vows to turn the forsaken lighthouse into a place to honor the lost. Your duty done, you take your leave, certain that Pharos Sirius will soon be restored to its former glory.
TEXT_HEAVNY004_02202_SEQ_00: The tetchy treasure hunter has the look of a woman who has seen rather too many morbols.
TEXT_HEAVNY004_02202_SEQ_01: You come across a terrified and bedraggled treasure hunter who explains that she has just escaped certain death at the claws of the seedkin hordes infesting Saint Mocianne's Arboretum. Within the ruins lies a treasure apparently worth risking life and limb over, and she asks that you aid her companions in obtaining it. Speak with the treasure hunter named Sawney in front of the Arboretum to join the search.
TEXT_HEAVNY004_02202_SEQ_02:
Sawney claims that the treasure he and his fellows seek within the Arboretum could benefit the residents of Idyllshire for years to come. Unfortunately, they lack the strength to fend off the beasts prowling the ruins where their prize presently rests. Eager to secure your aid in eliminating the creatures, Sawney offers to let you keep anything you find along the way. Venture into Saint Mocianne's Arboretum and clear a path for the treasure hunters so that they may search the ruins unimpeded.

※Saint Mocianne's Arboretum can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_HEAVNY004_02202_SEQ_03: You have fought your way through an army of Eorzea's flora and fauna, letting Sawney and his team search the Arboretum at their leisure. Return to the Dravanian hinterlands to see if their efforts bore any fruit.
TEXT_HEAVNY004_02202_SEQ_04: You find Sawney waiting for you outside the Arboretum. He happily exclaims that thanks to your efforts his fellows were able to find the object they sought without further incident. He then asks that you return with him to Idyllshire and report your success to Midnight Dew. Perhaps you will finally find out what the treasure hunters were so eager to obtain from the overgrown ruins.
TEXT_HEAVNY004_02202_SEQ_05: Sawney regales Midnight Dew with the tale of your brave foray into the Arboretum, and at last reveals the “treasure” he sought to be the seeds of specially cultivated crops. Midnight Dew hopes to use them to start a new industry in Idyllshire, and thereby free the settlement of its reliance on an ever-diminishing supply of Sharlayan junk. Even as Sawney departs to plant his treasure, you are cordially invited to visit Idyllshire in the near future to sample the bountiful harvest that the seeds will inevitably produce.
TEXT_HEAVNY301_02203_SEQ_00: Alys is casting pained glances at one of her regulars.
TEXT_HEAVNY301_02203_SEQ_01: Alys informs you that the wandering minstrel has been desperately awaiting your return to the Seventh Heaven. Share your tales of adventure with the forlorn bard, and supply him with the inspiration he needs to craft fresh verse.
TEXT_HEAVNY301_02203_SEQ_02:
You regale the melancholy minstrel with the story of your exploits on Azys Lla. The bard's transformation upon hearing your tale is nothing short of miraculous, and he immediately takes up his harp. The stirring epic he composes to commemorate your triumph is flattering, but seems to suffer from some measure of embellishment...

※The Minstrel's Ballad: Thordan's Reign can be accessed via the Duty Finder.
TEXT_CHREND201_02207_SEQ_00: Briardien appears to be lost in thought.
TEXT_CHREND201_02207_SEQ_01: Briardien tells you that while change has come to Ishgard, ill-feeling between the low- and highborn yet festers, with tensions rising by the day. The inspector is convinced that the recent hostilities are the result of a carefully laid plot conceived to further the interests of a party or parties unknown. Though he has yet to discover what their ultimate aim might be, he is not without a plan. Certain that the unexplained disappearances of Ulaa and volume eleven of the Articles of Halonic Polity are somehow related to the scheme, he declares his intent to find the missing girl by tracking down the missing book. While he continues to search for the tome, Briardien bids you inquire as to whether the students have heard anything concerning Ulaa's whereabouts or, failing that, observed any unusual goings-on.
TEXT_CHREND201_02207_SEQ_02: You speak with the students of the scholasticate, who are mostly preoccupied with their studies or else talking amongst themselves. As you continue making your rounds, however, it becomes clear that not everyone is present, and that two pupils in particular are notable by their absence. Ask Father Saturnois if he knows where Theomocent and Leigh might be.
TEXT_CHREND201_02207_SEQ_03: Father Saturnois reveals that ever since Theomocent and Leigh learned of Ulaa's disappearance, they have devoted all of their energies to finding her, determined that she should resume her studies. With this apparently in mind, they begged leave to travel to Gorgagne Mills, and duly received it.
TEXT_CHREND201_02207_SEQ_04: You arrive at the abandoned settlement to find Theomocent and Leigh kneeling in prayer. At your approach, the former rises to greet you, and reveals that Gorgagne Mills is the resting place of the boys' late mentor, Father Choisseau. He goes on to explain that the two of them often visit the grave when they are feeling lost or uncertain. Interpreting your unexpected arrival as a sign from on high, the two students seem satisfied that their time has been well spent, and resolve to return to the scholasticate forthwith. Follow in their footsteps, and report their deeds to Father Saturnois.
TEXT_CHREND201_02207_SEQ_05: Upon learning what his two best pupils were doing in the western highlands, Father Saturnois seems wholly unsurprised, acknowledging that Theomocent and Leigh had always held the man who raised them close to their hearts. Far from feeling misled, he is pleased to see that their feelings for Father Choisseau are as strong as ever, and heartened by the concern they have shown for their fellow students.
TEXT_CHREND202_02208_SEQ_00: Father Saturnois wears a troubled frown...
TEXT_CHREND202_02208_SEQ_01: According to Father Saturnois, the scholasticate is awash with rumors that Archombadin was complicit in Ulaa's disappearance. Reasoning that the youth would never involve himself in anything which might endanger his reputation, nor less bring dishonor to House Dzemael as a whole, he is convinced that an outsider must be responsible, and implores you to look into the matter. Wasting no time, he ushers you in the direction of Lebrassoir, who has been frantically searching for clues as to the identity of the true culprit.
TEXT_CHREND202_02208_SEQ_02: Unsurprisingly, Lebrassoir is adamant that Archombadin had nothing to do with Ulaa's disappearance, and he duly bombards you with evidence of his friend's innocence. However, he soon catches himself and abruptly changes tack, and after making you swear to tell none but Briardien what he is about to divulge, he produces volume eleven of the Articles of Halonic Polity, which he confesses to having found in Archombadin's room. Insisting that Ulaa must somehow be responsible for both the recent rumors, and the sudden appearance of the book in the prefect's dormitory, he hands over the tome, and beseeches you to find Ulaa so that Archombadin's name might be cleared. Now would seem a good time to apprise Briardien of all that has occurred.
TEXT_CHREND202_02208_SEQ_03: Briardien is both impressed and slightly flabbergasted to learn that you have found the missing volume. Though he is somewhat skeptical of the seminarians' grand conspiracy theories, he acknowledges that speculation will avail you naught, and that further investigation is in order. While he seeks to learn what he can from the tome, he bids you make your way to the Brume and see if any there know of Ulaa─or failing that, know of any unusual happenings, for one can never be too well-informed.
TEXT_CHREND202_02208_SEQ_04: Some of the residents of the Brume are more forthcoming than others, and while none of their information seems to pertain directly to Ulaa, two accounts in particular give you pause─one of a poor man come into a small fortune, and another of a rich man offering far too much for a simple errand. Though it seems unlikely that these incidents have any connection to Ulaa's disappearance, perhaps Inspector Briardien will think otherwise.
TEXT_CHREND202_02208_SEQ_05: Briardien informs you that Ulaa was the last person to have removed the book from the library─a fact which could lend credence to Lebrassoir's claims. Still, it is a far cry from conclusive evidence. Seeing as how the power of the Echo will avail you naught under these circumstances, you have no choice but to rely upon the traditional methods of continuing to search for clues and question persons of interest...
TEXT_CHREND203_02209_SEQ_00: Briardien is eager to continue his investigation.
TEXT_CHREND203_02209_SEQ_01: Briardien declares that he will continue investigating your newest leads into the whereabouts of the missing Ulaa. In the meantime, he requests that you speak with some of the seminarians once more─namely Blaisie and the group she has been assisting with their own search. Though he is loath to admit it, the inspector seems to think that the youths may have noticed something you have overlooked thus far. But before you can learn what Blaisie knows, you will have to find her...
TEXT_CHREND203_02209_SEQ_02: No one at the scholasticate seems to know exactly where Blaisie can be found, but a number of seminarians suggest that if you find Theomocent, she will not be far behind. As the young man is said to be somewhere in the vicinity of the Arc of the Venerable, that would seem to be the ideal location to begin your search.
TEXT_CHREND203_02209_SEQ_03:
You find Blaisie hiding behind a fountain, watching as Theomocent and his friends make their inquiries. Startled by your sudden appearance, she struggles to explain her behavior, but regains her composure upon realizing who you are. After introducing herself as Briardien's younger sister, she correctly deduces the purpose for which you have come and produces a scroll of considerable length containing countless testimonies she recently transcribed in an effort to ascertain the whereabouts of Ulaa.

Just as Blaisie is about to turn the scroll over to you, however, Theomocent, Leigh, and Crammevoix suddenly appear, and you find yourselves reviewing the many accounts together. Yet you are unable to read even half of Blaisie's accounts before Leigh grows frustrated at their apparent lack of relevant information. Whether or not they contain aught of value remains to be seen, but that is for Briardien to decide, as the seminarians are more than happy to let the inspector sift through the endless accounts in their stead.
TEXT_CHREND203_02209_SEQ_04: Briardien's efforts have borne fruit, it would seem, as he reveals to you that the gentleman seeking cough medicine and the tavern patron who paid his debts are likely one and the same. Once a notorious thug, now ostensibly reformed, he is rumored to have come into money and now makes a living as a traveling merchant. Needless to say, the inspector has every intention of tracking this suspect down, but he requires more information─which you are more than happy to provide in the form of Blaisie's notes. Together, you review the testimonies and eventually conclude that Mestonnaux, a merchant, has been engaged in suspicious activities. Your next course of action is thus decided: you and Briardien are to spy upon Mestonnaux, and see if he leads you to your suspect.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_00: Briardien is on the verge of a breakthrough.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_01: Briardien is eager to find and tail the shifty merchant from Blaisie's notes, and believes that staking out Mestonnaux's food stall will allow you to accomplish just that. Seeing as he could show up any time to procure his standard selection of items from the carvery, the inspector urges you make haste and follow him to the Jeweled Crozier. Securing a secluded corner on the bustling street, the two of you keep an eye out for a scar-faced man swathed in silken robes.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_02: As you stand watch at the Jeweled Crozier, a man fitting the description of the thug-turned-merchant appears, making a beeline for the food stall. Without taking his eyes off the merchant, Briardien begins pursuing the suspect with you in tow.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_03: Briardien is waiting for you at the Arc of the Worthy. According to him, the man you are tailing just passed through the gates and entered the Coerthas central highlands. Curtly reminding you to take care not to be spotted, he bids you follow him.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_04: Concealing yourselves behind a large tree, you and Briardien quietly observe a suspicious-looking carriage, into which the fake merchant disappeared but a moment ago. Taking note of the nearby guard, the inspector then asks you to create a diversion by announcing a surprise inspection of their wagon. While you distract the two men, he intends to gain entrance to the carriage and see what he can find. With the chat mode in Say, use your keyboard or the software keyboard to enter any phrase that contains the word “inspection” to draw the fake merchant and his guard's attention.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_05: You immediately draw the attention of the fake merchant and his guard by announcing a surprise inspection of their carriage. Marching toward you, they advise you in no uncertain terms to be on your way. However, when it becomes clear you will not─or rather cannot─abide by their wishes, they turn hostile. Charging at you with weapons in hand, it looks as though the only way to stop them would be through force.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_06: You overpower the two thugs, and see that they are restrained. As you turn to go and consult with the inspector on how to proceed, you notice he is hunched before a diminutive figure curled upon a thick blanket of Coerthan snow. Check if aught is amiss.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_07: You rush over to Briardien who─in hushed tones─is comforting Ulaa. Aside from appearing slightly peaky, she looks to be uninjured. The inspector informs you that, as suspected, she had been abducted, held captive in the fake merchant's carriage.  Shortly thereafter, a band of Temple Knights appears, inquiring as to what the earlier racket was about. Briardien quickly narrates the events that had transpired before handing the thug and his lackey over to them and escorting Ulaa back to the scholasticate dormitory.
TEXT_CHREND204_02210_SEQ_08: Briardien meets with you at Saint Reymanaud's Cathedral and informs you that Ulaa is being tended to by Sister Gaetelle and is expected to make a full recovery. While she is currently in no condition to be questioned, the interrogation of the kidnappers is already well underway. Alas, it has yet to yield any substantial information regarding the identity of their employer. Though this case seems to grow more convoluted with every passing day, you and the inspector remain hopeful that the truth will eventually be brought to light.
TEXT_JOBREL100_02211_SEQ_00: Rowena is planning a trip to Revenant's Toll.
TEXT_JOBREL100_02211_SEQ_01: You happen upon Rowena just as two unexpected visitors arrive. The first is an earnest young researcher bearing an urgent request, the second, Gerolt the ale-sodden blacksmith. Wasting no time, the researcher, one Ardashir, declares that he has been conducting research into the creation of artificial life─something he refers to as “anima.” Though all of his trials have thus far ended in failure, he is convinced that the Sharlayans' work on arcane sentries holds the key to success. Before he can continue with his suit, however, Gerolt decries him for his lack of imagination, and wryly suggests fusing the anima with a weapon─a proposal which Ardashir considers a stroke of genius. Never one to miss a chance to turn a profit, Rowena sets about persuading Gerolt to take part in the venture, and before you know it, you too have been roped in to test the finished product. You are to rendezvous with Ardashir and Gerolt in Azys Lla, where the pair will apparently be working.
TEXT_JOBREL100_02211_SEQ_02: You find Ardashir in Azys Lla marveling at the technological wonders of the once-great Allagan Empire. Now that you have arrived, he is ready to begin work on the anima weapon.
TEXT_JOBREL101_02212_SEQ_00:
Ardashir seems eager to bring anima into being.
※Changing classes or jobs will prevent progress during this quest.
TEXT_JOBREL101_02212_SEQ_01:
Ardashir hopes to begin work on the anima weapon as soon as possible. All the necessary elements are in place save two: astral and umbral nodules, the catalysts required to facilitate the process of channeling aether into the soulstone. Unsure of where to procure them, Ardashir suggests speaking with Rowena in Revenant's Toll. With any luck, she will know of a merchant who can provide what he needs.

※You may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.
TEXT_JOBREL101_02212_SEQ_02: Hearing of your need for crystals with unusual properties, Rowena suggests speaking with a merchant by the name of Syndony. She is a jeweler who also happens to be quite knowledgeable about crystals. You can find her on the terrace of the second floor in the House of Splendors.
TEXT_JOBREL101_02212_SEQ_03:
Upon speaking with Syndony, it soon becomes clear that your reputation has preceded you. When you inquire about the nodules, she is taken aback by your outlandish request, but is not deterred from the challenge of producing what you seek. The process will require elementally aspected luminous crystals, and she insists you bring her one of every element. However, she also believes there may be one other way: bringing her a Zodiac Weapon of the highest order. Seeing your nonplussed expression, she concedes that such a legendary weapon may be no more than a rumor.

※Should you be unwilling or unable to offer a suitable Zodiac Weapon, luminous crystals can be obtained by participating in FATEs in the following regions:
- Sea of Clouds: luminous wind crystals
- Azys Lla: luminous fire crystals
- Churning Mists: luminous lightning crystals
- Coerthas western highlands: luminous ice crystals
- Dravanian forelands: luminous earth crystals
- Dravanian hinterlands: luminous water crystals
TEXT_JOBREL101_02212_SEQ_04: With the nodules in hand, Ardashir is at last ready to go through with Gerolt's plan. He duly completes the infusion of aether, and hands the pulsating soulstone to Gerolt, who immediately sets about affixing the radiant gem to your weapon. Some time later, the sweating smith finally lowers his hammer, a look of both exhaustion and satisfaction on his face. The plan has succeeded and you are the proud owner of an anima weapon. Now begins the journey to discover its full potential.
TEXT_JOBREL102_02213_SEQ_00:
Ardashir seems curious to see how the anima will develop.
※Changing classes or jobs will prevent progress during this quest.
TEXT_JOBREL102_02213_SEQ_01:
The anima now residing in your weapon is as a newborn babe in mortal terms. In order to foster this fledgling spirit, Gerolt suggests that you treat it to some good old-fashioned combat. Knowing that you have been involved in more than a few titanic battles over the years, he recommends revisiting the sites of some of your most memorable encounters. Hearing this, Ardashir asks to accompany you to ensure the anima's development does not go undocumented. When you subsequently look back upon your past exploits, the frost-rimed halls of Snowcloak spring to mind. Perhaps Coerthas would be a good place to begin the anima's education.

※You may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.
TEXT_JOBREL102_02213_SEQ_02:
With anima weapon in hand, you fight your way through Snowcloak's frozen chambers, and emerge none the worse for wear. While contemplating your next destination, a glinting fish in the half-frozen water nearby catches your eye, and in that moment you decide where to continue the anima's education: the Sastasha Seagrot.

※The prerequisite quests for Sastasha (Hard) must be completed before continuing with this quest.
TEXT_JOBREL102_02213_SEQ_03:
