While admittedly shocked, the Cornservant immediately understands that the merchant's appetite is not his own and demands the entity responsible to come forth. The true culprit, it turns out, is a sentient dagger.

The Cornservant explains that such tools were once used for ritual sacrifices performed for bountiful harvests, but that the practice has long since been abandoned. Because the wayward blade requires life energies for sustenance, the Cornservant suggests it stay in your company so as to feast on the life force of your fallen foes. The merchant readily surrenders the knife to your care before taking his leave, and the Cornservant believes now would be as good a time as any for you to become acquainted with your new traveling companion.
TEXT_KINGZA101_05307_SEQ_04: Judging by the blade's swishing, you are quite certain your new companion─which you have elected to name the Deathservant─has taken a liking to you. Or so you hope... In any case, the rumbling of bellies has ceased, meaning it is time for the Cornservant to take their leave. They have every confidence the ritual blade will be safe in your capable hands─but will you be safe? Only time will tell...
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_00: The expedition messenger casts his gaze expectantly about the harbor.
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_01: At High Tide Harbor you meet a messenger sent by Ketenramm to find you. He soon fetches the legendary Eorzean explorer, who proceeds to outline his plans for one final voyage─sights firmly set on Shades' Triangle, a fabled and feared stretch of ocean in the Indigo Deep. Convinced that your aid will guarantee the expedition's success, he invites you to join his crew on a journey into the unknown. Having assented, you are to speak with Ofangeim, one of the expedition crew members waiting on the pier.
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_02: Ofangeim, the ship's navigator, informs you that the treacherous storms Shades' Triangle is famed for will briefly subside, leaving calm seas and perfect sailing conditions in their wake. Gesturing to the skiff moored nearby, she explains that the main vessel is waiting beyond the shallows, and bids you report to her when ready.
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_03: After making the necessary preparations for the voyage ahead, you speak with Ofangeim and set off for seas uncharted...
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_04:
On board the expedition vessel, Ketenramm reveals that the stormy waters of Shades' Triangle conceal a strange, crescent-shaped island, the sight of which is said to spell certain doom for all who sail too close. Listening to his explanation, it is clear that such cautionary tales have had quite the opposite effect on the veteran sailor. Still malms away from your destination, Ketenramm suggests you get to know the crew risking their lives alongside you on this perilous adventure.

※In the event that you leave the ship, you may resume your journey by speaking with the expedition ferryman at High Tide Harbor.
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_05: You meet the crew and hear their motivations for joining the expedition─not to mention a curious account of a wayward weaponsmith currently languishing in the ship's hold. Ketenramm is no doubt curious to hear your impressions of the crew.
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_06: Ketenramm announces that the ship will soon enter Shades' Triangle. The crew assume their positions, steeled for the final approach.
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_07:
As the crew contend with the island vanishing and reappearing at will, you hear a voice ring out over the waves, beckoning you onward. Shortly after, the ship lurches violently, seized by some arcane power as blinding light engulfs the vessel. As the white pall dissipates, you find yourselves docked at the island's crumbling stone pier. The ship is unscathed but locked firmly in place─perhaps held by the same force that transported you and the crew to these shores. For his part, Ketenramm is quietly pleased about the prospect of being trapped on the isle, and ventures forth with a grin.

※Should you leave the Occult Crescent, you will be able to return via High Tide Harbor whenever you wish to rejoin the expedition.
TEXT_KINGKD001_05309_SEQ_08: You gather by the entrance to a walled settlement nestled above the dock. Expecting the island to be uninhabited, Ketenramm is intrigued to find signs of civilization, albeit seemingly long absent. No doubt this will be but the first of myriad mysteries awaiting you once the expedition gets underway.
TEXT_KINGKD002_05310_SEQ_00: Ketenramm scans the empty settlement with wary eyes.
TEXT_KINGKD003_05311_SEQ_00: The Archive yearns to make sense of the situation.
TEXT_KINGKD003_05311_SEQ_01: You convene with the Archive and Ketenramm in the deserted plaza. As the tonberry ponders why his slumber went uninterrupted for so many years, a faerie floats forth and shares a curious revelation. She claims that whatever knowledge the Archive once possessed has been sealed away, and more bafflingly, that his present memory is somehow linked to the things you yourself have seen and learned. As the faerie leaves─the group none the wiser as to who summoned her, or indeed her purpose─the Archive notes that she is wreathed in the same aether permeating the isle. Discovering the identity of her master may shed light on how Shades' Triangle came to be. As the mysteries proliferate, Ketenramm is determined to forge on with the expedition, and bids you speak with Jeffroy who has been tasked with establishing a base camp on the isle.
TEXT_KINGKD003_05311_SEQ_02: Jeffroy apprises you of the crew's progress scouting the south horn of the island. With the advance party already working to establish a base camp, the Hyur asks that you let him know when you are ready to begin your excursion.
TEXT_KINGKD004_05312_SEQ_00: Ketenramm is overseeing activities at the expedition base camp.
TEXT_KINGKD004_05312_SEQ_01: You find Ketenramm presiding over an already well-established encampment, on the edge of which the Archive appears to have found something. The intrigued explorer bids you speak with the strange fellow in case he has pertinent information to share.
TEXT_KINGKD004_05312_SEQ_02: The scholar-turned-tonberry excitedly pores over a heap of rubble, from which he produces a crystal for your inspection. The moment you lay eyes upon it, the Archive claims to have recalled all that he once knew pertaining to his discovery. Having thus unlocked a portion of his sealed knowledge, he explains that the crystal─a soul shard─affords the bearer access to the martial techniques and arcane arts of eld, and insists you affix it to your garb.
TEXT_KINGKD005_05313_SEQ_00: The Archive insists you affix the soul shard to your person.
TEXT_KINGKD006_05314_SEQ_00: Ketenramm has devised a plan for the pending expedition.
TEXT_KINGKD007_05315_SEQ_00: The Archive is keen to hear your depiction of the southern ruins.
TEXT_KINGKD008_05316_SEQ_00: The Archive awaits your report on the island's myriad architectural remnants.
TEXT_KINGKD009_05317_SEQ_00: The Archive wishes to know if your ongoing search for ruins has proven successful.
TEXT_KINGKD010_05318_SEQ_00: Ketenramm wishes to discuss the next phase of the expedition.
TEXT_KINGKD010_05318_SEQ_01: You share the scouts' report with Ketenramm, revealing that the Tower of Blood is accessible during the right climatic conditions. While unwilling to commit the expedition's resources to exploring the tower, he nonetheless gives tacit approval to your own potential forays within. For his part, the veteran seafarer has turned his attentions to the next stage of the expedition, and bids you return to Tuliyollal and inform the messenger of progress thus far.
TEXT_KINGKD010_05318_SEQ_02: Back at High Tide Harbor, the messenger is delighted to hear the crew remain safe, despite being stranded. Progress report complete, all that remains is to await news of Ketenramm's ingress into the north horn and the resumption of your adventures upon the Occult Crescent...
TEXT_KINGKW001_05319_SEQ_00: Lydirceil is on the hunt for a missing weaponsmith.
TEXT_KINGKW001_05319_SEQ_01: You encounter Lydirceil by the isle's fledgling smithy, bemoaning the disorderly conduct of the master artisan hired for the expedition. After spending much of the journey to the Occult Crescent languishing in the ship's hold and making a sizable dent in the crew's liquid provisions, it would appear the weaponsmith has attempted to flee. Lydirceil bids you seek out the man in question─Gerolt─and implore him to return.
TEXT_KINGKW001_05319_SEQ_02: Gerolt turns out to be in the midst of a fruitless quest for rum among a pile of supply crates. According to the weaponsmith, he was not made aware of the expedition's destination until the ship had already left High Tide Harbor─perhaps explaining the erratic behavior Lydirceil recounted. Realizing that fulfilling his contractual duties will be the fastest way off the isle, Gerolt makes his way back to smithy, ready─though hardly raring─to work. No doubt Lydirceil will wish to thank you for locating the wayward weaponsmith.
TEXT_KINGKW001_05319_SEQ_03:
With Gerolt returned, Lydirceil is eager to see him earn his keep. The weaponsmith, however, considers all but the most challenging commissions beneath him, and outlines his plans for a brand-new weapon enhancement technique. Lydirceil acknowledges the folly of having a realm-renowned craftsman perform the everyday drudgery of running a smithy, and begrudgingly assents. According to Gerolt, your weapon can be raised to hitherto unimaginable heights of power through the use of crystalline objects known as demiatma.

※Three pieces of six unique varieties are required, and these can be obtained from FATEs and critical encounters on the Occult Crescent's South Horn, or from FATEs in the following regions:
Urqopacha, Kozama'uka, Yak T'el, Shaaloani, Heritage Found, or Living Memory.
TEXT_KINGKW001_05319_SEQ_04: You deliver the requisite six varieties of demiatma to the weaponsmith, who seems eager to begin─not least because renewed access to the expedition's rum supply is contingent on his progress. Taking the crystals, he vows to imbue his tools in preparation for the enhancement process.
TEXT_KINGKW002_05320_SEQ_00:
Lydirceil is eager for Gerolt to bring his plans to fruition.
※Changing classes or jobs will prevent progress during this quest.
TEXT_KINGKW002_05320_SEQ_01:
You approach Lydirceil, having resolved to seek the new heights of perfection promised by Gerolt's phantom weapons. Although the crew have unearthed a sizable quantity of the raw materials required, Lydirceil informs you of a somewhat knotty contractual agreement to the House of Splendors. Any and all resources obtained during the expedition are apparently the property of Rowena, which will entail a significant outlay on your part to purchase the necessary arcanite. Conveniently, Rowena's mercantile representative, Ermina, stands at the ready to do business. Mere strides away awaits Dodokkuli, a metallurgist assisting with preparations in Gerolt's stead.

※You may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.
TEXT_KINGKW002_05320_SEQ_02: Stock of tomestones greatly diminished, you deliver the three chunks of arcanite to Dodokkuli. The metallurgist dutifully prepares the ore before entrusting the remaining work to Gerolt, who puts demiatma-infused hammer to anvil and completes the process. The result is every bit the “pinnacle o' weapon fabrication” the master artisan claims it to be, and will no doubt prove an exquisite companion in future encounters with fiends great and small alike.
TEXT_KINGWZ001_05323_SEQ_00: Where there are idle hands, Mumukko finds ways to fill them.
TEXT_KINGWZ001_05323_SEQ_01: You happen to cross paths with Mumukko, project manager for the Cosmic Exploration Initiative, who insists that you have time to spare. As she explains to you, her job has been made difficult in recent days by certain brilliant but otherwise absent-minded workers who have yet to collect their crew uniforms. Thankfully for Mumukko, you have allegedly volunteered to assist her, and thus are you entrusted with the forgotten articles and a map with which to locate their owners.
TEXT_KINGWZ001_05323_SEQ_02: The first two deliveries are completed without incident. The off-duty gleaner, having joined the initiative in pursuit of more difficult jobs, was mortified at the sight of her uniform, lamenting her mistake as amateurish. The xenobiologist Chrysielle, on the other hand, scarcely blinked at the sight of hers, as her mind is far more fixated on the prospect of proving her theses. Only one suit remains, and according to Mumukko's map, its owner can be found somewhere near the Galactic Way.
TEXT_KINGWZ001_05323_SEQ_03: The final forgotten crew uniform belongs to none other than Kokkol Dankkol, the eccentric engineer who previously perfected the aetherburner for the Ragnarok, now promoted to chief propulsion systems engineer for the Cosmic Exploration Initiative. He is delighted to see you─less so the uniform, as he only feels at ease wearing his standard work attire. Mumukko, meanwhile, is unamused by his lax outlook on sanitation. After impressing upon him the importance of preventing contamination of their ship, and any stars upon which it may land, he is eventually cowed into compliance. The engineer then sets off in his new formfitting attire, and Mumukko invites you to return to the Lunar Hopopolis for a reward.
TEXT_KINGWZ001_05323_SEQ_04: Mumukko understands this errand is a matter well below your station, and so she apologizes for the triviality of it all. She believes that strong personalities, such as those drawn to the initiative, can only be corralled by those with strength in equal measure. Grateful for your assistance, she hopes to prevail upon it again in future.
TEXT_KINGWZ002_05324_SEQ_00: Where there are more idle hands, Mumukko will find even more ways to fill them.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_00: Hardiboiled's stoic silhouette is a fixture amidst the bright lights and bustle of True Vue.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_01:
Inspector's Log:
No sooner did I emerge from a thirty-year slumber than I found myself at the heart of a mystery most diabolical: the Case of the Fiendish Fugitives! A secretive researcher has been imbuing monsters with the souls of criminals, who are then set loose in Alexandria to commit their favored felony. With the cooperation of the surly-if-well-meaning Detective Hardiboiled─whom I feel compelled to reiterate resembles me not in the slightest─we were able to apprehend one such villain, an eyeclops with an eye for larceny. Though the fugitive knew naught of the researcher's grand scheme, it is only a matter of time─and the investigative genius of Hildibrand Helidor Maximilian Manderville─ere all is brought before the light of gentlemanly justice!
　　　　　　　　　　　　*　*　*
Hardiboiled has extracted more data from the storage device recovered from Yuweyawata, identifying a new fugitive-turned-fiend for your crew to pursue. The criminal in question has assumed the form of a cauahealoa, a bipedal wolf, and it is believed that it will be committing acts of wanton vandalism, for which it had earned notoriety as a man. While the fiend is like to avoid densely populated areas, for want of other leads, Hardiboiled suggests calling on one of his trusted sources, a man named Mymond. Setting aside the similarity to a certain information broker in Ul'dah for now, you make your way across the recreation zone to meet with the individual.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_02: In a development that would perhaps be amazing were it not but another of the countless curiosities you have experienced in the presence of Inspector Hildibrand, Mymond turns out to be the spitting image of Wymond. From the purveyor of information, you learn that a cauahealoa has been sighted entering yet not emerging from Vanguard. Furthermore, its mannerisms marked it as more man than beast. This is enough to convince Hardiboiled that your target has gone to Shaaloani, and you and your companions set off for the barrier's exit.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_03: During your passage through Vanguard, Hardiboiled betrays an irrational fear for oglops when he loses his characteristic cool in an encounter with the verminous insects. Your timely provision of a boiled egg thankfully suffices for him to regain composure, and you continue on to Shaaloani without further incident.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_04: Upon arriving in Shaaloani, Hardiboiled proposes that you begin by gathering information in settlements. Sheshenewezi Springs lies a short distance to the south, and it is there that your crew first makes its way.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_05: You and your companions split up to question the people of Sheshenewezi Springs about acts of vandalism in the area. Such incidents would serve to confirm the presence of your fugitive.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_06: Through your inquiries, you have learned that there has been a spate of vandalism targeting equipment and barns. Though the Dustwatch has no lead as yet, the culprit is believed to be an outsider. Armed with this knowledge, you go to seek out Hardiboiled.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_07: You report your findings to Hardiboiled, who says that he has heard much the same. When Hildibrand then wonders after Nashu's whereabouts, Hardiboiled expresses his exasperation before proposing that you split up to search for the inspector's absent-minded assistant.
TEXT_CHRHDB931_05378_SEQ_08: At the outskirts of Sheshenewezi Springs, you find Nashu being accosted by ruffians who, having seen her polishing her “medicine,” wish to take her in as the wanted vandal. As the confrontation heats up, Hardiboiled challenges the leader to settle matters the old-fashioned way, and the two subsequently square off for a duel in the middle of town. With his superior experience and skill, Hardiboiled gets the better of his brash young opponent before further dodging a spray of bullets from the remaining ruffians. The commotion draws out Kemakka, who deems Hardiboiled innocent for his part in an unlawful gunfight, but when Hildibrand accidentally ignites one of Nashu's Delights in his presence, the sheriff decides to arrest her as a vandal suspect. As his assistant is led away in shackles, the inspector manages to extricate himself from the ground in time to swear that he will clear her name.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_00: Where it concerns his assistant's well-being, not even Inspector Hildibrand can maintain his customary aplomb.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_01: Nashu's detainment on suspicion of being the vandal has made Hildibrand all the more determined to catch the true criminal. In the course of his inquiries, the inspector was able to learn that a wolflike fiend has been sighted near Luwateninyawawsa, and thus do you make for the settlement in hopes of finding a lead.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_02: Traversing the red plains of Shaaloani, you and your companions soon arrive at Luwateninyawawsa. This time, Hardiboiled suggests questioning the locals together, and bids you indicate when you are ready to begin.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_03:
At your word, you and your companions proceed into Luwateninyawawsa. With some luck, the residents will have information leading to your lupine fugitive.

※You must be accompanied by Hardiboiled and Hildibrand to complete this task. Speak with either of them again should you become separated.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_04: You speak with a farmer who claims to have witnessed a wolflike fiend making off with a sack of vegetables, indicating that your fugitive has been hungry. Making note of this finding, you continue making your way through Luwateninyawawsa.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_05: The second person you approach has not seen a wolf-fiend, but rather some manner of adorable, squealing creature. While Hardiboiled has heard about such a beast on True Vue, he believes it is unrelated to your investigation, and you look for other residents to question.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_06: You meet a woman who has caught sight of a wolflike fiend multiple times, in lunyucaua'pya territory to the south of the settlement. Hardiboiled is convinced that the fugitive must be hiding there, and you waste no time setting forth to investigate.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_07: You come to the Eshceyaani Wilds, the general location of the sighting, but the cauahealoa is not immediately in evidence. At Hardiboiled's bidding, you split up to scour the area for traces of the fugitive.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_08: Taking yourself around the wilds, you manage to find a set of clues: a sack of produce, an empty liquor bottle, and─most telling of all─a piece of paper appearing to bear diary entries written by the vandal. Next to the paper was an oglop, but you set that detail aside for now as you hurry to present your discoveries to Hardiboiled.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_09: A review of the diary entries confirms that, like the thieving eyeclops, the vandalizing cauahealoa indeed serves the mysterious researcher. The fugitive has now been instructed to “put on a bigger show,” to which end the mastermind will provide him with barrels of ceruleum. When Hildibrand reiterates his opposition to violence ahead of a potential confrontation, Hardiboiled reveals his tragic past as a cautionary tale. He, too, once had an assistant, but she was killed by the Crime King when he lowered his guard in a moment of softness. The warning duly given, you and your companions next head to Hhusatahwi, there to alert Kemakka and his Dustwatch to the fugitive's intent.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_10: When you alert Kemakka to the impending act of destruction, he reveals that the vandal has just announced the train to be the target. The sheriff departs to round up his officers, during which time your party hurries ahead to the station. There, you at last come face-to-face with the vandalizing cauahealoa, who threatens to ignite the barrels of ceruleum placed before the engine. However, the fiend carelessly sets itself ablaze instead, and it takes an inspired moment of collaboration between Hildibrand and Hardiboiled to stop the panicked creature from hurtling straight into the explosive fuel. Kemakka then arrives and has his men take the fugitive into custody, but it is revealed that the sheriff is in fact an impostor, with the Crime King, Carnelian, having assumed his likeness. The villain manages to flee the scene─but not before ominously declaring that the commotion has served its purpose...
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_11: Back at Dustwatch headquarters in Hhusatahwi, Kemakka has scarcely released Nashu from her cell when one of his officers bursts in with dire news: a large shipment of ceruleum has been stolen from Sheshenewezi, with the thieves striking while the watch's eyes were on the train station. Thus do you discover the researcher's true target, albeit too late. Kemakka promises to conduct a thorough investigation in Shaaloani, and having resolved the situation as it stands, you and your companions make your way back to the bright lights of True Vue in Solution Nine.
TEXT_CHRHDB932_05379_SEQ_12: With the researcher's grand design and identity still unknown, Hardiboiled says that he will continue working to extract more data from the storage device. He bids you check in from time to time, and you brace yourself for when next the Case of the Fiendish Fugitives resumes.
TEXT_KINGKW101_05380_SEQ_01:
Lydirceil informs you the surveyors have unearthed a new variety of ore with potential for use in the weapon enhancement process. While the team works to procure a sufficient quantity, the smithy foreman is eager to plan for the next phase of the endeavor. His efforts to secure Gerolt's continued cooperation have been unsuccessful, however, with the weaponsmith once again fixated on rum and the excessive consumption thereof. In the hopes of leveraging his pride as a craftsman and spurring him to action, Lydirceil bids you cast /doubt on Gerolt's capabilities.

※Speak to Lydirceil if you wish to abandon this quest.
TEXT_KINGKW101_05380_SEQ_02:
Having been subjected to the full force of your doubt, Gerolt reveals that, despite appearances, he has been contemplating how best to proceed. His grand idea: have someone else figure it out. More specifically, your resident knife-wielding know-it-all, the Archive. An exasperated Lydirceil calls the scholar-turned-tonberry over, who, once apprised of the situation, reveals unsealed knowledge of an ancient imbuing process known as “aetheric infusion.” The method turns out to be rather labor-intensive, requiring four vessels known as “aetherwells” to be filled with energy via repeated, intense combat. Enthused by the idea of acquiring this long-lost art, Gerolt offers to coat the aetherwells with a solution to increase their aetheric absorption rate and thus speed up the process. You are to collect the requisite ingredients and deliver them to the weaponsmith when ready.

Rroneek glue: seek a trader in the markets of Tuliyollal.
Ut'ohmu siderite: seek a Yak T'el trader who deals in precious stones.
Three varieties of synthetic dark matter: craft using the relevant recipe or purchase from the market board.

※Should you choose to craft the synthetic dark matter, you will need to have obtained the Master Recipe XII tomes of the Disciples of the Hand.
TEXT_KINGKW101_05380_SEQ_03: You hand over the ingredients to Gerolt and prepare to wait while Dodokkuli dutifully formulates the solution.
TEXT_KINGKW101_05380_SEQ_04: The Lalafellin metallurgist finishes applying the solution to the empty aetherwells, thereby boosting their capacity to absorb the aether generated in battle. Despite this provision to expedite the process, no doubt many a grueling bout of bloodshed lies ahead...
TEXT_KINGKW102_05381_SEQ_00: Lydirceil has been poring over the Archive's stone tablet.
TEXT_KINGKW102_05381_SEQ_01:
With the vessels glazed and ready, the trying task of filling them through ferocious combat lies ahead. According to Gerolt, the isle's unstable ambient aether is ill-suited to the endeavor, and instead recommends you strike out for battlefields distant and multifarious. Each aetherwell can be replenished via a different Duty Roulette category:

Green: High-level Dungeons
Blue: Alliance Raids
Red: Trials
Yellow: Normal Raids

You may use the aetherwell array to gauge how much aether has been accumulated.

※Speak to Gerolt if you wish to abandon this quest.
TEXT_KINGKW102_05381_SEQ_02: After an endless succession of hard-fought battles, the aetherwells are full. You deliver them to Gerolt, who soon performs the necessary preparations and channels the abundance of energy into his very being. The ancient art of “aetheric bleedin' infusion” thus absorbed, the cantankerous craftsman is almost ready to turn his attention to the phantom weapons themselves. What hitherto unimagined heights of refinement await?
TEXT_KINGKW103_05382_SEQ_00:
Lydirceil is keen to proceed with the weapon enhancement endeavor.
※Changing classes or jobs will prevent progress during this quest.
TEXT_KINGKW103_05382_SEQ_01:
With Gerolt exuding aetheric energies, all that remains is to procure raw materials to begin the enhancement process. Thankfully, it appears the survey team have managed to extract a sizable quantity of waxing arcanite, which will be necessary to refine your phantom weapon. Given ongoing contractual obligations to the House of Splendors, however, you will need to purchase the requisite three chunks of ore from Ermina, their mercantile representative on the isle. Dodokkuli, meanwhile, waits patiently by the smithy, ready to receive the ore for preliminary processing.

※You may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.

※Chunks of waxing arcanite can be obtained from Ermina in the phantom village.
TEXT_KINGKW103_05382_SEQ_02: Having parted with a hefty stack of hard-earned tomestones, you hand over three chunks of waxing arcanite to Dodokkuli. Eager to behold Gerolt's newfound forging potential, he swiftly completes preparations before passing the reins to the aether-rich weaponsmith. Gerolt draws upon the wellspring of energy within him, successfully emulating the ancient art of aetheric infusion and thus completing this phase of the refinement process. You hold your enhanced phantom weapon aloft, ready to test its true potential on the battlefield.
TEXT_KINGDD101_05405_SEQ_00: The bright-eyed child is regaling her mother with a tale.
TEXT_KINGDD101_05405_SEQ_01: If the excitable youngling is to be believed, a Fuath is not only in the Crystarium but on its way to the Hortorium in search of an environment amenable to water spirits. The child's mother is highly skeptical, but knowing a Fuath's capacity for chaos as you do, you decide to err on the side of caution and investigate.
TEXT_KINGDD101_05405_SEQ_02: The Fuath muttering questionable ditties in the Hortorium is called Aenc Daen and has been employed by none other than Feo Ul to recruit a mortal from the Crystarium. According to your beautiful branch, vagrant sin eaters have been wandering Il Mheg recently, emerging from the ruins of an old church of the First Light. Wards have been mysteriously activated around the chapel in question, preventing fae folk from investigating further, so the task must fall to mortal hands. Your hands, in fact─so it is that you follow Aenc Daen back to Wolekdorf and the trouble brewing in the Kingdom of Rainbows.
TEXT_KINGDD101_05405_SEQ_03: Accurately guessing that you know little about the Church of the First Light, Aenc Daen tells you how the once great religion faded to obscurity after the advent of the Flood. Armed with this new knowledge, you set forth to the Church at Dammroen Field where, allegedly, some ne'er-do-wells are awaiting your arrival.
TEXT_KINGDD101_05405_SEQ_04: The pixie Ose Wyd warmly welcomes you on behalf of the delinquent group of fae, and you gaze upon the blinking portal from which sin eaters have been appearing. Before long, Titania arrives to deliver a gift and some esoteric words of advice: should you require their assistance within the church, you are to burn juniper incense. The viability and significance of such an action is yet a mystery to you, but the Fuath in your company seems impressed by its potential.
TEXT_KINGDD101_05405_SEQ_05: Aenc Daen's parting words are cryptic─due to the web of magicks connecting Norvrandt's chapels, your journey may take you much farther than you anticipate. With only one way to discover how far that is, you turn to Vanthau the amaro, who has offered to take you to the awakening portal.
TEXT_KINGDD101_05405_SEQ_06: Vanthau is clearly nervous that you may succumb to your mortality on his watch, but it is this selfsame mortality that will allow you inside the churches locked tight to fae folk. You prepare to take your first steps down the path to discovery, an unlikely pilgrim attempting a perilous traverse...
TEXT_KINGDD102_05406_SEQ_00: Aenc Daen is eyeing you critically.
TEXT_KINGDD102_05406_SEQ_01: The rhyming Fuath is keen to hear your progress within the churches of the First Light. Your description of the great sin eater in clerical robes prompts them to send for the king, and as the two of you await Titania, Aenc Daen explains why you are able to summon the Madbloom to your side by burning juniper incense. It seems the scheme hinges upon your beautiful branch's past life as a mortal─a life they willingly forfeited─and their status as one who might have once received First Light funeral rites. In any case, once Titania arrives to hear your report, they are less than surprised. According to their research, the church's last archbishop was allegedly slain by sin eaters, but Aenc Daen postulates that the cleric, in fact, turned. In a time rife with difficulty for the church, the truth was likely sealed away along with the transformed archbishop, who continued to wander the halls of chapels near and far, hoping against hope for oblivion.
TEXT_KINGDD102_05406_SEQ_02: You have laid to rest the menace causing trouble in Il Mheg, but Aenc Daen reports that the fae barriers are still in place around the church. What this portends is yet unclear, but journeying further down the pilgrim road may lead you to greater answers─and greater threats.
TEXT_KINGDD103_05407_SEQ_00: Aenc Daen's muddy eyes regard you suspiciously.
TEXT_KINGDD103_05407_SEQ_01: Having reached the end of the pilgrim road, you report the details of your final battle to Aenc Daen. The Fuath is appropriately awed by your achievements and eager to see what changes your epic battle might have wrought upon the church, and thus you head to Dammroen Field whilst they notify the king.
TEXT_KINGDD103_05407_SEQ_02: King Titania arrives with their entourage and confirms the disappearance of the fae barrier. To all appearances, the First Light's last solemn rites are over. Even as some mystery yet lingers around the final fiend you dispatched and the innermost chamber, the fae wards are reinstated by Titania's hand, and you are thanked profusely for a job well done in service to Il Mheg. No matter where your journey leads, be assured that your beautiful branch is guaranteed to follow.
TEXT_KINGDD103_05407_SEQ_03: It transpires that Aenc Daen has been tasked to aid in any future exploration of the churches, so you may rest easy knowing your frog-like friend will be around to provide wisdom, witticisms, and the more-than-occasional couplet whenever fancy suits. Mind your mortal soul, lest you lose it to the Kingdom of Rainbows and find yourself permanently away with the fae...
TEXT_KINGWK201_05409_SEQ_00: The time is come for the initiative's next great hop.
TEXT_KINGWK201_05409_SEQ_01: With the Moongate Hub expanded to its fullest, the Cosmic Exploration Initiative is prepared to broaden its horizons. According to Searchingway, the Galactic Way has not only passed its test flights, but successfully ferried a scouting party to its first destination: a star known as “UL 9-6.” When Namingway laments the sterility of such a designation, Searchingway proposes he concoct something more stirring by making the journey himself. But this invitation is by no means exclusive─the new base camp needs all the contributors it can attract, and you have once again been pawpicked as one of them.
TEXT_KINGWK201_05409_SEQ_02: Armed with your artisan's tools, and Namingway with his dictionaries, you arrive at the cosmoport, whereupon Captain Cruisingway guides you aboard her vessel. The engine roars to life, and the Galactic Way hops its way through the great expanse by way of stellar current. At journey's end, a lustrous star comes into view, inspiring Namingway to dub it “Phaenna.”
TEXT_KINGWK201_05409_SEQ_03: You and your fellow passengers land safely on the glossy surface of Phaenna. Before you race off to explore the heretofore untouched frontier, however, Searchingway must brief you on its many-faceted environs.
TEXT_KINGWK201_05409_SEQ_04: Searchingway explains that an abundance of silicon has made certain parts of Phaenna sharp to the touch─including, somehow, the weather. Nevertheless, the prospect of mineral resources and undiscovered plant life is too enticing to pass up, for by using Phaenna as a stepping stone, the initiative may take further leaps into the great unknown.
TEXT_KINGWK202_05410_SEQ_00: Searchingway wishes to laud you for your efforts on Phaenna.
TEXT_KINGWK202_05410_SEQ_01: While you and Searchingway are discussing Phaenna's treacherous terrain, Namingway returns from making his rounds, confident that he has now named the entirety of the star. As with Sinus Ardorum, he invites you to take a tour with him, and Searchingway happily sends you on your way.
TEXT_KINGWK202_05410_SEQ_02:
The grand tour of Phaenna will start at Glassblowers' Beacon. Together, you and Namingway seek out a good, clear view of the area.

※You must be accompanied by Namingway to complete this task. Speak with him again should you become separated.
TEXT_KINGWK202_05410_SEQ_03: Namingway expounds on how the sheltering properties of the Glassblown Grotto's dome gave rise to its name, emphasizing that it provides an ideal location for a base of operations. Fragile though the works of man and Loporrit may be, Glassblowers' Beacon has undoubtedly proven itself the atelier in which the initiative's future will be shaped, just as he anticipated.
TEXT_KINGWK202_05410_SEQ_04: Your next destination is the Soda-lime Float, which─contrary to what the name suggests─is most certainly not potable. Within this stream of liquid glass are equally deceptive “fish” formed of glass and condensed aether, but lacking the qualities typically associated with fauna. For now, “arcane entities” appears to be the closest classification of these piscine impostors.
TEXT_KINGWK202_05410_SEQ_05: To the southwest, it transpires that Fusingway Vent was named for yet another glassworking technique because, as with so much on Phaenna, the magma within contains nearly enough silicon to be considered molten glass. He further warns you not to dawdle in the vicinity of said magma, lest the vacillating temperatures take you by surprise and result in the melting of the soles of your shoes (or worse).
TEXT_KINGWK202_05410_SEQ_06: You follow Namingway to the top of the Iridized Rise which, as he tells it, was named for the rainbow colors of its many glossy stairs. After speaking much and more of Phaenna's almost-plants, he reflects on the many questions that the star raises in his mind─questions that he entrusts to future generations to answer.
TEXT_KINGWK202_05410_SEQ_07: Back at Glassblowers' Beacon at last, you are ushered to an unexpected final stop on your tour: the Phaenna Stellascope. This massive magnifying device has already enabled the Cosmic Exploration Initiative to detect stars beyond Phaenna, some of which Searchingway hopes may yet harbor intelligent life in spite of Meteion's dire proclamations. Thus does the initiative's attention turn to finding the ideal candidate for the Galactic Way's next voyage.
TEXT_KINGWZ201_05411_SEQ_00: Mumukko prefers it when idle hands don't pretend otherwise.
TEXT_KINGWZ201_05411_SEQ_01: Successfully availing herself of your free time, Mumukko expounds on the source of her current predicament─and your impending volunteer assignment. While collecting feedback for a postmortem review, she and her management partner, Phasingway, identified a source of potential trouble: project leader Commandingway and magitek specialist Justa. As Mumukko tells it, the two are meant to be upgrading and refining the initiative's machinery, but are strangely reticent to reveal the details of their work, possibly in fear of disciplinary action. For that reason, she and Phasingway request that you approach the pair as a peer and learn what precisely is in the works.
TEXT_KINGWZ201_05411_SEQ_02: As soon as you ingratiate yourself with the pair, it becomes apparent that Commandingway and Justa have abandoned their good sense somewhere out in the great expanse. You witness an impassioned discussion in which each proposes increasingly more fanciful mech upgrades utterly divorced from the needs of the initiative─until management seizes an opportune moment to interrupt. Once expectations for Justa have been firmly reset, they drag Commandingway off for what will presumably be an even stricter scolding.
TEXT_KINGWZ201_05411_SEQ_03: Fortunately, by demonstrating an understanding of where they went wrong and a deep respect for their leadership position, Commandingway manages to escape Mumukko and Phasingway mostly unscathed. Phasingway remarks that the incident is all too representative of the state of the initiative at present, and you are left with the impression that you ought to keep an eye out for others that may be struggling─as well as the mysterious “guest” that is soon to arrive.
TEXT_KINGWZ202_05412_SEQ_00: The Ishgardian glassworker needs to touch glass.
TEXT_KINGWZ203_05413_SEQ_00: The vacuum suit specialist seeks qualified candidates only.
TEXT_KINGWZ204_05414_SEQ_00: Mumukko wishes to reward your idle hands with a special introduction.
TEXT_KINGVA101_05441_SEQ_00: Shallow Moor has an odd job for an enterprising adventurer.
TEXT_KINGVA101_05441_SEQ_01: Shallow Moor relays an odd job request from someone who apparently knows you by name: one Y'nazqha, a gleaner and younger sister of none other than Y'shtola. She has enlisted your aid in a most unusual quest: to keep her safe while she explores the pages of a magical book left to her by her late father. The nature of the book demands it be kept under careful watch, so Y'nazqha instructs you to come to the gleaners' lodgings in Journey's End at your soonest convenience to learn more.
TEXT_KINGVA101_05441_SEQ_02: Y'nazqha informs you that the book in question is entitled The Merchant's Tale, a fable passed down in Corvos following the narrative of a young merchant's quest to find a great treasure. While the enchantment imbued within the manuscript makes reading the book almost certainly dangerous, the young gleaner is heartened by your company and appears ready to leap into a world of fiction at your signal.
TEXT_KINGVA101_05441_SEQ_03:
As the magicked tome is held up before the two of you, its cover begins to glow, and the world falls away in a haze of white light. Its radiance soon fades, and you find yourselves in a small but well-kept room. What's more, you are not alone. A young woman is addressing Y'nazqha, who is now dressed in the garb of the tale's merchant. A scene plays out before you, and as the dialogue comes to a close, you suspect the gleaner may know how to move the story forward.

※In the event that you leave the area, you may return by reading The Merchant's Tale in Journey's End.
TEXT_KINGVA101_05441_SEQ_04:
With no clear path pointing towards the next plot point, you and Y'nazqha inspect the room. While what you find provides only vague hints at what is to come, your companion appears eager to step further into the book.

※The Merchant's Tale can be accessed via the V&C Dungeon Finder.
※To open the V&C Dungeon Finder, interact with the passage to the next chapter or select the option located under Duty in the main menu.
TEXT_KINGVA101_05441_SEQ_05: After a journey full of fantastic locales and fierce battle, you and Y'nazqha witness the final scene of The Merchant's Tale─one of the final scenes, in any case. Free from the pages of the enchanted manuscript, Y'nazqha asks you to meet her at Journey's End to discuss what you experienced.
TEXT_KINGVA101_05441_SEQ_06: Y'nazqha thanks you for your courage and for helping her learn more about the keepsake left by her late father, and asks you to help her explore the book further when you have time. With your odd job complete, all that is left is to return to Shallow Moor for payment.
TEXT_KINGVA101_05441_SEQ_07: Shallow Moor congratulates you on a job well done, happy to have another satisfied customer. Yet The Merchant's Tale has secrets left to tell, and Y'nazqha is depending on your protection to help uncover all the wondrous passages that are yet unread.
TEXT_KINGVA110_05442_SEQ_00: Fyrgeim has a message to deliver to you.
TEXT_CHRHDB941_05446_SEQ_00: Hardiboiled casts a resolute shadow beneath the unrelenting glare of True Vue's neon illumination.
TEXT_CHRHDB941_05446_SEQ_01:
Inspector's Log:
The Case of the Fiendish Fugitives continues! Detective Hardiboiled's latest lead led us beyond the dome in pursuit of a vandal wolfman. It was there, in a charmingly rustic town beset by troubles, that an unfortunate misunderstanding saw my loyal assistant arrested on suspicion of explosive mayhem. Naturally, I would not rest until her good name was cleared! Working closely with the detective, we apprehended the true perpetrator and freed the deeply traumatized Nashu from her unjust confinement. 'Tis a pity, though, that not all ended happily ever after: Carnelian, a dastardly villain from Hardiboiled's past, eluded our grasp. His involvement in the greater scheme has been made abundantly apparent, and I, Hildibrand, agent of enquiry, will be ready the next time the Crime King rears his metamorphic head!
　　　　　　　　　　　　*　*　*
Having extracted additional information from the salvaged storage device, Hardiboiled briefs you on yet another monster-fied criminal. This particular ne'er-do-well now inhabits the body of a cactuar and has a well-documented record for operating air-wheelers with reckless abandon. According to Hildibrand, a speedy succulent matching the description was witnessed streaking southwards upon some flying contraption, and Hardiboiled concludes that catching said fugitive will be impossible on foot. It would seem a trip to the nearby custom air-wheeler shop is in order...
TEXT_CHRHDB941_05446_SEQ_02: Hardiboiled wishes to retrieve his personal air-wheeler from Monom's care, but the mechanic is doubtful the neglected vehicle will run without replacing a number of key parts. The detective puts you in charge of obtaining the superconductor coil, a task which should be made easier with the help of a handy gadget supplied by Monom. Once in the western district of the old Alexandria ruins, you are to set off the distress signal, and salvage the component from any defective sentries that respond.
TEXT_CHRHDB941_05446_SEQ_03: Moments after you trigger the signal, you are assaulted by a wheeler-mounted soldier. One short battle later and you have the part you need to deliver into Monom's waiting hands.
TEXT_CHRHDB941_05446_SEQ_04: The mechanic seems satisfied with the scavenged coil, but also perplexed by Hardiboiled's failure to return from what should have been a routine shopping trip. Certain that a simple battery is readily available, he sends you off to the Nexus Arcade to search for your tardy companions.
TEXT_CHRHDB941_05446_SEQ_05: An irritated Hardiboiled explains how Nashu and the inspector suddenly wandered off, leaving him alone with his purchased battery. You begin searching for them together, and find the impulsive pair enjoying an unexpected reunion with a member of the Gentle Dead Men. At Hildibrand's urging, the zombie proceeds to tell you of his efforts to recruit the Yuweyawata undead, and from this account you learn the name of the sole surviving researcher and mastermind behind the fiendish fugitives' escapades: Keshkayi. Hardiboiled heads back to Monom's shop, promising to soon return upon his newly repaired air-wheeler.
TEXT_CHRHDB941_05446_SEQ_06: It is not long before Hardiboiled comes racing back atop the custom-built “Night Stallion,” much to the amazed delight of your comrades. In response to a simple question from Nashu, the detective launches into an overly descriptive story of how he finally took down the Crime King, and subsequently lost his boiling need for speed. With Carnelian back on the streets, however, Hardiboiled is eager to ride again.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_00: Hildibrand is eager to take to the air.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_01: The irrepressible inspector is ready to take flight, with your eccentric group of investigators planning to rendezvous at the Cocktail dirigible landing. Or was it Yak's Tail?
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_02: Detective Hardiboiled greets you at the Yak T'el landing, having already grilled the locals for eyewitness accounts. The cactuar criminal was seen flying down to the lower forests, and he suggests continuing your investigation in the largest settlement in that region: Mamook.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_03: Although momentarily distracted by Mamook's distinctive architectural style, Hardiboiled quickly returns to the matter at hand. You are to spread out and gather what leads you can on the cactuar's current whereabouts.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_04: Your questioning of Mamook's residents has gleaned several potentially useful nuggets of information. The detective will want to hear your findings.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_05: The others nod along with your report, having heard much the same stories. Now that you have confirmed the presence of the cactuar and learned of its destructive deeds, you decide to stake out the meteorites found alongside the road leading out of town in hopes of catching your quarry in the act.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_06: You linger by the first meteorite on the road, but the wheeler-riding cactuar is nowhere to be seen. The detective urges you on towards another space rock, further west into the Ja Tiika Heartland...
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_07: There is no sign of the cactuar at the second meteorite either. You set your sights on the next pockmarked boulder off to the north.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_08: The delinquent cactuar at last makes an appearance, challenging you and your fellow “slowpokes” to catch him if you can. Hardiboiled sets off in pursuit and, with a little unasked-for assistance from Hildibrand, manages to overtake the succulent speedster. Humbled and in no mood for a fight, the cactuar spills his guts and reveals the location where he was to make a meteorite delivery to Keshkayi. The detective leaps at the chance to enact his vengeance on Carnelian, leaving you with no choice but to follow him southwest to the aforementioned cliffs.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_09: Hardiboiled gets the drop on Keshkayi and Carnelian, but Hildibrand's bumbling interference ensures that the detective's nemesis once more escapes the justice promised by a Molt Python Maximum. Already distressed by the loss of his beloved air-wheeler, a furious Hardiboiled makes it clear that he wants nothing more to do with the inspector. Hildibrand accepts this chastisement with good grace, urging you to stick with Hardiboiled for the duration of the case, even as he and Nashu continue with their own independent inquiries.
TEXT_CHRHDB942_05447_SEQ_10: As opposed to his feelings for the inspector, Hardiboiled assures you that he values your worldly expertise and proven mettle. He requests your continued assistance with the investigation, which is set to resume once he salvages more readable files from the damaged storage device...
TEXT_KINGWK301_05448_SEQ_00: Searchingway hopes you are ready to go boldly once more.
TEXT_KINGWK301_05448_SEQ_01: Searchingway's giddiness all but gives away his glad tidings: the initiative has settled on its next destination─currently known only as RG 4-6─which may have once been home to intelligent life. Tempted by the possibility of replacing the star's mundane moniker and putting words to an unknown civilization's remains besides, Namingway gladly agrees to make the journey to this new-to-you star. Likewise, you find the promise of adventure too persuasive to ignore, and require no further encouragement to join the two Loporrits on the voyage.
TEXT_KINGWK301_05448_SEQ_02: Always happy to be of service, the good captain Cruisingway stands ready to launch at a moment's notice. You need only say the word─and possibly brace for impact.
TEXT_KINGWK301_05448_SEQ_03: With Cruisingway at the helm, you arrive safely at RG 4-6, a star afflicted with gravitational aether currents that strip the very land from its surface. In honor of the suffering this nevertheless beautiful world has undergone, Namingway decides it shall henceforth be known as Oizys.
TEXT_KINGWK301_05448_SEQ_04: Once you are settled as firmly on the ground as one can be under such conditions, Searchingway introduces you to Dylise, a Sharlayan scholar working on the Bibliotheca Historica. Owing to her expertise in the comparative study of civilizations, Searchingway has tasked her with leading the research effort on Oizys, and she already has a theory: the structures here were built not by indigenous peoples, but visitors like yourselves. This, of course, raises more questions than it answers, but with time and teamwork, any number of truths may be brought to light.
TEXT_KINGWK302_05449_SEQ_00: Having come this far, Searchingway is confident that nothing can bring the initiative down.
TEXT_KINGWK302_05449_SEQ_01: As you and Searchingway are chatting about your experience on Oizys, Namingway returns, having concluded his newly expanded duties. He invites you to join him on another enlightening stroll to learn more of the nomenclature that he has chosen to bestow upon this gravity-torn star.
TEXT_KINGWK302_05449_SEQ_02:
As ever, your tour is to begin with the initiative's base of operations─in this case, Terra Firma. To that end, the two of you will require an unobstructed view of its imposing structure.

※You must be accompanied by Namingway to complete this task. Speak with him again should you become separated.
TEXT_KINGWK302_05449_SEQ_03: Accompanied by Namingway, you observe the greater Megalithopolis, cradled by towering stone. There, he shares his initial fear of being unable to create appellations of equal significance to those that would have once been used on the star─as well as his newfound philosophy that each name has its time and place, and one need not necessarily supplant or belie any others.
TEXT_KINGWK302_05449_SEQ_04: The second stop on Namingway's tour features a pair of impressive stone protrusions. To the west is the Shielding Wall, named for the way it is positioned directly between the Megalithopolis and nearby gravity sphere. To the east, however, is the Falsifying Wall, which shields nothing but empty wasteland despite its grandiose appearance. Your next destination is promised to be more captivating still...
TEXT_KINGWK302_05449_SEQ_05: The Unmoored Anchor, as Namingway explains it, was named for its metaphorical relationship to Shadefleet rather than any real physical resemblance, this connection created through the use of the newly constructed gravitational generators. Beyond it to the south stretches a striking view of the Magnetic Horizon, which flouts Oizys's anomalous gravity by sheer magnetic force.
TEXT_KINGWK302_05449_SEQ_06: Speaking of gravitational anomalies, stepping into Shadefleet grants you a frighteningly close look at the nearest specimen. Everything from the trees to the very earth has been warped by its influence, but there remain glimpses of a potentially promising future for Oizys. While Namingway cannot but dwell on the past once more, his regrets only become greater motivation to craft monikers with the utmost care.
TEXT_KINGWK302_05449_SEQ_07: Upon your return to the Megalithopolis, Searchingway excitedly informs you of the latest report: the Euhedron is set to be restored in short order. Eager to learn what answers it holds, the three of you hurry into Terra Firma, where you find Dylise wrestling with the terminal. When it finally activates, it displays a strange holographic projection that resembles a navigational chart. Skilled as they were at gravitational magicks, could it be that the Voyagers' repeated interstellar departures were the cause of Oizys's corruption? And if they did leave the star ere its destruction, where did they go?
TEXT_KINGWZ301_05450_SEQ_00: There shall be no rest for Mumukko's favorite pair of idle hands.
TEXT_KINGWZ301_05450_SEQ_01: Seeing as you have time on your hands, Mumukko would ask a favor. During her investigation, Councilor Y'adebh documented two women at risk of working themselves into an early grave: Dylise and Justa. Naturally, the Forum has ordered the initiative rectify the matter posthaste, and issued two vicarious vacationers to aid in the enforcement of healthy habits. Your role is to see them into their charges' hands, and ensure that sufficient rest is taken as seriously as exciting advances in interstellar travel.
TEXT_KINGWZ301_05450_SEQ_02: You find Dylise chatting with Commandingway as she awaits word from the Phaenna observation team. She insists that the Euhedron data analysis must necessarily take precedence above all─until a bout of dizziness causes her to lose her balance. When the mammet identifies heart palpitations and elevated blood pressure among her symptoms, Commandingway realizes that she has not adjourned to bed in several days. For her part, Dylise is quick to grasp how morale would suffer were she to collapse from exhaustion, and so she submits to the vacationer's instruction.
TEXT_KINGWZ301_05450_SEQ_03: When you approach Justa, her new mammet minder promptly observes aloud that she has been working for six bells uninterrupted. As Garlean soldiers were typically barred from rest until they fulfilled their duty, Justa seems surprised that Mumukko would take such pains to look out for her health, and admits that to do so will take more discipline than she is used to exercising. However, understanding that the betterment of her work style is key to her ability to transform technology into a boon to mankind, she vows to embrace the occasional break.
TEXT_KINGWZ301_05450_SEQ_04: Mere moments after you report your success to Mumukko, Commandingway arrives to confirm that Dylise has indeed taken a proper meal break. Alas, this does not blunt Mumukko's wrath for the poor Loporrit, who is admittedly partially responsible for allowing so dire a situation to develop in the first place. To her mind, it is a manager's sacred duty to balance passionate progress with sustainable working conditions─for which purpose she intends to continue to deploy vicarious vacationers. Though it is difficult not to fear for those who might flaut her new zero-tolerance policy for excess work, either intentionally or through simple lack of attention to the clock, it should at least result in fewer mech-related accidents.
TEXT_KINGWZ302_05451_SEQ_00: The Cosmoliner engineer would rather do anything but his job.
TEXT_KINGWZ303_05452_SEQ_00: As ever, Mumukko seeks a pair of idle hands to carry out her bidding.
TEXT_KINGWZ304_05453_SEQ_00: Theorizingway awaits the arrival of erudite guests.
TEXT_KINGKW201_05454_SEQ_01:
Lydirceil wishes to see your phantom weapon further enhanced, and assures you that Gerolt is equally keen, if not quite ready, to proceed. In fact, the temperamental weaponsmith is diligently pondering the next step of the endeavor─or so Lydirceil claims. He encourages you to speak with Gerolt directly to learn what it is the blacksmith is planning.
※Please note this quest cannot be abandoned via the journal. If you wish to abandon the quest, you may do so at any time by speaking with Lydirceil.
TEXT_KINGKW201_05454_SEQ_02: Gerolt has indeed been deep in thought, eager to expand his repertoire and elevate your weapon to new heights of power. To this end, he has tasked the expedition's resident archaeologist to search the records for suitable techniques. His mind fogged by a few too many cups of rum, the weaponsmith bids you visit the archaeologist to glean her findings while he sobers up.
TEXT_KINGKW201_05454_SEQ_03: Upon your arrival, the expedition archaeologist provides a thorough explanation of the three ancient methods she has deemed worthy of further inquiry: “hexcarving,” “Karnak forgecraft,” and “aetheric conversion.” Armed with new knowledge and a sheaf of detailed notes, you make for the smithy to consult with Gerolt.
TEXT_KINGKW201_05454_SEQ_04:
After discussing the matter with Gerolt, the weaponsmith resolves to replicate the technique of aetheric conversion. To begin the process, a selection of ingredients is required, and as the only one free to leave the Occult Crescent, their procurement inevitably falls to you. Gerolt will be waiting by the smithy for your return.

Umbral clay: seek a trader in the markets of Tuliyollal.
Aspected aether agglomerate, aspected aetheroconductor, aspected aetherocatalyst: craft using the relevant recipe or purchase from the market board.

※Should you choose to craft the aspected materials, you will need to have obtained the Master Recipe XII tomes of the Disciples of the Hand.
TEXT_KINGKW201_05454_SEQ_05: You deliver the ingredients to Gerolt, who is ready and eager to proceed─after a swift libation. No doubt the freshly rum-fortified weaponsmith will begin his task once you speak with him again.
TEXT_KINGKW201_05454_SEQ_06: Having briefly relocated to one of the structures in the phantom village, Gerolt returns from his endeavors accompanied by a singular voidsent. Hearing the weaponsmith recount the aetheric conversion procedure, it becomes apparent that the creature was inadvertently summoned by his hand. The voidsent itself seems confused, and insists its original form was more powerful, leading Dodokkuli to surmise the vessel Gerolt crafted is somehow unsuitable. To encourage the beleaguered creature to stay─and secure its eventual cooperation in the weapon enhancement process─you form a pact, promising aether in exchange. The next step will be to aid it in unleashing its full potential─though by what means, and to what end, remains unclear...
TEXT_KINGKW202_05455_SEQ_00: Lydirceil is pondering the next step forward.
TEXT_KINGKW202_05455_SEQ_01:
Lydirceil believes the voidsent's vessel will need to be crafted anew if it is to leverage its power. The group manages to glean that unlike its current guise, the creature's true form has limbs, and thus a plan emerges. Gerolt, for his part, sees an opportunity to further strengthen the bond between voidsent and vessel through the addition of a material known as “crystal paste” to the mixture used to fashion its body. And thus you find yourself tasked with retrieving one hundred portions of the substance for the weaponsmith.

Crystal paste can be obtained by completing duties.

On the Occult Crescent's South Horn, crystal paste can only be obtained from critical encounters, excluding the Forked Tower: Blood.

You may use the phantom glass to gauge your progress.

※Speak to Lydirceil if you wish to abandon this quest.
TEXT_KINGKW202_05455_SEQ_02: Upon receiving the crystal paste, Gerolt soon fashions a new vessel replete with the requisite appendages. Although the voidsent reports a renewed sense of strength, they complain that their mental faculties are still diminished. Hearing this, the weaponsmith resolves to craft yet another vessel, one that inevitably requires more resources.
TEXT_KINGKW202_05455_SEQ_03: You deliver a fresh batch of crystal paste to Gerolt, who sets about crafting another vessel. The summoned voidsent seems pleased with the latest iteration, although there remains room for improvement. The creature insists its true form was beautiful─and thus the effort to restore this missing element to the vessel begins. According to Gerolt, an even greater quantity of crystal paste will be required.
TEXT_KINGKW202_05455_SEQ_04: Yet another delivery made, yet another vessel crafted. Alas, though vastly improved, it seems Gerolt's latest rendition is not quite perfect. To well and truly forge a bond between the voidsent and its vessel, additional crystal paste is called for...
TEXT_KINGKW202_05455_SEQ_05: After much trial and error, not to mention your peerless paste procurement, the vessel is finally complete. Overjoyed at having attained their true form, the grateful voidsent introduces herself as Brigid. She then channels her aether into Gerolt's hammer─as per your pact. Having successfully borrowed the power of the void itself, it will not be long before your phantom weapon is rightfully enhanced.
TEXT_KINGKW203_05456_SEQ_00:
Lydirceil would see your phantom weapon further enhanced.
※Changing classes or jobs will prevent progress during this quest.
TEXT_KINGKW203_05456_SEQ_01:
With Gerolt's hammer reborn, the time has come to utilize its void-given properties. Lydirceil informs you that waning arcanite will be necessary to facilitate the enhancement, and directs you to Ermina, the House of Splendors representative, who can provide the requisite ore for the right price. The ever-diligent Dodokkuli waits by the smithy, ready to undertake the preliminary processing once the arcanite has been procured.

※You may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.

※Chunks of waning arcanite can be obtained from Ermina in the phantom village.
TEXT_KINGKW203_05456_SEQ_02: Having delivered three chunks of waning arcanite to Dodokkuli, the metallurgist handily prepares the ore before entrusting the remaining work to Gerolt. Hammer in hand, the wayward weaponsmith channels its otherworldly energies into your phantom weapon, elevating it to formerly unimaginable heights of power.
TEXT_KINGSF201_05460_SEQ_00: Hhuki is studying you with a keen eye.
TEXT_SUBCTS830_05469_SEQ_00: The Tonawawtan boy's eyes light up at the sight of you.
TEXT_SUBCTS830_05469_SEQ_01: As you are making your way through Tuliyollal, you have a chance encounter with the wandering minstrel. The man presents you with what he claims is a relic of the legendary wing spirit─an enchanted flute that bestows wings divine upon the true hero who plays it. Believing you worthy of this honor, the minstrel bids you put the instrument to the proof, and thus do you set forth for Miyakabek'zoma in Kozama'uka, there to find a suitable vantage point.
TEXT_SUBCTS830_05469_SEQ_02: At the heights of Kozama'uka, you blow upon the flute, and watch in marvel as dazzling wings of white and gold manifest upon your shoulders. The spirit, it would seem, has seen fit to place itself at your disposal. Borne by these wings divine, you look forward to taking to the boundless skies on the adventures ahead.
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_00: Hardiboiled's pensive expression cuts a stark contrast to the frenetic buzz of True Vue's neon-lit streets.
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_01:
Inspector's Log:
We departed for the densely wooded environs of Yak's Tail in pursuit of a swift-moving succulent─another of Hardiboiled's fiendish fugitives. Purported to be an air-wheeler aficionado of unsavory repute, we learned that this spike-covered delinquent was racing around the forest in search of meteorites to smash and subsequently grab. When confronted, however, our quarry chose to flee, confident that his vaunted velocity would secure his escape. We gave chase upon the detective's trusty Night Stallion, ultimately outpacing the speedy cactuar and convincing him to surrender his superior's whereabouts. Alas, a miscalculation on my part resulted in our failure to apprehend Carnelian. As the furious detective has declined any further gentlemanly assistance, Nashu and I shall henceforth pursue independent inquiries into the masked mastermind...the man we now know as “Keshkayi”!
　　　　　　　　　　　　*　*　*
The salvaged data contains no further mention of monster-fied criminals, but what Hardiboiled has discovered is plans for repairing a “duplication device.” Said gadget was reportedly found aboard a flying vessel you immediately recognize as PuPu's flying vessel, and your description of its capabilities leaves the detective aghast. By your estimation, Keshkayi has already acquired all the materials required to effect repairs, and Hardiboiled is fresh out of leads. He heads off to visit Mymond and tap into the city's rumor mill, but your own departure is delayed by a disguised Hildibrand and Nashu. The intrepid pair intends to keep a watchful eye on the oglop following Hardiboiled, convinced it may prove crucial to cracking the case...
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_02: Mymond, the master of everyone else's business, has no direct information regarding the duplication device or calamities arising from its abuse, but he does have another interesting tidbit to share. It seems a hunter by the name of Circine came upon a badly wounded researcher out in Heritage Found and carried the man back to his house in the outskirts. Wondering if the wounded individual could be Keshkayi himself, you make for the hunter's abode to confirm if your suspicions are true.
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_03: Circine tells you of how he witnessed an air-wheeler crash to the ground, and his rescue of the man who crawled from the wreckage. The convalescing researcher is in no state to talk, but the hunter is nevertheless able to provide you with a name based on the identification card found on his person: Keshkayi. Hardiboiled attributes the villain's terrible burns to Carnelian, and with little else to do until Keshkayi awakens, you head outside to ponder what led to this fiery betrayal.
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_04: Hardiboiled reasons that Carnelian only played the lackey long enough to get his hands on the duplication device. As for what the Crime King would want to duplicate, the detective muses that an old accomplice of Carnelian's might have insights to share. She now works as a fortune-teller out of a shop in Solution Nine, which means your first step is dealing with her receptionist, Saralla.
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_05: Kacia is rather bemused by Hardiboiled's question regarding the duplication device and why her former associate would want it. She can only attest to Carnelian's insatiable desire to augment his arcane strength. As things stand, he lacks the power to cast the ultimate spell devised by his ancestor─an infamous archmage known as “the Lich.” Kacia suggests researching this sinister forefather using the public database, which Hardiboiled intends to access via the terminals in the commerce sector.
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_06: While the detective digs into the Lich's history, he asks that you read up on the clot─the species of monster which Carnelian specifically requested as the vessel for his soul. With the chat mode in Say, enter the search term “Clots” at the commerce sector data terminal.
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_07: You educate yourself on the peculiarities of clots, learning that these amorphous creatures can merge both their physical bodies and magical potential with others of their kind to form a single powerful entity. This is exactly the sort of information Hardiboiled will wish to know...
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_08: Hardiboiled's own research has uncovered several disturbing facts about the Lich, including the mage's propensity for raising the dead and his invention of an unstoppable spell capable of instantly killing any living creature. After listening to your report on clot characteristics, the detective deduces Carnelian's grand scheme: to make multiple copies of himself and fuse with them into one massive, murderous Crime King capable of casting the ultimate spell of slaying. Even as Hardiboiled makes plans to foil this ambition and claim vengeance for Noirshu, he receives a call from Circine informing you that Keshkayi has regained consciousness. Once again, the detective's departure heralds the arrival of Hildibrand and his assistant. Lack of evidence notwithstanding, Nashu, it seems, is all but convinced that Noirshu was not actually killed, but rather transferred into the body of the oglop. They promise to keep you apprised of their ongoing investigation, even as you look to rejoin Hardiboiled at Circine's house in the outskirts.
TEXT_CHRHDB951_05481_SEQ_09: Hardiboiled remarks on your tardiness, but nevertheless appears glad of your presence. The case is building towards an explosive end, and he would hate for you to miss it...
TEXT_CHRHDB952_05482_SEQ_00: Hardiboiled's eyes are alight with anticipation, nose full of the scent of his quarry.
TEXT_CHRHDB952_05482_SEQ_01: Awake and seething with fury, Keshkayi shares the tale of his failed scheme and Carnelian's betrayal. He freely reveals the location of the duplication device─a hidden lab in the bowels of the Kanilokka Corpus─demanding that you make the Crime King pay for ruining his plans. Although certainly eager to charge in, guns blazing, the detective first wishes to pay his respects at Noirshu's grave in the nameslates. He bids you wait for him there while he picks up his air-wheeler from the repair shop.
TEXT_CHRHDB952_05482_SEQ_02:
Your wait at the nameslates ends with the arrival of Mymond, who bears a letter from an apologetic detective. Hardiboiled writes that he has gone to confront Carnelian alone, not wanting to risk any more lives for his vendetta. No sooner do you finish reading when Hildibrand and the others arrive, having interrogated Keshkayi and confirmed that Noirshu's soul was indeed transferred into an oglop. You inform them of Hardiboiled's reckless solo endeavor, and the inspector immediately dashes off at a ludicrous pace.

Meanwhile, in the Kanilokka Corpus lab, Carnelian has succeeded in creating multiple replicas of himself. He merges his clot copies into the towering form of the Lich, and proceeds to treat Hardiboiled to a hostile demonstration of his ancestor's necromantic magicks...

※In the event that you leave the area, you may return by speaking with the accommodating reforger at the driftdowns.
TEXT_CHRHDB952_05482_SEQ_03:
As the undying zombies rise again and again, Hardiboiled's cool demeanor begins to crack, but Hildibrand's persuasive dance moves provide a timely rescue. Now able to combine the detective's firepower with the inspector's gentlemanly flair, they manage to overwhelm the incredulous Lich. You arrive with the others just as Hardiboiled aims for the kill, but the revelation of Noirshu's survival proves a fatal distraction. Carnelian unleashes a spell of certain death at the detective, yet it is Hildibrand's soul that is torn free when he intercepts the unholy blast. This seeming tragedy allows the fate-linked pair to fuse the spiritual and corporeal into a new form of their own─Hildiboiled! The golden giant shrugs off the Lich's deadly incantations before slamming him into submission with unprecedented Mandervillian might.

The impact severs their union, and Hildibrand's soul is soon caught up by the afterlife's inexorable current. Yet a sliver of life remains in the inspector's breast, and you draw his soul back into his body with your own irresistible performance. With Hildibrand none the worse for wear, you leave the lab behind to accompany Hardiboiled as he awaits Noirshu's long-overdue restoration.
TEXT_CHRHDB952_05482_SEQ_04: You head outside to escape the oppressive air of the facility, and it is not long until Hildibrand and the others emerge with the restored Noirshu. Overwhelmed with emotion at the return of his assistant, Hardiboiled is ready to call it a day...only to find Hildibrand sat astride his beloved Night Stallion. The inspector's attempt to operate the air-wheeler sends it shooting up into the air, where he and the vehicle are promptly struck by lightning and spun off into the distance. Nashu chases after her ever-dwindling mentor, leaving you to accept Hardiboiled's invitation to meet him back at his house in Solution Nine.
TEXT_CHRHDB952_05482_SEQ_05: The case now closed thanks to your stalwart assistance, the detective shows his appreciation by presenting you with a Night Stallion replica (sans customization). From Noirshu you receive a delightful new oglop companion─one of the many friends she made during her insectoid days. Having said their farewells, Hardiboiled and his oddly familiar assistant return to running their detective agency. You wonder if your paths will ever cross again, even as their distinctive silhouettes are swallowed by the neon jungle of Solution Nine...
TEXT_KINGWK401_05483_SEQ_00: Though subtlety has never been Searchingway's strong suit,  he is vibrating at a frequency that suggests he's fit to bursting with news.
TEXT_KINGWK401_05483_SEQ_01: Unable to conceal the good news any longer, Searchingway reveals that analysis of the Voyagers' navigational chart has pinpointed your next destination. Though the provisional designation “EG 1-9” inspires naught in Namingway but the determination to replace it outright, you find yourself sufficiently enticed by the potential of yet-unseen relics to meet your traveling companions at the Galactic Way.
TEXT_KINGWK401_05483_SEQ_02: At the cosmoport, Cruisingway is poised to sweep you off your feet once more. Naturally, Searchingway and Namingway will be joining you.
TEXT_KINGWK401_05483_SEQ_03: A comparatively uneventful flight sees the Galactic Way to EG 1-9, a star brimming with aether, lush with dense forests, and bearing the unmistakable mark of civilization. Beautiful as it is, Namingway cannot help but wonder how the Voyagers spent their days upon this prosperous star─which he chooses to name “Auxesia.”
TEXT_KINGWK401_05483_SEQ_04: Upon landing, Searchingway introduces your new base of operations, situated at the center of the city ruins. There, you are soon joined by Dylise, who has once again taken charge of survey efforts. She explains that the architecture on this star, while still arcane in nature, is rather more sophisticated than that which was found on Oizys─supporting the hypothesis that Auxesia could be the Voyagers' point of origin. But this theory raises questions regarding the conspicuous absence of intelligent life at present...the answers to which you can only hope lie concealed amidst the overgrown foliage.
TEXT_KINGWK402_05484_SEQ_00: Searchingway could not be prouder of the initiative's blossoming efforts.
TEXT_KINGWK402_05484_SEQ_01: While you and Searchingway are discussing the uniform greenery, Namingway returns, having assigned appellations to nearly all of Auxesia. In turn, Searchingway reports that the research team is almost finished restoring Grandma Laurel's core functionality. He proposes that the three of you check in with Dylise to see what she may have uncovered.
TEXT_KINGWK402_05484_SEQ_02: You arrive at Grandma Laurel just as Dylise and her team were on the point of supplying it the aether needed to function. When she does, a voice reverberates in your head─and, unusually, everyone else's─and a plantlike entity is projected above. Speaking on behalf of the Nagylvi, the native civilization previously referred to as the Voyagers, this knowledge construct demands to know who dares disturb their slumber, and to what end. When Searchingway explains that the initiative's only intent is to learn of Auxesia, the Nagylvi offer a small terminal bud to accompany you and Namingway on what promises to be your most educational tour yet.
TEXT_KINGWK402_05484_SEQ_03:
As always, Namingway is eager to begin his grand tour. This time, however, you have the good fortune to be guided by a native with encyclopedic knowledge of all things Auxesia.

※You must be accompanied by Namingway and the Nagylvi bud to complete this task. Speak with either of them again should you become separated.
TEXT_KINGWK402_05484_SEQ_04: Your first destination is the Core Shroud, or as a native would call it, Laynysel T-ay: central administration. According to your guide, the Nagylvi were born of plants and gained sentience through the star's ambient aether. Upon hearing how they came to sculpt the city from trees, Namingway decides to show them the Cosmic Exploration Initiative's own base of operations.
TEXT_KINGWK402_05484_SEQ_05: In the Timberlodge, the Nagylvi bud recounts the exact process they once used to travel to other stars. You discover that, by alternating between two different relay points, they minimized the strain of the gravitational magicks employed, unwittingly sparing Auxesia the fate that ultimately befell Oizys. As the mood takes a dour turn, Namingway suggests you all visit Pileus Pergola for a much-needed change of pace.
TEXT_KINGWK402_05484_SEQ_06: Just as Namingway suspects, Pileus Pergola was once important to the Nagylvi─specifically, as a sunbathing area known as Tolygya Xifya. However, that was before the societal decline brought about by the total depletion of Oizys jasper. In awe of the Nagylvi's resilience, Namingway invites you to Full Bloom Gardens situated on the city's edge.
TEXT_KINGWK402_05484_SEQ_07: The visit to Full Bloom Gardens reveals even more intriguing details about Auxesia and the lives the Nagylvi once led.
